title: Robust Decoupled Input Filtering for Internal Model Principle-Based Output Regulation of Polynomial Exogenous Signals
abstract: Internal model principle-based controllers regulate polynomial references and disturbances exactly, but only asymptotically, and their transient input can peak and oscillate, increasingly so as the degree of the exogenous signals grows. A filter placed in series with the plant smooths the command but alters the closed-loop spectrum and can destroy stability. We propose an architecture that keeps the filter outside the loop the regulator stabilizes: the internal model is driven by the error of an ideal, unfiltered copy of the plant, the physical plant receives the filtered command, and an auxiliary plant copy absorbs the mismatch between the two inputs. If the filter satisfies blocking conditions at the origin, any gains that stabilize the unfiltered loop can be combined with any such filter without losing regulation of the true error. Under additive plant uncertainty, we derive a small-gain condition that guarantees robust stability and regulation. On a scalar plant, the proposed controller produces a smoother input and a larger input-delay margin than the unfiltered one, and it maintains regulation under a large loss of actuator effectiveness. On a three-mass chain, its tolerance to unmodeled actuator dynamics and delay stays essentially constant as the regulator is made more aggressive.

title: Real positive definite counterexamples to a monotonicity conjecture for the $q$-permanent
abstract: The $q$-permanent $P_q$ of an $n\times n$ matrix weights the term of each permutation $σ$ by $q^{\inv(σ)}$, where $\inv(σ)$ is the number of inversions of $σ$. It interpolates between the determinant ($q=-1$) and the permanent ($q=1$). Extending a conjecture of Bapat on $[-1,1]$, it was conjectured in 2010 that the $q$-permanent of every non-diagonal real symmetric positive definite matrix is strictly increasing on an interval $(\varepsilon,+\infty)$ with $\varepsilon<-1$. In this note, we disprove this conjecture. An explicit real symmetric positive definite integer matrix of order five, whose $q$-permanent has only nine nonzero terms, satisfies $P_{14}(A)>P_{15}(A)$. A sparse family shows that for every real $r>1$ some real symmetric positive definite matrix has a $q$-permanent with negative derivative at $q=r$. The counterexamples can be chosen to be correlation matrices without zero entries or, separately, to have integer entries. We also show that the smallest order of a counterexample is four, and that matrices supported on three coordinates separated by identity blocks fail much closer to $q=1$: in order five already near $q=1.7$, and in order $O(1/(r-1))$ at any prescribed $q=r>1$.

title: Steady-state of Lévy process with general resetting: unreflected and reflected cases
abstract: We study (unreflected and reflected) Lévy processes that are modified at independent Poisson review epochs by a random state-dependent reset map. The first model is unreflected: between resettings the level evolves as a Lévy process, and at a resetting epoch the new level is $F$ of the level seen just before the resetting. The second model is the reflected Lévy process at $0$, but with reset maps chosen from a wider transform-solvable class. In this work, we give contraction-type ergodicity criteria for the existence of the steady-state. We identify this steady-state of the system as the solution of certain stochastic fixed-point equation. This allows to find the Laplace-transform, moments recursions, and regularly-varying-tail formulae. For non-reflected case, the examples include affine deterministic resets $F(x)=cx+b$, random-coefficient resets $F(x)=Cx+b$ with two-point $C$ for the finite-activity Lévy process, spectrally positive Lévy flight, reflected Brownian process. For the reflected cased we analyse affine resetting mechanism $F(x)=cx$, the alternating resetting $F(x)=(B-x)^+$, and uniform proportional resetting $F(x)=Cx$ with $C$ having uniform distribution.

title: Twisted algebras of invariant formal power series over monoids
abstract: We develop a general monoid-theoretic framework to construct and study graded and color Hopf algebras of formal power series of bounded degree invariant under group actions. Rather than working with external alphabets of commuting, noncommuting, or anti-commuting variables, we start from an abstract monoid $M$ equipped with a $2$-cocycle twisting $τ:M\times M\to \mathbb{K}$, which is allowed to vanish, a bigrading over a commutative monoid $\mathcal{G}\times\mathbb{N}$ endowed with a bicharacter $φ$, and a group $G$ acting on $M$ via a bigraded action $ρ$ that is quasi-multiplicative with respect to $τ$, coupled with a $1$-cocycle weight function $ω:G\times M\to\mathbb{K}^\times$. By formulating local finiteness, gradings, quasi-multiplicativity, and ideals relative to the non-vanishing of $τ$, we prove that the invariant space $\mathbb{K}\langle\kern-0.2em\langle M\rangle\kern-0.2em\rangle^G$ forms a well-defined bigraded subalgebra of bounded-degree formal power series with a canonical monomial basis indexed by $ω$-admissible orbits. Furthermore, we establish four functorial constructions: embeddings into larger invariant algebras via restricted actions, color tensor product decompositions for direct products and diagonal actions, connected color Hopf algebra structures induced by internal monoid duplication, and quotient color Hopf algebras governed by invariant-retraction pairs with an explicit description of their kernel bi-ideals. As applications, we uniformly recover and extend the classical and twisted Hopf algebras of symmetric and quasisymmetric functions in commuting and noncommuting variables, MacMahon symmetric functions, the full square of symmetric and quasisymmetric Hopf algebras in superspace, symmetric and quasisymmetric functions in partially commutative variables, and signed-symmetric functions associated with the hyperoctahedral group.

title: $\mathbb Z$ is Diophantine over $\mathbb Q$ with 28 unknowns
abstract: Recently, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. Motivated by this work, G. Conant et al. showed that $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$, i.e., there is an integer-coefficient polynomial $F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ such that for any $x\in\mathbb Q$ we have $$ x\in\mathbb Z\quad\iff \exists\,y_1,\ldots,y_{n}\in\mathbb Q\ [F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{n})=0].$$ They constructed such a polynomial $F$ with deg $F=4$ and $n=393$. In this paper, we prove the existence of such a polynomial $F$ with $n=28$.

title: Universal Invariants for $\gcd(n^k-1,n!-1)>1$
abstract: For integers $k\geq2$ and $λ_1,λ_2\in\{-1,+1\}$, let $S_k^{λ_1,λ_2}:=\{n\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\{0,1\}:\gcd(n^k+λ_1,n!+λ_2)>1\}$. This family arose from a MathOverflow problem concerning the existence of integers $n$ satisfying $\gcd(n^2+1,n!+1)>1$ and from the subsequent question of whether arbitrarily many, but finitely many, solutions can be obtained by varying the exponent and the signs. We concentrate on the case $λ_1=λ_2=-1$ and introduce the notion of a universal invariant for an odd prime $p$, namely an integer $n\geq2$ such that $\gcd(n^{p\cdot m}-1,n!-1)>1$ for every integer $m\geq1$. We prove that this condition is equivalent to $\gcd(n^p-1,n!-1)>1$, characterize the possible prime divisors in terms of roots of unity over finite fields, and recall an explicit construction due to Jonathan Love that yields a universal invariant for every odd prime $p\geq5$, with the cubic case treated separately. As an application, we prove that $|S_k^{-1,-1}|\geqω_{\mathrm{odd}}(k)$ for every integer $k\geq2$, where $ω_{\mathrm{odd}}(k)$ denotes the number of distinct odd prime divisors of $k$. Hence, the cardinalities of these sets are unbounded as $k$ varies. This lower bound is deliberately coarse and constructive, as it is obtained by considering only universal invariants; stronger general lower bounds are obtained by different constructions. We also discuss minimal universal invariants, their persistent common divisors, the special structure of the cubic case, and a heuristic due to Will Sawin suggesting that there may be infinitely many cubic universal invariants, although the known examples are exceptionally sparse. Whether $S_k^{-1,-1}$ is finite or infinite for any fixed exponent $k\geq3$ remains an open problem.

title: Incidence Geometry of Local Maxima: Howe Duality and Branching
abstract: For a finite-dimensional unitary representation of a finite or compact group, consider the mean squared matrix coefficient on the unit sphere. Its local maxima are the vectors generating irreducible cyclic subrepresentations. We show that for compatible group actions this variational picture retains the incidence structure of representation theory. For two commuting actions, intersections of projectivized local-maximal components recover the weighted support graph of the product representation, including its multiplicity spaces; Howe duality is the multiplicity-one matching case. More generally, for pairwise commuting actions, and for subgroup chains, every positive linear combination of the corresponding functionals has exactly their common local maxima, while every other critical point has a positive Hessian direction. On a fixed irreducible module at the top of a subgroup chain, the simultaneous projective local-maximal components are indexed by vertex paths in the weighted Bratteli diagram. Each component is the product of the projective space of the bottom representation and the projectivized branching multiplicity spaces. In the multiplicity-free case with one-dimensional bottom type, these reduce to the Gelfand-Tsetlin lines. Peter-Weyl, Frobenius reciprocity, Young branching and Schur-Weyl duality provide concrete instances of the general picture.

title: Hotelling's $T^2$ and the generalized domain of attraction of the normal law
abstract: Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be independent copies of a full random vector in $\mathbb R^p$, where $p$ is fixed. We prove that Hotelling's $T^2$-statistic at a prescribed location converges to $χ_p^2$ if and only if the underlying distribution belongs to the generalized domain of attraction of the normal law and has that location as its mean. Our proof of necessity combines moment bounds with matrix comparisons for self-normalized sums. It yields a sharp moment inequality for the squared norm of the uncentered self-normalized sum. Convergence of the first two moments of this squared norm to the chi-square values implies generalized normal attraction and identifies the mean. The necessity part of the multivariate Student normal-limit theorem follows as a corollary. Its sufficiency is the established result of Sepanski and of Vu, Maller and Klass.

title: Strongly quasidiagonal C*-algebras with nuclear dimension one and infinite decomposition rank
abstract: We construct the first, to our knowledge, examples of strongly quasidiagonal C*-algebras with finite nuclear dimension and infinite decomposition rank. The examples are extensions of the form $0\to I \to E\to C(\mathbb{T})\to 0$ where $I$ is a simple AF-algebra. These examples are in some sense the easiest `natural' choices in light of Spielberg's work on AF-embedding extensions and the behavior of each dimension theory with respect to extensions. The standard extension bound provides $\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}} E \leq 2$ which is improved to 1 by recent work of Evington, Faurot and Schafhauser. Nuclear dimension 1 is the lowest possible for such an example because decomposition rank and nuclear dimension agree at 0. Finally, failure of the comparison property used to show infinite decomposition rank was inspired by local operator space techniques of Junge, Ozawa and Ruan.

title: Random feature policy iteration for inverse mean field games with complex geometry and high dimensions
abstract: We propose a random feature policy iteration method for reconstructing the obstacle function in a mean-field game (MFG) from observations of its value function, leveraging the method's mesh-free nature and flexibility to handle complex geometries and high-dimensional problems. The method builds on a policy iteration framework for inverse MFGs, which decouples the coupled nonlinear forward-backward PDE system into a sequence of linear PDE and inverse problem solves. The fixed random feature representations preserve this linear structure, allowing the resulting subproblems to be solved by minimizing residuals at sampled collocation points through linear least-squares problems. The mesh-free nature of the method further extends the applicability of the policy iteration framework to inverse MFGs with complex geometry and in high dimensions. Another key advantage is its flexibility in using different spatial approximations for different variables: the obstacle function, value function, and population density can be represented in separate feature spaces, accommodating obstacles that are substantially less regular than the corresponding PDE solutions. Moreover, boundary conditions can be enforced through collocation on irregular domains without constructing boundary-fitted meshes. Numerical experiments involving smooth and discontinuous obstacles, a domain with holes, and higher-dimensional problems demonstrate the accuracy and flexibility of the proposed method.

title: Talagrand's Convolution Bound for Tensor Powers of Finite-State Markov Semigroups
abstract:
Talagrand's convolution conjecture, recently proven by J. Lu, S. Guo, and E. Fang, concerns the smoothing properties of the heat semigroup on $\{-1,1\}^N$. We follow their perturbed coupled reverse-heat approach to generalize the theorem to tensor powers of irreducible continuous-time Markov semigroups on finite state spaces. Specifically, let $(S_t)_{t\geq0}$ be the semigroup of an irreducible continuous-time Markov chain on a finite state space $G_0$ with stationary distribution $π$. Then, for every $τ>0$, there exists a finite constant $C_{τ,S,π}<\infty$ such that, for every $N\geq1$, every nonnegative function $f:G_0^N\to[0,\infty)$, and every $η>1$, \begin{align*}
  π^{\otimes N}\left(S_τ^{\otimes N}f>η\int_{G_0^N}f\,dπ^{\otimes N}\right)\leq\frac{C_{τ,S,π}}{η\sqrt{\logη}}, \end{align*} where the constant is independent of $N$, $f$, and $η$. Most of the machinery developed by Lu, Guo, and Fang transfers cleanly, but since probability distributions on $|G_0|$ elements are not determined by their mean for $|G_0|>2$, we must use explicit terminal bridge laws to find a dimension-independent bound for the terminal-discrepancy estimate. We have formalized our result in Lean 4. The formalization is publicly available.

title: Random Diophantine inequalities in few variables
abstract: We prove that for almost all additive Diophantine inequalities of degree $k$ in at least $k+1$ variables the expected asymptotic formula for the density of solutions holds true. This improves the result of Brüdern and Dietmann \cite{BD}.

title: A counterexample on the main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles
abstract: The main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles predicts the existence of a unique strongly positive flat compatible Hermitian metric for every $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundle. We use cyclic Higgs bundles to disprove this conjecture for every rank $n \geq 3.$

title: Beyond weak convergence of signed spectral measures: Eigenvector overlaps and high-dimensional prediction risk
abstract: Many results in random matrix theory and high-dimensional statistics depend on weak convergence of spectral measures, which is usually established via pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms. This approach has recently been applied to signed measures. However, for signed measures, pointwise convergence of Stieltjes transforms alone no longer characterizes weak convergence. While this is unproblematic in many cases, in the high-dimensional regression setting, recently considered by Green and Romanov (2025), the underlying signed eigenvector-overlap measures can fail to converge weakly, despite pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms. Using a novel approach to risk analysis, we show that weak convergence can be replaced by a simple convergence result for bilinear forms. This allows us to establish convergence of the prediction risk for estimators based on arbitrary continuous spectral filters, including (regularized) gradient descent and ridge regression, even when the underlying signed measures fail to converge weakly. Under additional regularity conditions, we construct an explicit finite signed measure yielding an integral representation of the asymptotic prediction risk. This representation provides necessary and sufficient conditions for minimum-norm interpolation and optimally tuned ridge regression to attain the smallest asymptotic prediction risk among estimators with continuous spectral filters. Moreover, we provide characterizations of weak and vague convergence of finite signed measures in terms of pointwise convergence of their Stieltjes transforms.

title: Sign components for general bosonic-fermionic coinvariant rings
abstract: We prove that the sign-isotypic components of the symmetric group coinvariant rings $R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(a,b)}$ and $R_n^{(k+a,\ell+b)}$ are isomorphic if and only if $n \leq 2$ or at least one of $(k,\ell)$ or $(a,b)$ is $(0,0)$ or $(0,1)$. Moreover, for $k \geq 1$ the $ν$-isotypic components $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(0,1)}\right)^ν$ and $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell+1)}\right)^ν$ are isomorphic if and only if $ν$ corresponds to the sign representation. We also show that the socle of $R_n^{(k,\ell)}$ always contains the sign component, extending one direction of a result of Haiman for $R_n^{(2,0)}$. We settle the hook components conjecture of Bergeron (2024) for coinvariant rings, and a conjecture of Bergeron (2020) that the multiplicity of the sign character of $R_n^{(1,2)}$ is $3^{n-1}$. Our results also recover several existing results in the literature. Lastly, we extend our results to the hyperoctahedral group ${\mathfrak{B}_n}$ and prove that the determinant-isotypic components of $R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(0,1)}$ and $R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(k,\ell+1)}$ are isomorphic.

title: Cluster-roots of $n$-representation-finite algebras
abstract: We study cluster-roots of $n$-representation-finite algebras, namely the dimension vectors of cluster-indecomposable modules. We give a direct proof of Mizuno's higher analogue of Gabriel's theorem, and show that cluster-roots are precisely the non-negative integer vectors whose Coxeter orbits contain the dimension vector of an indecomposable projective module. Moreover, we give an explicit description of all cluster-roots of the $(n-1)$-Auslander algebras of type $A$. For $n=2$, we use periodic integer sequences to give a method for constructing counterexamples to Mizuno's positivity conjecture within this family, which reduces to determining whether finitely many quadratic equations admit non-negative integer solutions.

title: Remarks on the BKM criterion for both classical and variable Euler systems
abstract: In this paper, we establish new results on BKM-type criteria for the incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ as well as the Euler equations with space-time variable coefficients in a bounded domain. Our first result shows that if a finite-energy solution to the Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ blows up at a time $T_\ast$, and $T_\ast$ is the first such time, then $\limsup_{t\to T_\ast^-}(T_\ast -t)^{1+2k/5}\|D^kω(t)\|_{L^\infty} = \infty$ for every $k \geq 1$, thereby excluding the endpoint rate allowed by previously established lower bounds. The proof assumes the endpoint rate as an upper bound near the blowup time and uses a result by Chae and Wolf to obtain a contradiction. The second result gives a BKM-type criterion for solutions to the incompressible Euler equations with variable coefficients in the minimal regularity class $H^r$, where $r \in (2.5,3)$.

title: Diffusion phenomena for evolution equations
abstract:
We study the diffusion phenomenon for the abstract damped wave equation $u''+Bu'+Au=0$ on a Banach space and its possibly degenerate parabolic counterpart $Bv'+Av=0$. We assume that $B$ is bounded and the wave equation is well-posed, without requiring symmetry, injectivity, or commutativity of $A$ and $B$. Our aim is to identify initial data for which the parabolic solution is a genuine diffusive profile: $\|u(t)-v(t)\|=o(\|v(t)\|)$ as $t\to\infty$.
  Using Fourier analysis of resolvent expressions for the associated quadratic and linear operator pencils, we establish decay estimates for the difference of hyperbolic and parabolic solutions and their time derivatives. In particular, we characterize broad classes of initial data yielding the classical upper bounds of orders $t^{-1}$ and $t^{-2}$. We also prove lower bounds for both solutions, of the form $\|u(t)\|,\|v(t)\|\gtrsim r(t)$, for large sets of initial data and arbitrary prescribed functions $r(t)\to0$ that decay sufficiently slowly. Combining these results with high- and low-frequency resolvent estimates and a condition on the ranges of $A$ and $B$, we obtain genuine diffusive profiles. The analysis uses spectral properties of a sectorially holomorphic parabolic solution semigroup, which need not be strongly continuous.
  We apply the theory to damped wave equations on $L^2(Ω)$ with the Dirichlet Laplacian and bounded nonnegative damping that may vanish on large sets. We establish criteria for the required resolvent and range conditions, treat the whole space and exterior domains, and construct diffusive initial data using Weyl sequences.

title: Relative divisors and intersections of noncommutative rational localizations
abstract:
The simple constituents of monic pencils determine singularity support in a free skew field. For a pencil inverse algebra that is a free ideal ring, the multiplicities of the nonbase constituents compute the scalar-regular part of Cohn's matrix divisor theory. For independent generic invertible matrices of size at least two, every entry of a nonidentity free-group word is an atom with one relative singularity component. In rank two, opposite pivots give the exact identifications among these components. Intersections of word-entry localizations are then given by intersections of their label sets. An irreducible pencil of dimension six represents a commutator entry.
  For an algebra finitely generated over the free polynomial algebra at a common regular scalar point, the residual closure is a finite pencil inverse algebra determined by the generators' common domain. Every nonzero inverse-adjoining defect is infinite-dimensional. We compute how free-group quotients change intersections and give additive formulas for general quotient and tensor intersections. We prove Berenstein--Retakh's polygon conjecture using $n-2$ charts for $n\geq4$. For an unpunctured Möbius strip with $n\geq2$ boundary marks, the upper-algebra equality follows from $n+1$ charts. For the once-marked strip, the allowed algebra is strictly smaller than its residual hull, which equals the full chart.

title: Stability of Hilbert--Samuel functions with linear bounds in homological degree
abstract: Let $(R,\mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring and let $I$ be generated by a filter regular sequence. Set $A=R/I$, $s=\dim A>0$, and $D= \operatorname{hdeg}(A)$. If $A$ is equicharacteristic, we prove that perturbations of order $(2s+1)D$ preserve the Hilbert--Samuel function in every dimension. In arbitrary characteristic, we obtain the order $[s+(s+1)(k!)^{k-1}]D^k$, where $k$ is the maximum of $1$ and the dimensions of the lower deficiency modules of $\widehat A$. Both bounds depend only on the final quotient. The proof constructs monic annihilating equations for the deficiency modules and uses them to choose a parameter $d$-sequence with an explicit relation to a reduction of the maximal ideal. In the equicharacteristic case, a dimension filtration and characteristic polynomials over regular subrings give equations of degree at most the arithmetic degree, with coefficients in the required powers of the reduction.

title: Exact Values and Bounds for Four Color Quadratic Polynomial van der Waerden Numbers
abstract:
For a nonzero polynomial $P(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $P(0)=0$, let $W(P(x);4)$ denote the least integer $N$ such that every four coloring of $[N]$ contains distinct integers $u,v$ of the same color with $v-u=P(d)$ for some integer $d$. The best known general upper bounds for polynomial van der Waerden numbers are primitive recursive but remain enormous compared with the few known exact values.
  In this paper we determine the exact four color polynomial van der Waerden numbers for \[ \begin{gathered} x^2+x,\quad 2x^2+x,\quad 3x^2+x,\\ x^2+7x,\quad 2x^2+7x,\quad 3x^2+7x,\\ x^2+9x,\quad 2x^2+9x,\quad 3x^2+11x. \end{gathered} \]
  We derive upper bounds using combinatorial proofs and lower bounds using constructions of explicit colorings of $[N]$ found using the alternative computing inspired method of simulated annealing.
  More generally, we also prove that the four color polynomial van der Waerden numbers for the entire family of nonzero polynomials $ex^2+fx$ grow only linearly in the magnitude of their coefficients \[ W(ex^2+fx;4)=Θ(|e|+|f|). \]

title: Falconer's conjecture through descent and chaining
abstract: OpenAI proved that a compact set $E\subset{\mathbb R}^d$ of Hausdorff dimension greater than $\frac{d}{2}$ determines a set of Euclidean distances of positive length. We give a complete proof of this theorem which follows the overall architecture of the OpenAI argument, from the construction of the initial pair measures to the final Fourier estimate, but which modifies that argument substantially at the points where the geometric costs are paid and where the estimates are reassembled. The reductions are organized by the descent and chaining viewpoint of Burstein, Iosevich, and Krause: one potential, built from two separated depths together with a penalty for insufficient separation, pays for every reduction on every interval of scales, the terminal intervals included, and a finite-record chaining lemma keeps the fixed power losses attached to the few reductions which incur them. In odd dimensions the radial improvement is obtained directly at each finite scale from a quantitative contact interval, chosen by minimizing a mass curve against lines of two slopes, with explicit margins in place of a compactness argument, and the conditional estimates on the three parts of that interval are multiplied by a lemma on full source fibers. A random sign identity represents the coarse pair filter by products of endpoint multipliers and reduces the cost of reassembling the spatial pieces inside the shell estimate. The argument gives more than positive length. Since the mass first excluded near heavy hyperplanes at each late scale is summable with a power rate, all the Fourier estimates compare with one fixed measure, and the distance set supports a probability measure with an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$ and with power Fourier decay, so that $Δ(E)$ has positive Fourier dimension.

title: Splitting and Alternating Minimization Methods for Training Orthogonal Deep Feedforward Networks
abstract: Training deep feedforward networks with weight matrices constrained to layer-wise Stiefel manifolds serves as an effective regularization technique to improve generalization. However, the simultaneous presence of orthogonality constraints and nonsmooth activation functions poses severe theoretical and computational challenges for standard stochastic gradient and Riemannian optimization methods. In this paper, we propose two splitting and alternating-based algorithms to train orthogonal deep feedforward networks (OrthDFNs). By introducing auxiliary variables, we decouple the nested nonsmooth compositions and manifold constraints into a structured equality-constrained optimization problem. To solve this model, we develop OrthALM, an inexact augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) that employs a proximal alternating minimization scheme to solve its subproblems. Crucially, every block coordinate subproblem admits an exact, closed-form solution. We establish a rigorous convergence theory for OrthALM, proving that every accumulation point of the generated sequence is a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) point of the regularized, reformulated problem. Furthermore, we introduce OrthADMM as a practical, proximal-free variant that executes a single inner alternating sweep per multiplier update to accelerate computation. Extensive numerical experiments show that OrthALM attains lower training error and constraint residuals than OrthADMM in most configurations. OrthADMM achieves competitive test accuracy and the lowest reported runtime in most comparisons with the selected baselines.

title: Real monopole Floer homology and the Alexander polynomial
abstract: We prove that the Euler characteristic of the framed real monopole Floer homology of the double branched cover of a link is given by the Alexander polynomial evaluated at $\sqrt{-1}$. For knots $K$ with determinant one, this formula shows that Miyazawa's degree invariant of $K$ can be computed in terms of the Alexander polynomial of $K$. The proof involves a new connected-sum formula and oriented skein exact triangles for some new variants of real monopole Floer homology, called the diagonal and cone real monopole Floer homology, which admit mod-two gradings. This is the monopole counterpart of Srivastava's Euler characteristic formula in real Heegaard Floer homology.

title: Orthogonal Splines Associated to Root Systems and Applications to Function Approximation From Generalized Derivative Samples
abstract:
Let $\mathcal{S}(X)$ be the principal shift invariant space generated by a box spline $B_X$ with $d$-dimensional direction set $X$ and associated differential operator $D_X$. Assuming that each direction in $X$ appears with even multiplicity i.e $X = [X_0|X_0]$, we may endow $\mathcal{S}(X)$ with a special inner product $\langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle_X$ which is similar to a homogeneous Sobolev-like inner product of order $|X_0|$. Then, for the special case when the directions in $X$ are selected from a root system, we introduce bi-orthogonal systems for $\mathcal{S}(X)$. Within any fixed bi-orthogonal system, each basis function is compactly supported albeit the diameter of the supports of the basis functions is not uniformly bounded. On the other hand, the image of any bi-orthogonal system under $D_X$ (which is necessarily finite and discrete) is uniformly finite. In other words, the basis elements, while having non-sparse box-spline representation, are uniformly sparse in their truncated-power representation.
  Using the Sobolev-like inner product and an aforementioned biorthogonal system for $\mathcal{S}(X)$, the analysis-synthesis operator from smooth compactly supported continuous functions into $\mathcal{S}(X)$ is well-defined. Using integration by parts and the orthogonality satisfied by the bases under $\langle \cdot , \cdot \rangle_X$, this operator is a local discrete quasi-interpolation operator. When $X$ comes from an irreducible root system, we can slightly modify these quasi-interpolants to ensure they have optimal approximation order. In other words, if $f$ is sufficiently smooth and compactly supported, we can optimally approximate $f$ from a collection of generalized derivative samples induced by one of our bases.

title: Damped wave equation with a dynamic boundary condition: sharp resolvent estimate
abstract: This work investigates the stabilization of a wave equation with a localized damping and dynamic boundary conditions. This model traces back to the classical treatment of torsion and impact problems. Consider a second-order hyperbolic equation posed with a dynamic boundary condition on a smooth compact Riemannian manifold $(\M,g)$ with boundary, in which the damping acts either in the interior or on $\d \M$. Under the assumption that the damping is positive on an open subset of its domain of action, a resolvent estimate is established. A logarithmic decay rate is then deduced for the energy of strong solutions. We provide examples that establish the sharpness of the resolvent estimate.

title: Cubic fourfolds with a symplectic involution from finite Prym data
abstract: We study how many polarized anti-invariant factors of the intermediate Jacobians of smooth Eckardt hyperplane sections determine a cubic fourfold with a symplectic involution. In rank three, the equation is determined by its fixed cubic surface and a conic in the dual projective space. The Torelli theorem of Casalaina-Martin--Zhang recovers the surface together with one plane section from each factor. When the surface has no automorphisms, these planes can be compared in a common dual space, and reconstruction reduces to classical conic interpolation. Five factors suffice without parameter data, and four suffice with their ordered parameter configuration; both bounds are sharp. In rank two, we construct two-dimensional families of pairwise nonisomorphic equivariant fourfolds with the same entire unparametrized Prym image. For a fixed fourfold, we also show that the closure of the anti-invariant factor family in an associated OG10 compactification is an integral projective Lagrangian subvariety.

title: schubmult: Symbolic algorithms and input-sensitive bounds for Schubert multiplication
abstract: We present schubmult, a GPL-licensed Python system for exact multiplication of ordinary, double, quantum, and quantum double Schubert polynomials, as well as independent-alphabet triple and quantum triple products. Its central algorithm expands one factor into filtered column paths and couples them to Pieri computations on the other factor. Dynamic programming shares intermediate states, and the algorithm returns every Schubert-basis coefficient as an exact arithmetic circuit. We prove input-sensitive operation bounds for the entire product, not just a selected coefficient: for inputs of minimal rank $n$, the classical algorithms have complexity $2^{O(n\log n)}$ and polynomial complexity in $n$ for fixed Lehmer-code lengths. The quantum algorithms have the same general bound and polynomial complexity when, in addition, the number of nonzero entries in the Lehmer code of $v^{-1}$ is fixed. We describe the implementation and distinguish it from the algorithms analyzed, verify computations against independent routines and exact identities, and report reproducible timings for flag and Grassmannian workloads. Parabolic quantum products are treated separately via the Peterson-Woodward comparison.

title: Asymptotic Consistency of a Weighted Nadaraya-Watson Estimator Driven by Fractional Brownian Motion at Random Times
abstract: Nonparametric regression conventionally assumes equispaced observations, a premise often violated by empirical data with irregular sampling and long-memory noise. This study establishes the asymptotic mean square ($L^2$) consistency of a weighted Nadaraya-Watson (wN-W) estimator for stochastic processes sampled at random times and perturbed by fractional Brownian motion (fBm). Leveraging the occupation time formula and Fernique's Theorem, we derive exact parametric restrictions on bandwidth and sampling rates ensuring convergence. We validate these theoretical findings via extensive simulations evaluating the mean squared error under varying noise persistence. Crucially, we explicitly benchmark the performance of the estimator under random sampling times against classical deterministic grids, while assessing the relative efficiency of quartic versus Gaussian kernels. Finally, we introduce an interactive Shiny application to dynamically visualize the admissible parameter space, and we empirically validate our theoretical framework by applying the estimator to the Vostok ice core paleoclimatological dataset. This real-world application demonstrates the practical capacity of the methodology to extract macroscopic trends while robustly avoiding severe overfitting under random sampling times.\

title: Connected regular $Γ$-distance magic graphs with magic constant zero
abstract: Let $(Γ,+)$ be a finite Abelian group. A $Γ$-distance magic labeling of a graph is a bijection from its vertex set to $Γ$ such that the sum of the labels of the neighbours of each vertex is a fixed element of $Γ$, called the magic constant. The constructions of Kovář and collaborators provide regular distance magic graphs of odd order with consecutive integer labels for every even degree from $4$ to $14$. We adapt these constructions to prove the existence of connected $r$-regular $(A\times\mathbb{Z}_n)$-distance magic graphs with magic constant $0$, where $A$ is any finite Abelian group of odd order, $n$ is odd, and $r\in\{4,6,8,10,12,14\}$, under explicit sufficient conditions on $n$. Here $\mathbb{Z}_n$ is the cyclic group of order $n$. It suffices to take $n\ge13$ for $r=6$, $n\ge19$ for $r=14$, and $n\ge15$ for $r\in\{4,8,10,12\}$.

title: Stochastic Dominance in Discrete Parking Processes on Graphs
abstract: In a recent study on the one-dimensional discrete parking process, it was conjectured that the number of occupied sites in the sequential model first-order stochastically dominates its static counterpart on any path graph. In this paper, we first prove this conjecture for all path graphs and then explore whether stochastic dominance holds for general graph topologies. We show that the property extends naturally to all cycle graphs, and an exhaustive computational analysis confirms that it holds for all 31 connected simple graphs with fewer than 6 vertices. For graphs with 6 or more vertices, we demonstrate that this dominance does not hold universally by constructing explicit counterexamples in which the static model dominates the sequential one; moreover, while one model always dominates the other for all connected graphs with up to 7 vertices, we show that stochastic comparability fails starting at 8 vertices. We also prove that stochastic dominance is inherited by disjoint unions when all connected components share the same dominance direction, and we exhibit mixed unions in which stochastic comparability is either preserved or lost. Finally, supported by algorithmic computations, we formulate a conjecture proposing that the dominance of the sequential model over the static one holds for all graphs with maximum degree at most 3.

title: Critical schemes, jet syzygies, and twisted periods
abstract: We study nonreduced critical schemes with prescribed support on nilpotent orbit closures and on the Kleinian singularity $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, and show that one specified minimal invariant syzygy among the first jet equations fixes their scheme structure. For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_N$ or $\mathfrak{so}_{2N}$ with Coxeter number $h$ and $p\ge2$ coprime to $h$, the selected polynomial is the coefficient of $s^{p+1}$ in $\det(1-sM)^{p/h}$, with reduced critical locus $\{M^p=0\}$, and the selecting syzygy is equivalent to the twisted period equation of Dubrovin and Feigin-Silantyev. The minimal invariant syzygies of that degree correspond to the lowest nonquadratic twisted periods, which, for $\mathfrak{so}_8$, form the standard representation of triality; in type D the Betti number alone does not determine the scheme. On $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, the selected polynomial is given by a terminating hypergeometric series. Restriction to Slodowy slices commutes with forming critical schemes and their nilradicals. These results determine, uniformly in rank and degree, the rings and nilradical filtrations through which the Schur and Macdonald indices of the corresponding Argyres-Douglas theories are proposed to arise as Hilbert series of arc spaces.

title: Structural Results on the Unfair 0-1 Polynomial Conjecture
abstract: A $0$-$1$ polynomial is a polynomial whose coefficients are all either $0$ or $1$. The unfair $0$-$1$ polynomial conjecture states that if $f$ is a $0$-$1$ polynomial and $f(x)=g(x)h(x)$ is a factorisation into non-constant polynomials with non-negative real coefficients, then $g$ and $h$ must themselves be $0$-$1$ polynomials. We call $f$ fair if every such factorisation has this property, and unfair otherwise. In this paper, we study structural properties of possible unfair factorisations and obtain conditions which guarantee fairness. In particular, we prove that if $$ f(x)=x^{n-\operatorname{deg} w}w(x)+v(x), $$ where $v$ and $w$ are $0$-$1$ polynomials and $v$ is fair, then $f$ is fair whenever $$ n\geq\max\{\operatorname{deg} w+2\operatorname{deg} v,\,2\operatorname{deg} w\}. $$

title: What the occupation law of a finite Markov chain determines: time reversal and principal minors
abstract: What does the occupation law of a finite Markov chain determine about its generator $Q$? From the stationary start, the law of the occupation times at one time determines $Q$ exactly up to time reversal and reversals of memoryless blocks, the sets of states that are all left at one rate with one landing law and are entered in proportion to the stationary law. These reversals commute and give exactly $2^k$ generators, with $k$ read off a tree of memoryless blocks. This leaves only time reversal when $Q$ has no rank-one cut, when there are at most 4 states, and generically. The law at one time determines the law at every time, and a generic start determines $Q$. A renewal block is a set of states that is left at the same rates from each of its states, is entered with one law, and is charged by the start in proportion to that law. From every start the law determines $Q$ exactly up to lumped reversals, which lump disjoint renewal blocks to single states and reverse a memoryless block of the lumped chain. We also find every start that hides time reversal. At the scale of large deviations, the functional of Donsker and Varadhan determines exactly the principal minors of $-Q$.

title: Divergent Trajectories in the $3x+1$ Problem and a ${\em S}$- Units Equation
abstract: In this note we assume the existence of divergent trajectories (if any) under the Collatz map and investigate the consequences of this assumption, even though the Conjecture of Collatz seems to be true. In a trajectory we show that the Diophantine exponential equation $x + y = w 2^n$ in the integers $x, y, w, n$ plays an important role. In this context the recent strong finiteness theorem of Bennett and Billerey on ${\it S}-Units has consequences on the set of prime numbers generated by a collection of local minima, called wave-minima (defined ad hoc for simplicity's sake) in a divergent trajectory. It allows to define canonically a density of a trajectory and some conjectures and open problems related to these prime numbers.

title: Frames and representing systems in Hardy spaces
abstract: We study representing systems of Cauchy kernels or dilations of a given function in Hardy spaces. We give a complete geometric description of countable sets $Λ\subset \mathbb{D}$ such that the system $\{\hat{k}_λ\}_{λ\in Λ}$ of normalized Cauchy kernels forms a generalized frame in the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{D})$ with $p \in (1, \infty)$ with respect to a particular coefficient space. For a wide class of functions we construct representing systems of their dilations in $H^2$. We also obtain a linear method for expanding functions in series of Cauchy kernels in $H^2$.

title: Piecewise Interpretations in Many-Sorted Logic
abstract: Piecewise interpretations, introduced by Visser, generalize ordinary interpretations between first-order theories by allowing formulae to be interpreted using disjoint unions of definable sets. This makes it possible to capture natural constructions, such as the projective completion of an affine plane, but also leads to a notion of equivalence of theories, namely piecewise bi-interpretability. We develop the theory of piecewise interpretations systematically in the many-sorted setting. Each piecewise interpretation induces a semantic dual, a functor between categories of models. In addition, we introduce a syntactic notion of morphism between piecewise interpretations, which likewise has a semantic dual. Using these semantic duals, we collect theories, piecewise interpretations, and morphisms between them into a bicategory, in particular defining a well-behaved notion of composition of interpretations, associative up to coherent isomorphism. As an application, we consider a familiar idea, championed by Quine, namely that one can replace any many-sorted theory with a corresponding single-sorted one by replacing sorts with sortal predicates. We show that this leads to a biequivalence between the developed bicategories of theories with finitely many sorts and single-sorted theories, thereby providing an argument for the dispensability of sorts.

title: The Sprague--Grundy Function of Slow Exact $k$-Nim with $k+1$ Piles
abstract: We give an explicit formula for the normal-play Sprague--Grundy (SG) function of slow exact $k$-Nim with $k+1$ piles. A move removes one stone from each of exactly $k$ nonempty piles. A truncation preserves every legal move sequence. The SG value depends only on the total of the truncated coordinates modulo $2k$, their number of odd entries, and the parities of the two smallest piles. For every $k\geq2$, the set of the SG values is $\{0,1,2,3\}$. We prove the formula by the mex characterization, including the reductions needed after boundary moves. We also prove a unit-shift identity and use it with a known optimal-move theorem to explain the four-value bound independently of the explicit formula.

title: A regular free action on the integral plane and a problem on left braces
abstract: We construct a free subgroup of countably infinite rank in $\ZZ^2\rtimes\SL_2(\ZZ)$ that acts regularly on $\ZZ^2$. At each stage we adjoin an affine transformation taking the origin to the least point of a prescribed orbit. Disjoint domains for reduced words ensure that the stabilizer of the origin remains trivial. The orbit map gives a left brace with additive group $\ZZ^2$ and multiplicative group free of countably infinite rank. This group contains a nonabelian free subgroup and is therefore nonsolvable, answering both parts of Problem 20.126 of the Kourovka Notebook.

title: The frustration index of fully frustrated hypercubes
abstract:
The frustration index of a signed graph is the minimum number of edges meeting every negative cycle. Let $F_n$ be the frustration index of the signed $n$-cube $Q_n$ in which every square is negative. Using signings constructed from weighted cubes, we prove that for every positive integer $r$, \[
  F_{r^2+1}=(r^2-r+1)2^{r^2-1}. \] When $4\mid r$, our construction also gives the exact value $F_n=(n-r-p/4)2^{n-2}$ in the six dimensions $n=r^2+1+pr/2$, $p\in\{\pm1,\pm2,\pm3\}$. In dimension nine an argument with integral eigenvectors gives $F_9=772$.
  By varying one weight in the construction for $r^2+1$, we obtain $F_n=(n-\sqrt n+O(n^{-1/2}))2^{n-2}$ for arbitrary $n$. The values at $n=r^2+1$ show that the error term has the best possible order. Taking the positive edges of an optimal signing gives a square-free subgraph of $Q_n$ with at least $(n+\sqrt n-O(n^{-1/2}))2^{n-2}$ edges whose complement is also square-free.

title: Existence, relative Morse index and the number of positive multi-peak solutions to subcritical Hamiltonian systems
abstract:
We construct positive multi-peak solutions of a singularly perturbed Hamiltonian elliptic system with a common uniformly positive potential $a$ and powers $p,q>1$ below the Sobolev critical hyperbola. The peaks concentrate at any prescribed set of $k$ distinct nondegenerate critical points $P_i$ of $a$.
  The Hessian of the action is strongly indefinite. A Schur complement gives exactly $kN$ eigenvalues near zero and their leading terms, which have order $\varepsilon^2$ and are determined by $D^2a(P_i)$. The solutions are nondegenerate. A scalar Schur reduction and localization of its inverse term give the relative Morse index $k+\sum_{i=1}^k\ind D^2a(P_i)$.
  Local Pohozaev identities give local uniqueness. A compactness argument then shows that, for $m$ prescribed nondegenerate critical points, the union of the fixed profile neighborhoods associated with their nonempty subsets contains exactly $2^m-1$ positive solutions. Using uniqueness of positive solutions of the limiting system up to translations, we obtain the same count in classes defined by nonvanishing in fixed balls and a scaled nonlinear mass bound that excludes an additional peak. We also give second-order expansions of the peak locations and rescaled profiles.

title: Golod thresholds of ideals and products of ideals in dimension 3
abstract: Let $I$ be a proper ideal in a standard graded polynomial ring $P$ with homogeneous maximal ideal $\m$. We show that there exists $k_0\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\m^kI$ is Golod for all $k\geq k_0$. The smallest such $k_0$ is denoted $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$. We give an explicit formula for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ in the case when $I$ is a monomial complete intersection and bounds for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ for other classes of ideals. We show that under a certain degree condition, the product of a Golod ideal with a maximal homogeneous ideal is Golod. In the last section, we show that in a regular local ring of dimension 3, the product of any two proper ideals is Golod; this solves a question posed by Dao-Stefani \cite[Question 4.5]{dao2022monomial} and VandeBogert \cite[Question 4.11]{vandebogert2022products}.

title: A Novel Iterative Algorithm Incorporating Machine Learning for the Poisson-Nernst-Planck Equations in Three-Dimensional Ion Channel Simulation
abstract: The Poisson Nernst Planck (PNP) equation is widely used to simulate ion channel transport, but its strong nonlinearity and coupling characteristics make numerical solutions extremely challenging, and decoupling methods are usually required. The Gummel iteration method is widely adopted as a common decoupling algorithm owing to its simplicity, ease of implementation, and applicability even under complex conditions. But its convergence efficiency highly depends on the selection of the relaxation parameter, unsuitable parameters will lead to slow convergence or even divergence. At present, parameter selection relies heavily on manual experience, which is inefficient and unstable, significantly hindering the solving efficiency for practical problems such as ion channel simulations. To address this, we propose a machine learning-based parameter selection method, which can select near-optimal relaxation parameters for the Gummel iteration of PNP equations for ion channels. Based on the machine learning-based parameter selection algorithm, we develop a coupled finite element and Gummel iteration solver, and more stable convergence and higher computational efficiency have been achieved in ion channel simulations. To validate the method, we conduct tests on two real channels with complex geometries that differ significantly from the training samples. Numerical results demonstrate that this method has a significant effect on improving the convergence efficiency and stability of Gummel iteration, confirming its applicability in practical ion channel simulations.

title: Perimeter-Regularized Critical Shapes in the Class $\mathcal{O}_C$: Core-Normal Transfer and First-Order Return-Map Response
abstract: Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a compact strictly convex core and $\mathcal{O}_C$ denote the class of domains whose outer boundary is a global outward normal graph over $\partial C$ and whose inward boundary normals return to the interior of $C$. We study volume-constrained critical domains of the Dirichlet-perimeter functional: \[ \mathcal{E}_μ(Ω) = -\frac{1}{2}\int_Ω|\nabla u_Ω|^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x + μP(Ω), \qquad -Δu_Ω = f, \quad u_Ω|_{\partialΩ}=0, \] in the large-perimeter regime $μ\to\infty$. We give an adapted Lyapunov--Schmidt construction near translated spheres to extract the first physical shape coefficient of scale $μ^{-1}$. We then prove that $\mathcal{O}_C$ is open under small $C^1$ thickness perturbations and establish a quantitative coordinate-transfer theorem to a unique core-normal thickness. Finally, we prove that the forward return-map operator $d \mapsto F_d$ is Fréchet $C^1$ between Hölder spaces and provide its explicit derivative. This yields a shape-to-dynamics sensitivity theorem for $\mathcal{O}_C$: a perimeter-regularized PDE-constrained critical deformation produces an explicitly controlled first-order deformation of the return dynamics. A nonradial example confirms that the response coefficient is generically nonzero.

title: Regularization Independence in the One-Dimensional Schrödinger Equation with Delta Potential
abstract: We consider a class of regularizations $\{δ_\varepsilon\}$ of the Dirac delta defined by a uniform $L^1$ bound, the normalization $\intδ_\varepsilon\to1$, and a truncated first-moment condition, with no restriction on sign, shape, support, or scaling. For this class we prove that the transmission and reflection coefficients for the Hamiltonian operator $H_\varepsilon=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}-λδ_\varepsilon$ at fixed energy converge to those of the delta interaction. Under the additional assumption that each $δ_\varepsilon$ is bounded, we show that any family of negative eigenvalues of $H_\varepsilon$ bounded away from zero converges to $-λ^2/4$ when $λ>0$, and that no such family exists when $λ<0$. Both convergences are obtained with an explicit rate, expressed through two integrals of $δ_\varepsilon$, directly computable for a given regularization. The bound-state convergence follows from the work of Brasche, Figari, and Teta; here, our contribution is an elementary proof with an explicit rate. Their norm resolvent convergence, however, does not by itself imply convergence of the scattering matrix, which was previously known for families obtained by scaling a single fixed profile; we prove it for a strictly larger class.

title: Automating the Derivation of Advanced Algorithms in Numerical Linear Algebra using Associative Algebras with Involution
abstract:
Standard algorithms of numerical linear algebra use their scalars through seven operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, the adjoint, the $*$-square root and $(i,j)$ indexing. This thesis overloads these operations, as automatic differentiation overloads arithmetic, allowing scalars in associative algebras with involution. Many of the resulting decompositions and algorithms reduce to Hermitian eigendecomposition over these $*$-algebras.
  The decompositions are organised by doubly-signed quivers, whose vertices record real, complex or quaternionic scalars and the action of the involution. We prove an analogue of Gabriel's theorem: every finite-dimensional real $*$-algebra is a matrix algebra, with sizes and signs, over a quotient of its quiver's path $*$-algebra. Spectral theorems, the singular value decomposition, Takagi factorisation, Sylvester's law of inertia and the real Jordan form arise as unitary similarity problems for Hermitian matrices.
  Division and square roots take place in a completed localisation which inverts the arrows. For the singular value decomposition, Householder tridiagonalisation becomes Golub--Kahan bidiagonalisation. Over split-complex numbers, the QR algorithm becomes Rutishauser's LR algorithm, two steps at a time, and Cholesky factorisation becomes Doolittle's LU factorisation. These identifications require suitable $*$-square roots and hold whenever the steps are defined.
  Infinitesimals make limits of algorithms exact computations: Gram--Schmidt yields the Bruhat decomposition, and Gaussian elimination with pivots chosen by orders of magnitude yields Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm in leading terms. A Python library implements the seven operations and algorithms. An appendix visualises the QR algorithm on $2\times2$ real matrices.

title: Randomly growing uniform hypergraphs
abstract: We investigate growing uniform random hypergraphs whose hyperedges are $(k-1)$-simplices. At each step, one of two processes occurs: (i) a new vertex is added with probability $p$; (ii) a simplex $\langle v_1,\ldots,v_k\rangle$ with randomly chosen distinct vertices is added with probability $1-p$. Emerging random uniform hypergraphs exhibit a percolation transition. A giant component is formed when $p<p_c=1-(2k-1)^{-2}$. The fraction of vertices in the giant component scales as $\exp[-C/\sqrt{p_c-p}]$, a signature of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase transition. In the non-percolating phase, the cluster size distribution has an algebraic tail with a continuously varying exponent, while at $p=p_c$, it acquires a logarithmic correction. We analyze triadic hypergraphs ($k=3$) in detail and then generalize to higher $k$. We show that the Euler characteristic and the first Betti number of the giant component scale linearly with system size. Higher Betti numbers fluctuate between realizations but remain finite, and hence the normalized Euler characteristic and the first Betti number of the giant component are asymptotically equal, up to a sign.

title: Complete Intersection Semigroups and End Curves on Singularities of Splice Type
abstract: We prove that any complete intersection numerical semigroup can be realized as the value semigroup of an end curve in a splice quotient singularity. Therefore, providing a converse to the semigroup-theoretic statement of the End Curve Theorem of Neumann and Wahl for integral homology sphere links. Moreover, for a complete-intersection numerical semigroup, we define a family of knots such that the Alexander polynomial of any knot of the family coincides (up to a factor) with the generating series of the semigroup. Let $(X,0)$ be a splice quotient singularity with $\mathbb{Z}HS^3$ link $Σ$ and let $(C,0)$ be a reduced curve-germ embedded in $(X,0)$ defined as the zero locus of the product of end curve functions. We prove, thorugh our topological characterization of complete intersection semigroups, the coincidence between the Alexander polynomial of the knot cut out by $C$ in $Σ$ and the Poincaré series of the embedded curve. Hence providing a generalization of the result due to Campillo, Delgado and Gusein-Zade for plane curve singularities. Furthermore, for any good resolution of $(X,0)$ compatible with the splice quotient analytic structure, we provide an explicit description of the semigroup of integer multiplicities of functions along any divisor of the resolution.

title: Hopf algebras of leaf-graded forests
abstract: We examine the relationship between the Hopf algebra on nonplanar binary forests, previously defined by the author, and a Hopf algebra defined by Bruned and used in the renormalization of stochastic PDEs. We show that Bruned's Hopf algebra and its reduced analogue, previously studied by Foissy in the context of combinatorial twisted bialgebras, are dual to Hopf algebras derived from pre-Lie insertion operations respecting the number of leaves, which induce leaf-based gradings on the dual Hopf algebras. We compute Hochschild 1-cocycles for these Hopf algebras and show that Bruned's Hopf algebra satisfies a similar universal property as the Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra.

title: Maximal nilpotence for higher Verlinde categories
abstract: We show that all higher Verlinde categories are maximally nilpotent, as conjectured by Coulembier (2023). By previous results, it suffices to show that non-trivial simple objects have only finitely many non-zero symmetric powers in odd characteristic. We compute the maximal degrees of these non-zero symmetric and exterior powers explicitly, hence confirming their finiteness. We discuss some of the far-reaching consequences.

title: Bipartite Matchings, Matrix Permanents, and Zeon Power Series
abstract: Perfect matchings of a bipartite graph are counted by the permanent of the graph's biadjacency matrix, and permanents of sequences of structured biadjacency matrices lead to integer sequences. We consider a number of such sequences and illustrate how zeon-algebraic representations of bipartite graphs lead to recursively defined zeon sequences. Then, using formal power series methods, we show that the ``$Ω$-exponentials'' of these zeon sequences reveal numbers of perfect matchings in the graphs.

title: The higher order regularity problem for elliptic systems with data in Banach function spaces
abstract: We characterize the well-posedness of the higher order regularity problem in the upper half-space with data in Sobolev Banach function spaces by proving its equivalence to natural weighted estimates for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator. The generality of our framework allows for applications to Lebesgue spaces, rearrangement-invariant spaces such as Orlicz spaces, and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces, as well as their weighted counterparts, among others. This is established for the family of second-order, homogeneous, elliptic, constant complex coefficient systems in ${\mathbb{R}}^n$ that admit a distinguished coefficient tensor, a natural condition that always holds in the scalar case and for the Lamé system of elasticity.

title: ComBO: Community Bayesian Optimization for Carrier Shutdown in HAPS-Hypercell Networks
abstract: In this paper, we investigate carrier shutdown (CS) in high-altitude platform station (HAPS)-Hypercell-assisted networks, leveraging network-wide information to optimize both coverage macro cells and capacity cells CS. To address the high dimensionality of this problem, we propose ComBO, a community-aware Bayesian optimization framework that exploits user equipment (UE) reference signal received power (RSRP) reports to construct a fallback graph representing the underlying network and identify groups of strongly coupled cells. The resulting communities decompose the original optimization problem into lower-dimensional subproblems, which are sequentially optimized using trust region Bayesian optimization (TuRBO) and refined through a final joint search. Evaluation in a high-fidelity 3GPP-based system-level environment shows that ComBO consistently outperforms legacy CS strategies and overcomes the scalability limitations of global Bayesian optimization (BO). Considering normalized terrestrial power ComBO achieves nearly 84% savings while preserving quality of service. These results demonstrate the potential of community-aware decomposition as a scalable approach to large-scale network optimization.

title: Stability of equilibria in discrete-time modified-gradient systems and the multivariate breeder's equation
abstract:
The multivariate breeder's equation $Δ ar z=G
abla\ln ar W$ is a widely used discrete-time modified-gradient system describing the evolution of continuous traits in organisms. This system could more conventionally be expressed as $x_{k+1}=x_k+P_k
abla f(x_k)$. For its continuous-time counterpart $x'=P(t)
abla f(x)$, it has been proven that an isolated local maximum of $f$ is uniformly stable whenever $P(t)$ is positive semidefinite, as is the case for the "$G$-matrix." Furthermore, the continuous time system is uniformly asymptotically stable when the maximum is an isolated critical point and $\int_0^\inftyλ_1(P(t))\,dt=\infty$. We show that the literal discrete analog of this result is false: with constant positive definite $P$ the iterates can oscillate or diverge. The result is restored by a single additional hypothesis, a uniform bound on the largest eigenvalue of $P_k$, $λ_n$, such that $λ_n(P_k)\le 2/L$ where $L$ is a local Lipschitz constant of $
abla f$. Under this bound the maximum is uniformly stable; under a stricter version together with $\sum_kλ_1(P_k)=\infty$, the maximum is uniformly asymptotically stable. Given these hypotheses, a level-set estimate of the basin of attraction carries over. Both bounds are sharp, and each remaining hypothesis is shown to be necessary. Biologically, the bound says that genetic variance in every direction must be small relative to the curvature of log mean fitness; outside this regime the mean phenotype can overshoot a fitness peak as hypothesized by Fisher's geometric model. As further application of our results, the same conditions apply to the mean update of Gaussian evolutionary optimization algorithms, in which the covariance of the search population plays the role of $G$.

title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 5: cyclic total variation
abstract: We study the cyclic discrete total variation obtained by adding the wrap-around edge to the usual open-chain statistic. Under the uniform multinomial law the cyclic symmetry recombines the same per-edge, adjacent, and disjoint covariance blocks used for the linear statistic, but with different multiplicities, and this simplifies the variance: the bin-independent leading coefficient \(2A+4B\) carries over, the constant-order correction collapses \emph{exactly} to \(β_c(n)=β_1 n\) (no \(n^0\) or \(1/n\) tail; obtained directly here, and already reached in Part~2 through the transfer identity), and a conditional second-order coefficient \(γ_c(n)\) is given. The exact finite-\(N\) cyclic--linear transfer identity of Part~2, read order by order, both delivers these and, as its main consequence for the \emph{linear} statistic, explains the traveling mode of the linear variance: comparison with the (first-order) mode-free symmetric cyclic profile shows that deleting one edge introduces a rising contribution whose balance against the falling cyclic bulk creates a ridge at \(n\asymp\sqrt{K_0N}\) with local optimizer \(K_0=C_1/β_1\). Uniform control of three ridge blocks proves this optimizer on every compact ridge window, upgrading the previously heuristic \(\sqrt N\) mode law to a theorem; the global localization of the exact maximizer remains open. We also record the corresponding cyclic reference-centered statistic under a fixed alternative and the leading Nabeya variance formula for the matched non-uniform cyclic statistic. Throughout, ``exact'' refers to the asymptotic coefficient in \(N\); the operative symmetry is cyclic stationarity (rotation invariance), not exchangeability.

title: Fundamental Limits of Honest Inference with Heterogeneous Transfer Sources
abstract: Transfer learning can improve precision by borrowing information from external sources, but how much improvement is possible while maintaining valid inference? We address this by studying honest confidence intervals for a target parameter using multiple sources with heterogeneous prespecified discrepancy bounds. Under local information and admissibility conditions, we establish a universal lower bound on interval length for procedures maintaining uniform coverage. A scalar information equation characterizes the bound, revealing how precision depends jointly on source sample sizes and discrepancies. Large source samples need not yield greater precision gains when their discrepancies are large. When discrepancies are unrestricted, honest intervals cannot improve upon the target-only rate, even when all sources are unbiased. For the Gaussian location model, we calculate optimal source weights and construct honest intervals attaining the lower bound order, establishing sharpness. We extend the lower bound theory to semiparametric models through parametric submodels. For the Cox proportional hazards model, we verify the information conditions under which the lower bound applies, including under right censoring.

title: Additive Relations and Betti Growth in Goldbach Rings
abstract: The binary Goldbach ring over a field $k$ is the quotient of $R=k[x_p:p\text{ an odd prime}]$ by the relations $x_px_q=x_{p'}x_{q'}$ whenever $p+q=p'+q'$, with $°x_p=(p,1)$. We prove that if $g$ is a map from the odd primes to an abelian group and $g(p)+g(q)$ depends only on $p+q$, then $g(p)=g(3)+\frac{p-3}{2}(g(5)-g(3))$ for every odd prime $p$. This settles Kátai and Phong's conjecture on shifted prime arguments and proves, for odd primes, the affine classification they conjectured for binary sums. The universal group of binary prime relations is free of rank two. We obtain a minimal bigraded free resolution from compatible resolutions of finite truncations and determine the growth of its linear Betti numbers in two regimes. For fixed monomial degree $d\ge3$, as the Goldbach degree $n\to\infty$ through $n\equiv d\pmod2$, we prove $β_{d-1,n,d}\sim(d-1)T_d(n)/d!$, where $T_d(n)$ counts ordered representations by $d$ odd primes. Explicit Koszul cycles from common prime shifts span a positive fraction of this strand. For finite supports $\mathcal{A}_m=\{p\le m:p\text{ an odd prime}\}$, fix the homological degree $i\ge1$ and sum over all Goldbach degrees. As $m\to\infty$, the linear-strand totals are asymptotic to $i|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when all binary relations on $\mathcal{A}_m$ are retained, and to $(1-2^{-i})|\mathcal{A}_m|^{i+1}/(i+1)!$ when only relations of common weight at most $m$ are retained. These leading estimates are uniform over fields. The interpolation theorem gives eventual depth at most two for the variable truncations; both truncation families have asymptotically maximal projective dimension.

title: Uniform Hyperbolicity of Automorphism Orbit Graphs in Rank Two
abstract: We study automorphism orbit graphs of oriented conjugacy classes in the  free group of rank two, with every elementary Whitehead move assigned unit cost. Collapsing signed permutations of the basis turns each orbit component into a tree of edges and triangles. We obtain this description by combining the known rank-two conjugacy-class stabilizer structure with the Bass-Serre tree of the rank-two outer automorphism group. The simplified graph and all its vertex-induced subgraphs have optimal thin-triangle constant zero for tree components and 3/4 otherwise. Every whole orbit component of the original graph has thin-triangle constant at most 2, while every component of every vertex-induced subgraph has constant at most 5/2. Both bounds are sharp in the primitive orbit and apply to the full geometric realization, including edge-interior triangle corners. The hereditary upper estimate also follows from known chordality theory; the whole-component improvement uses the geometry of adjacent permutation fibres. These results complement earlier fixed-length and minimum-length orbit classifications.

title: Finite bases for matrix semirings: transfer theorems and nilpotent counterexamples
abstract: We first show that the nonfinitely based six-element ai-semiring $SR_6$ has finitely based full matrix semirings for every $n\ge2$, with a four-identity basis relative to the ai-semiring axioms. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first known example of this phenomenon. We then construct a countably infinite flat ai-semiring $P$ whose scalar and two-by-two matrix varieties are nonfinitely based, whereas its matrix varieties in sizes $n\ge3$ admit a five-identity relative basis. For both examples, the intervals from the scalar variety to each matrix variety of size at least two have cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Finally, we establish transfer results for stronger forms of nonfinite basability and a finite-basis dichotomy for matrix semirings of size at least two over scalars with a genuine zero generating a locally finite variety: finite basability in the multiplicatively nilpotent case, and inherent nonfinite basability otherwise.

title: An Inexact Augmented Lagrangian Method for Semidefinite Complementarity Optimization
abstract: Semidefinite complementarity constraints arise in applications such as inverse semidefinite programming and rank-constrained matrix optimization. We develop a structure-preserving augmented Lagrangian method (SPALM) for mathematical programs with these constraints. The method augments the smooth constraints and retains matrix complementarity in its subproblems. We handle these subproblems by an inexact proximal alternating framework with verifiable descent and stationarity conditions. With vanishing absolute subproblem errors, feasible accumulation points of infinite outer sequences are asymptotically M-stationary. Under AM-regularity, these points are M-stationary. We prove that active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ is sufficient for this regularity. For each AL subproblem, the full stationarity residual converges to zero along infinite accepted inner sequences if the initial sublevel set is bounded, the proximal parameters are bounded above and away from zero, and the block errors vanish. If the block errors are also square-summable, an $O(T^{-1/2})$ best-residual bound holds over $T$ accepted iterations. Huber-Stiefel and fixed-basis procedures generate feasible matrix candidates, whose acceptance is verified by descent tests and computable limiting-normal certificates. For rank-constrained correlation matrix approximation, we construct a lifting that preserves the projected feasible set and global optimal value and satisfies active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ at every feasible point. The stationarity guarantees apply to this lifted model. Finite-budget experiments on this lifting and a single-equality observation-fitting inverse SDP meet the prescribed numerical feasibility and stationarity tests in all 120 runs.

title: On the uniform algebras generated by powers of the coordinates and smooth functions on compact subsets of $\Bbb C^N$
abstract: Let $K\subset\Bbb C^N$ be compact and let $f=(f_1,\dots,f_N)$ be a smooth map on a neighbourhood of $K$. We give sufficient conditions for the algebra generated by $z_1^{m_1},\dots,z_N^{m_N}$ and $f_1,\dots,f_N$ (or by all monomials of degree $n$ and $f_1,\dots,f_N$) to be dense in $C(K)$. We appropriately extend the techniques developed in our previous works [3,4,6] and [8] for algebras of functions on the complex plane to tackle the problem in the several-variable setting. More precisely, the argument separates a purely algebraic reduction, in which the rotated graphs are glued one coordinate at a time, from the study of the single graph of $f$. For the latter we give an exact computation of the Levi form of $|w-f|^{2p}$, which yields a Hermitian matrix criterion on the polynomial hull of the graph; a criterion by peak functions that removes the invertibility hypothesis from a theorem of Preskenis; a division theorem for $f_j=\bar k_jh_j$ with degenerate holomorphic factors $h_j$; and a treatment of the singular set $\{\det(\partial f_i/\partial\bar z_j)=0\}$, which in several variables is not finite. The angle $π/m_j$ in the reduction is shown to be sharp.

title: The optimization landscape of robust high-dimensional mean estimation: stability, moment adaptation, and mirror descent reweighting
abstract: We study efficient robust estimation of a high-dimensional mean under strong contamination when the clean distribution has only $p\ge2$ moments, bounded by $ν_p$. We give a unified proof of stability for every $p\ge2$ with the optimal dimension-free sub-Gaussian rate, linking the reweighting, trimming and truncation techniques of the outlier and heavy-tailed robust literatures through concentration of counting and truncation processes. Building on stability and spectral signatures, we quantify the optimization landscape over sample weights that remove at most a fraction $\varepsilon_{n,k}=k/n$ of the mass, where the trimming parameter $k$ slightly exceeds the number of outliers. An unobserved convex spectral loss has inexact quadratic growth, with curvature $\frac{1-\varepsilon_{n,k}}{\varepsilon_{n,k}}$, relative to a mean-induced Bregman divergence, and the observable spectral loss supplies a dimension-free, inexact, relatively weakly star-convex subgradient oracle for it. This yields a Lyapunov analysis of mirror descent reweighting for $\varepsilon_{n,k}<\frac13$ that covers Hedge, the projected subgradient method, a new mean-induced mirror descent, and a centered multiplicative weights update. Each method uses one top-eigenvector computation per step and attains the optimal sub-Gaussian rate without knowledge of $(p,ν_p)$. Mean-induced mirror descent further achieves faster optimization rates and last-iterate guarantees, at the cost of a more expensive projection step in higher dimensions.

title: Sharp asymptotics and stability for a two-power affine Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality
abstract: We study the affine Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality under the constraint $\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}(f^{q-\varepsilon}+f^{q+\varepsilon}) dx=1$ for $f\ge0$, where $q=\frac{2n}{n+α}$, $n\ge2$, $0<α<n$, and $0<\varepsilon<q-1$. We determine the second-order expansion of its sharp constant and the scale selected by all normalized radial extremals as $\varepsilon\rightarrow0^+$. For sufficiently small fixed $\varepsilon$, we prove stability estimates with power $2$ in $L^{q-\varepsilon}\cap L^{q+\varepsilon}$ for the Euclidean and affine energies. The power $2$ is sharp, and the sharp stability constants admit $O(\varepsilon^2)$ upper bounds as $\varepsilon\rightarrow0^+$. The proof combines identities for the two power integrals with Euclidean spectral estimates, affine compactness and a nonlinear directional expansion. No uniqueness or additional regularity of the radial extremals is assumed.

title: A Master Identity for Forsyth-Glaisher-Type Series for $1/π$
abstract: We derive a novel three-parameter master identity for Forsyth-Glaisher-type series for $1/π$. By unifying disparate results from the literature into a single overarching framework, we demonstrate that Glaisher's original series and numerous known variations emerge naturally as special cases through systematic choices of the parameters. This master identity simplifies the derivation of existing formulas, provides a mechanism for generating an infinite number of new series for $1/π$, and is further utilized to derive associated series involving harmonic and odd harmonic numbers.

title: Geometric Combinatorics of Polynomials with Rotationally Symmetric Roots
abstract: In a recent paper by Dougherty and McCammond, the authors introduced a piecewise Euclidean cell structure for the space of monic centered polynomials. This was achieved by studying the relationship between the polynomials and their critical values, using the Lyashko-Looijenga (LL) map, as well as the noncrossing combinatorics of the polynomials. In this paper, we extend their results to the space of polynomials with rotationally symmetric roots by studying an appropriate generalisation of the LL map, which relates the polynomials and their reduced critical values. The combinatorics of the polynomials are noncrossing partitions of type $B_d$. This give us a piecewise Euclidean cell structure built using the order complex of the noncrossing partition of type $B_d$. Along the way, we also give a compactification of this space of polynomials.

title: A family of alternating projection examples whose Cesàro means fail to converge strongly
abstract:
In 1965, Bregman proved that the sequence of iterates of the method of alternating projections applied to two closed convex sets with nonempty intersection in a Hilbert space converges weakly to a point in the intersection. The question whether this convergence may actually fail to be strong was settled in a seminal paper by Hundal in 2004.
