He provided a counterexample featuring a halfspace and a closed convex cone generated by a certain curve. While largely elementary, the details of Hundal's construction and analysis are quite involved.
  We revisit this seminal example and present a family of such examples that allows for simpler proofs. Our generating curve combines unit vectors with Gaussian inner products and a height determined by a scalar function. The orbits converge weakly --- but not strongly --- to the origin, while their norms have a positive limit for which we give explicit lower bounds. We also prove that the associated Cesàro means behave likewise; in fact, this is generalized to alternating proximal mappings whose composition has a fixed point. Finally, these orbits allow interpretations in the context of projected-gradient, proximal-point, and gradient-descent algorithms.

title: Permutation codes via spectral graph theory
abstract: We use the Eigenvalue Method to obtain upper spectral bounds on the size of permutation codes in the Hamming, Ulam, Cayley and Kendall metrics. For the Kendall metric, we improve the double-ball upper bound of Buzaglo and Etzion [IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 2015] at minimum distance four and lengths seven and eight. For the Cayley metric, we improve the sphere packing bound, and determine when these spectral improvements occur. We derive theoretical spectral criteria for improvements from the ratio-type bounds of low degree, and show that the quadratic ratio-type bound for the Kendall metric always equals sphere packing. Furthermore, we prove sharp spectral bounds and recover known optimal code sizes for the Hamming and Ulam metrics.

title: Encoding rational $Δ$-triples on elliptic curves
abstract: A $Δ$-triple for a natural number $n$ is a triple $(x,y,z)$ of divisors of $n$ with $1<x<y\leq z<\sqrt n$ and $n/x-x=(n/y-y)+(n/z-z)$. The numbers that admit such a triple are those with the $Δ$ property, which governs the existence of certain $n$-simple triangles in factor graphs of split graphs. We allow the three components to be rational numbers, and show that, once the quotient $z/y=a/b$ is fixed, the rational $Δ$-triples for $n$ are exactly the rational points of the elliptic curve $Y^2=n\,ab\,w(w+ab)\bigl(w+(a+b)^2\bigr)$ lying over the interval $-b(a+b)<w<-ab$. Since a rational $Δ$-triple for $n$ amounts to $Δ$-triples for infinitely many of the numbers $κ^2n$, the chord--tangent construction becomes a way of producing new $Δ$-triples from old ones. For perfect squares, the curve always carries a rational point coming from a degenerate triple. This point has order $4$ if $a=b$, and infinite order if $a>b$. As a consequence, for every quotient $a/b>1$ there are infinitely many pairwise non-proportional $Δ$-triples of perfect squares with $z/y=a/b$, in contrast with the fact that perfect squares have no $Δ$-triple with $y=z$. For arbitrary $n$, there are infinitely many rational $Δ$-triples for $n$ with a given quotient if and only if the corresponding curve has positive rank.

title: On Koebe theorem for Sobolev mappings on Riemannian surfaces
abstract: We consider mappings between domains of two Riemannian surfaces. The main subject of the investigation are families of homeomorphisms with moduli inequalities. For such families, we obtain the uniform openness (uniform lightness). As a consequence, we obtain similar results for homeomorphisms of Sobolev classes with finite distortion whenever its maximal dilatations have a majorant integrable on almost all concentric circles. In particular, we obtain the Koebe-type theorem for both direct and inverse Sobolev mappings.

title: Compactness-uniqueness method for null controllability
abstract: We develop the compactness--uniqueness method for the null controllability of abstract linear control systems on Banach spaces. Our first main result characterizes the null controllable states for systems that are null controllable up to finite dimensional spaces, and shows that null controllability is then equivalent to the Fattorini--Hautus test. Our second main result gives a dual counterpart of this assumption, an observability inequality with a suitable compact remainder. These results unify and extend several known results, such as those on heat equations with nonlocal terms and on the simultaneous controllability of systems. Finally, for a transport equation with nonlocal terms from population dynamics, we characterize the null controllable states after a sharp time, including in the non-reflexive space $L^1$.

title: Sliding 2-handles over 3-handles and the barbell diffeomorphism
abstract: We give three fundamental examples highlighting the relationship between loops of spheres in $\#^k S^2\times S^2$, pseudo-isotopies, and diffeomorphisms of the 4-sphere. First, we describe an explicit pseudo-isotopy and Hatcher-Wagoner family that realizes the barbell diffeomorphism $β$ of the 4-sphere by constructing a finger-Whitney system for the family. From the Hatcher-Wagoner family, we are able to conclude that the example in §7 of ``Pseudo-isotopies of simply connected 4-manifolds'' generates $β$. Next, it is known that the square of $β$ is isotopic to id. We reprove this by building an explicit 2-parameter family of Morse functions that trivializes the Hatcher-Wagoner family for $β^2$. We do this by utilizing exchange points and families of handle slides. In the final example, we show that another Hatcher-Wagoner family, affectionately called the double cross, also generates $β$.

title: A Characterization of Completely Integrally Closed Prüfer $v$-Multiplication Domains
abstract: We generalize a result known for Prüfer domains to show that a PVMD $R$ is completely integrally closed if and only if $\text{Inv}^t(R)$ is an archimedean $\ell$-group. It has been conjectured that a PVMD is completely integrally closed if and only if it is an Archimedean domain. It is known that a completely integrally closed PVMD is an Archimedean domain. We provide an example to illustrate that an Archimedean PVMD need not be completely integrally closed.

title: Modular $n$-queens in higher dimensions
abstract: A chess queen in $d$-dimensions can move any distance in the direction of any edge or diagonal of the $d$-dimensional hypercube. (That is, a queen can move from a position $x$ to $x+cv$ for any $c$ and any nonzero $v\in\{-1,0,1\}^d$.) We prove that one can place $n^{d-1}$ non-attacking queens on the $d$-dimensional modular board $(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^d$ if and only if all prime factors of $n$ exceed $2^d$. The $d=3$ case of this result is a conjecture of van Rees from 1981. Our proof involves both human ideas and substantial AI assistance.

title: Lagrangian cobordisms and morphisms of persistence modules
abstract: We consider a version of Legendrian contact homology filtered by the action of Reeb chords. In this version, a union of two disjoint exact Lagrangian cobordisms with Legendrian boundary conditions gives rise to a morphism between persistence modules. We discuss a certain algebraic invariant of such morphisms and use it to obtain obstructions to Lagrangian isotopies of the cobordisms, as well as applications to symplectic and contact dynamics.

title: Emergent Anyons in a Weakly Interacting Gauged Chern Insulator
abstract: We derive a microscopic relation between the many-body Chern number $C$ of the fermionic ground state and the braiding of fluxes in $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ gauge theory coupled to matter: under a spectral gap condition, dressed flux loops obey $W_2W_1=e^{i\fracπ{2}C}W_1W_2$ on the ground-state sector. We realize $C=1$ by gauging charge parity in a weakly interacting Qi-Wu-Zhang insulator. Reflection positivity and chessboard estimates show that flux defects are massive, which yields a gapped, topologically ordered phase with four locally indistinguishable ground states.

title: A simple proof of the Bourgade-Sodin-Zeitouni theorem on the excess of the sine-$β$ process for non-integer $\sqrt{2/β}>1$
abstract: We give an alternative proof of the Bourgade-Sodin-Zeitouni theorem on the excess of the sine-$β$ process for the Paley-Wiener space when $\sqrt{2/β}\in (1,+\infty)$ is not an integer. Let $k(β)=\lfloor\sqrt{2/β}\rfloor$. For almost every configuration, removing any $k(β)$ points leaves a minimal uniqueness set for the Paley-Wiener space. The same conclusion holds for each Bernstein space $\mathcal{B}^p$ of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$-integrable functions with $m(β)<p<\infty$, where $m(β)=β(k(β)+1)-\sqrt{β^2(k(β)+1)^2-2β}$.

title: Two-sample Behrens-Fisher problems for high-dimensional data: noncentral normal-reference inference
abstract: We study noncentral normal-reference inference for high-dimensional two-sample Behrens-Fisher problems. Within the Gaussian reference, a shifted null law is accurate if and only if covariance-weighted signal energy is negligible relative to the trace of the squared covariance. We establish the sharp uniform fourth-root error order over unrestricted spectra and a linear bound under spectral spread. A separate spectral-range criterion determines when signal magnitude alone suffices. An augmented spherical reference gives finite-sample calibration for Gaussian samples and asymptotically recovers Gaussian-reference local power under projection fourth-moment bounds and control of diagonal fluctuations, without a dimension-to-sample-size restriction. For unknown Gaussian covariance, explicit trace and hollow-Gram confidence bounds turn the linear approximation bound into a simultaneous, computable certificate over local effect ranges. Eigenspace signal energies describe directional power, while a two-point argument limits estimation of unknown local power. Simulations with 10,000 evaluation replications per configuration examine unequal and noncommuting covariances, severe sample imbalance, non-Gaussian observations and the informativeness of the certificate.

title: Random Chowla and Goldbach Conjectures
abstract:
We prove that for a Rademacher random multiplicative function $(f(n))_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ and any non-linear polynomial $P\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ admitting a positive constant $κ_P$ such that \[\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty} \frac{\#\{n\in\left[N\right]:P(n)\text{ is square-free}\}}{N} =κ_P,\] we have \[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{κ_PN}}\sum_{n\leqslant N}f(P(n)) \xrightarrow[]{d}\mathcal{N}(0,1), \] as $N\rightarrow\infty $, where convergence is in distribution to a standard Gaussian. Using a direct combinatorial argument, we establish paucity estimates for non-trivial square products of square-free polynomial values at every fixed moment order. These estimates yield the Gaussian limit by the method of moments.
  We also study partial sums of the form $\sum_{n<N} F(f(n),f(N-n))$ for a suitable class of bivariate functions $F$ when $f$ is a Steinhaus random multiplicative function, and prove analogous results in special cases in the Rademacher setting. These results can be viewed as random analogues of the Goldbach-type problems considered by Mangerel.

title: Another Multivector Inverse Algorithm
abstract:
A numerical algorithm is described for computing the inverse of a non-singular multivector across dimensions. The method wraps a reversion-like product around a Faddeev--LeVerrier--Souriau (FLS) polynomial core. While FLS provides dimensional extensibility, the wrapper reduces the polynomial order of the FLS method, and introduces a sparse multivector which can be further exploited. The construction and essential properties of the initial involution are explained.
  For dimensions 4--7, the optimized inverse requires fewer real multiplications than a same-dimension multivector product. Dimensions 8--11 follow easily on common hardware with similar efficiency. For dimensions 12--15, higher-precision arithmetic demonstrates the generality of the algorithm when the arithmetic can support it. Performance on common hardware is reported. Directions are included for obtaining a Python package with examples for numerical computation in Clifford algebra, supporting arbitrary signatures including degenerate cases.

title: Involutive Duality of Lie Operators in the Extended Alpha Group
abstract: This work investigates the involutive, adjoint, and spectral structures arising in the extended Alpha Group. Starting from the four-dimensional Alpha Group transformation matrix, whose angular depen- dence is governed by coupled tan θ and cot θ modes, an iterative commutator procedure generates a sixteen-dimensional real Lie algebra. Within this algebra, the operators B5 and B6 are identified as structurally distinguished elements and analyzed through their adjoint actions. The operator B6 is veri- fied to be involutive and induces an 8 + 8 decomposition of the Lie algebra, while the adjoint action of B5 defines an eight-dimensional invariant mixed sector through a polynomial kernel. The restricted adjoint operators preserve this sector, and their coupled action generates an idempotent operator Q, satisfying Q2 = Q, revealing an invariant projective structure. The spectral analysis further identifies characteristic- polynomial factorizations associated with B5 , B6 , and their compositions, including golden-ratio relations among distinct generators of the extended algebra. These results establish structural connections between the original modal representation, Lie-algebraic involution, adjoint dynamics, projective organization, and the spectral structure of the extended Alpha Group.

title: Fast Computation of the Kippenhahn Hypersurface of a Joint Numerical Range
abstract: We present a fast modular interpolation method for computing the hypersurface components of algebraic Kippenhahn varieties over number fields. Starting from Hermitian matrices, we factor their determinantal polynomial and use Katz's test to identify the factors whose duals are hypersurfaces. For each such factor, we sample smooth points over finite fields and compute their tangent hyperplanes. These give points on the dual hypersurface, from which we interpolate its defining equation. For number-field coefficients, we use primes at which the defining polynomial of the field factors completely into distinct linear factors. Interpolation across all its roots recovers the residues of the coefficients in a fixed number-field basis. Chinese remaindering and rational reconstruction then recover an equation over the original number field from the computations at different primes. An exact polynomial divisibility test and an irreducibility check certify each reconstructed equation. Four determinantal quartics arising from matrix examples in the literature yield certified dual surfaces of degrees $12$, $18$, $24$ and $34$. We give implementations in Magma and Singular and compare their running times with Gröbner basis elimination.

title: On the Classification of Nilpotent Lie Superalgebras over Fields of Characteristic 2
abstract: The salient result of this paper is the complete classification of all nilpotent Lie superalgebras in dimensions up to four over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2. Our method adapts the Skjelbred-Sund method to show that every n-dimensional nilpotent Lie superalgebra arises as a one-dimensional central extension of an (n-1)-dimensional one, and determines precisely when two such extensions yield isomorphic superalgebras. Carrying out this construction for dimensions up to 4, we obtain a finite, non-redundant list of pairwise non-isomorphic examples.

title: Making Poisson σ again - an étude on groupoidal gauging, anomalies, gerbes, and defects
abstract: The Poisson $σ$-model (PSM) over a closed worldsheet $Σ$ is reinterpreted as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle $P_0 = Σ\times G \to Σ$ with the symplectic structure groupoid $(G,ω)$ integrating the Poisson target $(M,Π)$, and that of sections of the shadow bundle $F_0 = Σ\times M \to Σ$ - as defined in 2503.09886 [math.DG]. The flat directions of the PSM are explained as linearisations of automorphisms of $P_0$, modelled on maps from $Σ$ into the group of lagrangean bisections of $G$, which induce Poisson automorphisms of $(M,Π)$. The gauge anomaly of the ensuing field theory is derived and demonstrated to vanish for prequantisable $ω$. A general anomaly-cancellation mechanism is proposed, which couples the bare model - rewritten as the holonomy of a connection-dependent trivial gerbe on $F_0$ - to a background gerbe over $M$ endowed with a $G$-equivariant structure. The coupling takes the form of the tensor product of the two gerbes and the extended PSM is defined as the holonomy of the product gerbe. An essential generalisation of the theory is then proposed - to shadows $F$ of principaloid bundles $P$ of arbitrary topology, in keeping with the interpretation of the gauging as descent to the orbistack $M//G$. The generalisation uses local product gerbes depending on local connections over trivialisations of $F$. The $G$-equivariant structure is proven to ensure a 2-stacky descent of the local gerbes to a global one over $F$. Its holonomy is taken as the definition of the generalised PSM. A cohomological discussion of obstructions against the descent is provided. Finally, a reformulation of the generalised PSM as a field theory with a topological gauge-symmetry defect is given, in which the $G$-equivariant structure is employed - alongside the transition cocycle of $P$ - as the datum of the defect.

title: On open weakly 2-semiconvex sets with nonempty 2-nonsemiconvexity-point sets in three-dimensional Euclidean space
abstract: We study general topological properties of open weakly $2$-semiconvex sets in real three-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$. An open set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is called weakly $2$-semiconvex if through every boundary point of the set there passes a closed half-plane that does not intersect the set. The largest subset of the complement of a given set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ such that every closed half-plane intersecting this subset also intersects the given set is called the $2$-nonsemiconvexity-point set corresponding to the given one. We prove that the nonempty $2$-nonsemiconvexity-point set corresponding to an open weakly $2$-semiconvex set is open and weakly $2$-semiconvex. We also construct a weakly $2$-semiconvex domain whose $2$-nonsemiconvexity-point set is an unbounded domain that can be either convex or nonconvex.

title: Symplectic capacities of 4-dimensional monotone toric domains
abstract: We compute the cylindrical contact homology chain complex associated with a monotone toric domain in $\mathbb{R}^4$. The chain complexes allow us to compute the cylindrical contact homology capacities associated with monotone toric domains with one or two inflection points. These capacities are conjecturally equal to the Gutt-Hutchings capacities defined using $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. Using our results, we find embedding obstructions between toric domains.

title: Foliations, free cores, and Terao's conjecture for seventeen lines
abstract: We prove that freeness is determined by the intersection lattice for arrangements of seventeen lines in the complex projective plane. The proof reduces a possible counterexample to smaller arrangements whose realisation spaces can be computed. A minimal logarithmic derivation defines a foliation; its inflection divisor and a local singularity count imply that the non-free member of a counterexample is nearly free with exponents $(7,10)$. Deleting four lines then produces a thirteen-line arrangement whose second Chern class is controlled by a combinatorial deficit. When the deficit is four, the remaining arrangement is free with exponents $(6,6)$. An exact covering argument places the necessary thirteen-line cores in four finite classes, containing $3{,}829{,}691$ lattices. We compute their realisation spaces and reconstruct all relevant seventeen-line extensions, including specialisations of positive-dimensional families. Among the candidate lattices, exactly sixteen admit a non-free realisation; they are rigid and have no free realisation. Together with the known cases, this establishes Terao's conjecture for central arrangements of at most seventeen planes in $\mathbb{C}^3$.

title: The inscribed $4$-polytope of maximal volume with ten vertices
abstract: We prove that a $4$-polytope with ten vertices inscribed in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $\frac{25}{384}(10 + 2\sqrt{5})$, and that, up to orthogonal transformations, equality holds only for the convex hull of two regular pentagons inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ in orthogonal $2$-planes through the origin. As for six to nine vertices, the optimum is thus the convex hull of two regular polygons in orthogonal planes. On the combinatorial type of the pair, whose boundary complex is the join of two $5$-cycles, the sharp bound follows from our work on nine vertices. Since an optimal polytope is simplicial, by a result of Horváth and Lángi, it remains to exclude the other $162003$ simplicial types. We do this by sum-of-squares certificates checked in exact arithmetic, extended by nonnegative multiples of facet polynomials, which are positive on every positively oriented realisation of

title: A convergent Lagrangian scheme for the Navier Stokes equations on the normed Wasserstein space
abstract: We extend the differential structure on Wasserstein spaces of Schichl (arXiv:2508.15140) to the normed Wasserstein space $\mathbb{W}_1$ of finite signed measures, the natural setting for measure differential equations with source terms. We generalize the averaged flow dispersion and expectational flow operators to $\mathbb{W}_1$ and show that along divergence--free tangent vectors they act by measure--preserving flows, and further define source operators. As an application, we construct a purely Lagrangian splitting scheme for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^N$, inspired by the Averaged Flow Approximation Series (AFAS) in \cite{Schichl2025}. We recover, with explicit constants, the classical lifespan bound, a blow--up rate and the inviscid limit with rate $O(η^2)$, and a linearised scheme yields $L^{\infty}$, Hölder, $L^1$ and moment estimates for classical solutions.

title: The exact region of the Average Rectangular Volume and Spearman's rho, with an application to arachnitude
abstract: The average rectangular volume ($\ARV$) of a bivariate aggregation function is the average of its volumes over all axis-parallel rectangles of the unit square; for a copula, it is the expected copula volume of the rectangle spanned by two independent uniform points. We determine the exact region of the pairs $(\ARV(C),ρ(C))$, where $C$ ranges over all bivariate copulas and $ρ$ is Spearman's rho. The region is compact, convex and symmetric, and its upper boundary consists of three analytically parametrized arcs. A previously proposed family of shuffles of Min generates one arc, but only on part of its range; the other two arcs are generated by singular copulas whose supports contain hyperbolic branches. The boundary is continuously differentiable away from its left endpoint $\ARV=\frac{11}{120}$, where it has a vertical tangent. The proof uses a folding transformation and explicit Kantorovich potentials for a family of optimal transport problems. Finally, we show that the arachnitude, a rank correlation used in actuarial practice, is an affine transformation of $\ARV$, so that the result also describes the joint region of Spearman's rho and arachnitude.

title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
abstract: Guérin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory, strongly biased starts are unimodal, and the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval. Outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$, whose uniqueness follows from a positive-weight integral for the central curvature of the fair-start density. We control sign changes in the finite walk's first and second differences, including those created at the boundary, and pass them to the limit. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one.

title: Quivers with potential for quantum affine superalgebras
abstract: We construct a surjective algebra homomorphism from the $K$-theoretic Hall algebras of certain quivers with potential to the (half) quantum affine and toroidal orthosymplectic superalgebras.

title: Thin Edges in Braces
abstract: A connected graph with at least two vertices is matching covered if each of its edges is contained in a perfect matching. A bipartite matching covered graph is a brace if no nontrivial cut meets every perfect matching in exactly one edge.An edge $e$ of a brace $G$ is thin if $G-e$ is matching covered and its retract is a brace. Every brace can be reduced to $K_2$ or $C_4$ by successively deleting thin edges and taking retracts. Indeed, Carvalho, Lucchesi and Murty proved that every brace of order at least six has at least two thin edges. They conjectured that there exists a positive constant $c$ such that every brace of order $n\ge6$ has at least $cn$ thin edges. In this paper, we prove that every simple brace of order $n\ge6$ has at least $\left\lceil\frac{n+2}{6}\right\rceil$ thin edges and that every brace of order $n$, withparallel edges allowed, has at least $\frac{n}{13}$ thin edges. This proves the conjecture. Moreover, we prove that every cubic brace of order $n$ has at least $\left\lceil\frac{n+1}{5}\right\rceil$ thin edges for $n\ge6$ and that the coefficient $\frac15$ is best possible.

title: Understanding the Asymptotic Transience of Q-Learning via Distributional Expansion
abstract: Q-learning has been empirically observed to exhibit substantial transient error. This transient remains uncaptured by the leading Gaussian limit because the central-limit normalization removes the smaller-scale displacement generated by the initial nonlinear evolution. On the other hand, worst-case finite-sample guarantees, while accounting for transient effects, can obscure the mechanisms responsible for the error on a particular problem instance. We develop a finer asymptotic analysis that gives an asymptotically exact characterization of this transient for a fixed instance. Specifically, for synchronous Q-learning in finite discounted Markov decision processes, we separate the last-iterate error into an optimal-policy temporal-difference (TD) component and a nonnegative displacement caused by maximization. The centered TD component has Gaussian fluctuations at scale $n^{-1/2}$, whereas the maximization transient is of order $n^{-1}$ and converges almost surely, after rescaling by $n$, to a random limit. This limit represents the propagated effect of maximization errors generated before the greedy policy stabilizes. We combine this characterization with an Edgeworth expansion of the TD component to identify the corrections to its Gaussian approximation, separating the effects of initialization, non-Gaussian TD fluctuations, and maximization. The results reveal how transient errors arise for individual Q-learning instances and how their effects persist below the central-limit scale.

title: Sharp partition function bound for the attractive logarithmic gas
abstract: For the attractive logarithmic potential, we prove that the partition function is bounded uniformly in the number of particles on every compact inverse-temperature interval $[0,\be_0]$ with $\be_0<B$, where $B\in(0,2\d]$ is the sharp constant in the logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. The proof separates a smooth bulk, which inherits the entropy inequality, from a short-range singular interaction. The singular contribution is controlled on the event that each box of a fixed grid contains few particles. The complementary overcrowding event has exponentially small probability, which compensates a crude linear-in-$N$ bound on the log partition function. The resulting estimate supplies the partition bound that can be used recycled in a few different results. A separate Lean formalization verifies the conditional partition-bound theorem under the log-HLS assumption.

title: Message-Passing-Based Bayesian Joint Channel Estimation and Data Detection for Pilot-Guard-Free AFDM
abstract: Existing channel estimation methods for affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) over doubly dispersive channels commonly isolate pilots and data with pilot guard symbols, resulting in substantial transmission overhead, while fractional Doppler introduces off-grid mismatch and complicates accurate channel estimation. This paper develops a pilot-guard-free AFDM transmission and reception scheme with a Bayesian receiver for joint channel estimation and data symbol detection. Uniformly interleaved pilots are embedded among data symbols without dedicated guard symbols, and the resulting pilot-data coupling is explicitly incorporated into the joint inference problem rather than suppressed through guard-based isolation.

title: Rational isogenies of of rank-two Drinfeld modules
abstract: We determine the $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-rational points on the Drinfeld modular curves $X_{0}(\mathfrak{n})$ of arbitrary level, obtaining a complete classification of rational cyclic isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules over $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$. As consequences, we prove Schweizer's conjecture on rational torsion, establish optimal uniform bounds on the number of isomorphism classes in an $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-isogeny class of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules and determine the geometric automorphism groups of $X_{0}(\mathfrak{p})$ for primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree at least three.

title: Entropy-degree rigidity for non-collapsed $RCD$ spaces
abstract: We prove the entropy-degree theorem for continuous maps from a closed orientable non-collapsed $RCD(K,N)$ space $X$ to a closed negatively curved locally symmetric $N$-manifold $Y$, with $N \geq 3$. In the equality case, under a fundamental group index condition, we show the space is isometric to a smooth locally symmetric Riemannian manifold, and the map is homotopic to a Riemannian covering.

title: Equilateral simplices over general fields
abstract: A classical theorem of Schoenberg (1937) characterizes the dimensions $d$ for which $\mathbb{Q}^d$ contains the vertex set of a regular simplex with $d+1$ vertices. We generalize Schoenberg's result to all fields of characteristic not equal to $2$, using elementary Witt theory and Lagrange's four-square theorem. Our generalization also sharpens Schoenberg's theorem and complements more recent work of Lorenz and Zimmermann (2026) by characterizing the admissible edge lengths. In the case of finite characteristic, equilateral simplices with $d+2$ vertices can sometimes exist (F.~Radó 1986), and we characterize this situation as well, again for all fields of characteristic not equal to $2$. We also briefly consider the edge lengths of equilateral simplices of $d$ vertices.

title: Two-Stage Mixed-Integer Quadratic Programming in Polynomial Time
abstract: Lenstra showed that mixed-integer linear programming can be solved in polynomial time when the number of integer variables is fixed and the number of continuous variables is arbitrary. Mixed-integer quadratic programming (MIQP) can be solved in polynomial time when the total number of variables is fixed. However, since MIQP is NP-hard already without integer variables, the analog of Lenstra's result fails unless P = NP. Hence, polynomial-time algorithms for MIQP with an arbitrary number of continuous variables must exploit additional structure. We study MIQPs with two-stage structure, which underlies Benders decomposition and two-stage stochastic programming. A few linking variables, including all integer variables, are coupled with many blocks of continuous variables that interact only through them, both in the constraints and in the objective. We give a polynomial-time algorithm for MIQP with an arbitrary quadratic objective when the number of linking variables and the block size are fixed, while the number of blocks, and hence the number of variables, is arbitrary. The case with no blocks is MIQP in fixed dimension. None of our assumptions can be dropped. Unless P = NP, the number of linking variables and the block size must both be fixed, the blocks cannot interact or contain integer variables, and large blocks cannot be allowed even if their objective is linear. Unless FPT = W[1], the exponent of the running time must depend on both the number of linking variables and the block size.

title: The bounded approximation property in Banach function lattices, interpolation of the essential norm, and applications
abstract: We prove the bounded approximation property for Banach function lattices with order continuous norm on which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator is bounded. This allows us to develop a general framework for the quantitative interpolation of compact operators, understood in terms of the essential norm, encompassing a large class of function spaces including weighted Lebesgue spaces, rearrangement invariant Banach function spaces, and variable exponent Lebesgue spaces. Combined with extrapolation techniques, we show how to transfer compactness (or, more generally, control of the essential norm) from unweighted Lebesgue spaces to the three aforementioned classes of function spaces. Finally, we present several applications in analysis and partial differential equations.

title: On piecewise-regular and quasirational functions
abstract: We fully characterize piecewise-regular functions on nonsingular real algebraic varieties in terms of continuous quasirational functions. We also obtain extension theorem for piecewise-regular functions defined on closed semialgebraic subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n.$

title: Sidorenko inequalities and symmetry-forcing for graph orientations
abstract: We study directed graphs whose homomorphism densities never increase or never decrease when the host edge directions are randomized. We call these properties oriented Sidorenko (OS) and oriented anti-Sidorenko (OAS), respectively. A directed graph is symmetry-forcing if equality between its original and randomized densities forces quasi-random edge directions. We characterize connected OS directed graphs in terms of weakly norming graphs and show that they are symmetry-forcing exactly when their underlying graphs contain a cycle. We also prove that a connected graph is step forcing exactly when it is step Sidorenko and contains a cycle, giving a negative answer to a question of Doležal et al. Both forcing results follow from a characterization of strict convexity: the homomorphism density functional of a graph is strictly convex on nonnegative kernels exactly when the graph is weakly norming and contains a cycle. On the OAS side, we construct an infinite symmetry-forcing family and a nonbipartite example. We also classify OS and OAS orientations of stars, paths, and cycles.

title: The minimum size of the 3-dimensional torus
abstract: We prove a conjecture of Kühnel, Lassmann, and Lutz, first asked in 1984, that the minimal number of vertices in a triangulation of the $3$-dimensional torus is $15$.

title: The maximum product of nontrivial cross $t$-intersecting families
abstract:
Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be nonempty families of $k$-subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that $|A\cap B|\ge t$ for all $A\in\mathcal A$ and $B\in\mathcal B$, and suppose that each family has fewer than $t$ common elements. For $k\ge t+2\ge4$ and $n\ge(t+1)(k-t+1)$, we prove \[
  |\mathcal A||\mathcal B|\le\max\{h_t(n,k)^2,b_t(n,k)^2\}, \] where \[
  h_t(n,k)=\binom{n-t}{k-t}-\binom{n-k-1}{k-t}+t,\quad
  b_t(n,k)=(t+2)\binom{n-t-2}{k-t-1}+\binom{n-t-2}{k-t-2}. \] The bound is sharp, and we characterize all extremal pairs, whose families have equal sizes but need not coincide. The proof combines clique lifts, exchanges of generating families and a density inequality for cross-intersecting uniform layers. This gives a product version of the Hilton--Milner--Frankl theorem throughout the Erdős--Ko--Rado range. In particular, it answers a question of Wen and Lv on whether a threshold of order $kt$ suffices for the sharp product bound.

title: Quasihyperbolic geodesics in the twice-puntured plane
abstract: We study quasihyperbolic distance and geodesic uniqueness in the plane punctured at 0 and 2. For endpoints on the perpendicular bisector of the punctures and on opposite sides of the real axis, the distance is the smaller of the length of the vertical segment and the least length of a feasible detour. For symmetric endpoints 1 \pm it with t > 0, the geodesic is unique precisely when arsinh t + arctan t < π. At equality there are exactly three geodesic images, and above the threshold there are exactly two. For arbitrary endpoints, we derive variational formulas for the distance in terms of admissible logarithmic spirals and their contacts with the bisector. The minimizing candidates in these formulas give all geodesic images and yield a length-comparison criterion for uniqueness.

title: Stability of analytic monodromic singularities without curves of zero angular speed
abstract: The aim of this work is to give conditions on the parameters of a family of analytic planar vector fields with a fixed Newton diagram and a monodromic singularity in order to guarantee that the coefficient (generalized first Lyapunov constant) of the linear part of the Poincaré map has an explicit formula. We revisit using this formalism some monodromic examples appearing in the literature and also we apply the results to other families were, as far as we know, the stability problem was open.

title: Zero-Hopf Networks
abstract: A zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur for dynamical systems that have a singularity where the linear part has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. We call a zero-Hopf network a regular network whose adjacency matrix has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of complex eigenvalues with zero real part. In this work, we prove that there is an infinite number of zero-Hopf networks for which the zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur as a generic codimension-one phenomenon for the class of the network admissible smooth vector fields. Our results are achieved using the network adjacency matrices and the associated eigenvector structures. General results are presented for four-cell zero-Hopf networks concerning the network set of synchrony spaces. As a case study, we present a classification of all connected zero-Hopf 4-cell regular networks of valency two showing that, up to permutation of the cells, there are 9 distinct such networks. Moreover, the normal forms of these networks are computed using the method of Rink and Sanders (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 367 (2015) 3509--3548) for coupled cell networks. It is remarked that these normal forms are less simplified as the input symmetry of the network admissible smooth vector fields restricts the admissible normal form transformations. Nevertheless, the networks share a common coupling function normal form.

title: Prescribed inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature flow on finite trees
abstract: We characterize the image of the inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature map on finite edge-weighted trees. We prove that the prescribed curvature flow converges if and only if the target curvature is attainable, and that the convergence is exponential whenever it occurs. The key ingredient in the proof is a formulation of the prescribed curvature flow as the gradient flow of a convex functional.

title: Liouville type results for super-$p$-biharmonic immersions and $p$-biharmonic submanifolds
abstract:
We introduce a weak notion of $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion into Euclidean space, formulated through a divergence inequality for the mean curvature vector. This class naturally extends the $\varepsilon$-superbiharmonic immersions previously introduced by the third author while remaining well-defined for all $p>1$, including the singular range $1<p<2$. We prove a Liouville-type rigidity theorem showing that every proper $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion is minimal provided
  \[
  \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac1{r^{2}} \int_{f^{-1}(B_r)} |\vec{H}| ^{q}\,dμ=0
  \]
  for some $q>p-\varepsilon$. This extends the corresponding superbiharmonic rigidity theorem to the $p$-biharmonic setting under a natural growth hypothesis.
  We also establish a minimality theorem for complete $p$-biharmonic immersions into Riemannian manifolds of non-positive sectional curvature under a polynomial growth assumption on the mean curvature. More precisely, if
  \[
  \int_{B_r(x_0)} | \vec{H} | ^{\,q}\,dμ= O(r^d)
  \]
  for some $q\ge0$ and $d>0$, then the immersion is minimal. For $q=0$ this recovers the polynomial volume-growth theorem of Cao--Luo \cite{CL16}, while for $q>0$ it provides a polynomial-growth analogue of Han's $L^q$-integrability rigidity theorem \cite{H15}.

title: On pseudospectra of the relativistic rotated harmonic oscillator
abstract: We establish an upper bound to the norm of the resolvent of a relativistic version of the non-self-adjoint operator obtained by a dilation analytic transformation of the quantum harmonic oscillator. The estimate implies a decay for large complex energies along rays with angles larger than that of the dilation. In this way we positively answer a question left open in [Proceedings of the Royal Society A 2025].

title: Robust High-Order BUG Integrators without Basis Augmentation
abstract: We develop robust high-order basis-update and Galerkin (BUG) integrators for dynamical low-rank approximation without basis augmentation or rank truncation. The basis and core updates use the same approximate increment. We establish a two-sided relaxed-exactness estimate that controls the error in the low-rank approximation by the increment error. Under the stated assumptions on the vector field and its normal component, sufficiently accurate increments yield local and global error bounds whose constants and step-size restrictions are independent of small singular values. Using explicit Runge--Kutta increments, we obtain robust orders two, three, and four for the explicit midpoint method, Heun's third-order method, and Merson's fourth-order method, respectively. Every internal stage and final approximation has rank at most the prescribed rank $r$. We also prove that these orders are retained under arbitrary basis augmentation followed by best rank-$r$ SVD truncation at the internal stages and the endpoint, without a separate assumption on the truncation error. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence orders and show comparable performance with and without augmentation.

title: On Star Monotone Operators: Theory and Applications
abstract: Introduced by Solodov and Svaiter \cite{SS}, star monotone operators have repeatedly appeared as a sufficient condition ensuring global convergence of first-order algorithms, without requiring full monotonicity. Yet, despite this recurring role, a systematic study of the class itself has been missing from the literature. This paper fills that gap with the first comprehensive treatment of star monotone operators, a class that strictly encompasses monotone and pseudomonotone operators with nonempty zero sets, together with operators that are strongly quasimonotone along rays and satisfy a radial nondegeneracy condition. We develop basic calculus rules, existence and uniqueness results for zeros, global metric subregularity, and precise structural relationships with classical monotonicity notions. We further demonstrate the versatility of star monotonicity through a Clarke subdifferential characterization of nonsmooth star quasiconvexity, applications to Minty and Stampacchia variational inequalities, linear convergence guarantees for subgradient-type methods, and separable operators related to the Debreu--Koopmans problem.

title: Subgradient and Stochastic Finite-Difference Methods for Constrained Strongly Quasiconvex Optimization
abstract: We propose a projected subgradient method for solving quasiconvex minimization problems. By employing the Clarke subdifferential, we prove that the sequence generated by the proposed algorithm converges to a solution of the minimization problem when the objective function is locally Lipschitz continuous and strongly quasiconvex in the sense of Polyak, under the same assumptions required for convex functions with the convex subdifferential. Moreover, we derive explicit convergence rate estimates for both the iterates and objective function values. In particular, compared with the corresponding results for nonsmooth, locally Lipschitz, strongly convex optimization, our analysis replaces strong convexity with strong quasiconvexity while preserving the order of the convergence rate, thereby extending the guarantees to a class of possibly nonconvex objective functions. In addition, we investigate a stochastic finite-difference scheme for minimizing a strongly quasiconvex function subject to inequality constraints defined by strongly quasiconvex functions, and establish a convergence rate of order $O(k^{-1/4})$, consistent with known complexity bounds for stochastic zeroth-order methods.

title: Domination in token graphs of graphs with domination number two
abstract: The $k$-token graph $F_k(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the graph whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of $V(G)$, with two $k$-subsets adjacent if and only if their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. In this paper we study the domination number of $F_k(G)$ for graphs $G$ whose domination number $γ(G)$ is at least two, with a primary focus on the case $γ(G)=2$. For $k=2$, we give an upper bound for $γ(F_2(G))$ in terms of a dominating pair of $G$, and show that this bound is sharp for every double star $S_{a,b}$ with $2\le a\le b$; moreover, we determine the exact value for every double star, namely $γ(F_2(S_{a,b}))=2a+b-1$ for $1\le a\le b$. We also prove that $γ(F_2(G))\ge\lceil n/2\rceil$ for every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $γ(G)\geq2$, with equality for the graphs with the maximum number of edges among those with $γ(G)\geq2$. Then, we focus on complete bipartite graphs; we give upper bounds for $γ(F_2(K_{r,t}))$ that match the exact values independently established in recent work, together with a short proof that $γ(F_2(K_{2,n-2}))=n-2$. For $k\ge3$ we show that $γ(F_k(K_{2,n-2}))$ equals, up to lower-order terms, the Turán number $T(n-2,k,k-1)$, and we determine $γ(F_3(K_{2,n-2}))$ exactly, obtaining $T(n-2,3,2) +n-4=n^2/4+O(n)$; for $k=4$, determining the leading constant is related to the still-open Turán conjecture for 3-uniform hypergraphs. Finally, for $n\geq 12$ even, we prove that $γ\left(F_3(K_{n/2,n/2})\right) =\frac{7}{48}n^2+O(n)$.

title: Relative-energy stabilization of an irreversible port-Hamiltonian tubular reactor
abstract: This paper develops a relative-energy control approach for a boundary-controlled irreversible port-Hamiltonian model of a non-isothermal tubular reactor around a spatially nonuniform stationary profile. The starting point is a thermodynamic duality between the entropy-based availability used in earlier reactor control and the relative Hamiltonian induced by the irreversible port-Hamiltonian representation. Under physically interpretable stability conditions---positive heat capacity, positive compressibility and positive compositional susceptibility---the Hamiltonian density is shown to be strictly convex, while the corresponding entropy representation is strictly concave. The resulting relative Hamiltonian decomposes into kinetic, compressive, thermal and mixing contributions and yields an exact relative-energy balance in which irreversible dissipation is separated from profile-dependent terms. This structure leads to a bounded monotone distributed jacket feedback that injects thermal damping without cancelling the nonlinear PDE dynamics. A continuous coercivity condition gives a local a-priori decay estimate for sufficiently regular nonlinear solutions, while a composite energy functional provides an exponential estimate for the linearized closed-loop initial-boundary value problem. Structure-preserving PFEM simulations are used to verify the predicted dissipation mechanisms and constrained profile regulation.

title: Sharp weighted bounds for reverse fractional integral operators
abstract:
In this paper, we prove the one-weight reverse fractional integral operators \[ \|I_s f\|_{L^q(w^q)}\geq C_w\|f\|_{L^p(w^p)} \] holds for all nonnegative measurable functions $f$, with $\frac ns<p<1$ and $\frac1q=\frac1p-\frac sn$, if and only if $w^{p/(1-p)}\in A_{\frac{p(s-n)}{n(1-p)}}$. Furthermore, we show the lower bound \[ C_w\gtrsim_{n,s,p}[w]_{p,q}^{\min\left\{\frac{p(n-s)}{n(1-p)},\frac{p(n-s)}{sp-n}\right\}}, \] and the exponent is sharp.
  We also investigate when the reverse weak-type estimate \[ \|I_s f\|_{L^{\frac{n}{n-s},\infty}(w^{\frac{n}{n-s}})}\geq \frac{n}{s}\,v_n^{(n-s)/n}[w^{\frac{n}{n-s}}]^{(n-s)/n}_{A_1}\|f\|_{L^1(w)} \] holds if and only if $w^{\frac{n}{n-s}}\in A_1$.

title: Polynomial approximations to Calabi--Yau metrics on quartic K3 surfaces and quintic threefolds
abstract: On the Fermat quartic K3 surface and the Fermat quintic threefold, we construct Kähler metrics from explicit rational polynomial potentials and bound their differences from the Ricci-flat metrics in integral tensor norms. For specified compact families of smooth quartic and quintic hypersurfaces near the Fermat hypersurfaces, we give a terminating algorithm that constructs polynomial Kähler metrics with prescribed pointwise bounds on their differences from the Ricci-flat metrics and on their Ricci forms. The resulting metrics converge to the Ricci-flat metrics in every $C^r$ norm, uniformly in the parameter.

title: Nonabelian Hodge theory in positive characteristic for rank-2 vector bundles over curves
abstract: We describe the Nonabelian Hodge Theory correspondence in positive characteristic between nilpotent Higgs bundles and flat bundles with nilpotent p-curvature, as constructed in the seminal paper by Ogus-Vologodsky, in the special case of rank-2 vector bundles over a smooth projective curve. In this set-up we can rephrase this correspondence as a shift of the extension class of a rank-2 vector bundle by a cohomology class encoding a W_2-lift of the curve. As an application, we obtain that a general rank-2 vector bundle of degree 0 admits a connection with non-zero nilpotent p-curvature.

title: Path complexes with concatenation and their relation to digraphs
abstract: The path homology theory is based on the notion of path complex and is a part of GLMY-theory created and developed by Grigor'yan, Lin, Muranov, and Yau in a cycle of papers in 2012-2014. In this paper we define a path complex with concatenation ($PC$-complex) which is a particular case of a path complex. We define a natural topology on a set of vertices of any $PC$-complex, and describe properties of this topology and its relation to the discrete topology of Alexandroff. We prove the existence of functorial relations between some categories of $PC$-complexes and digraphs. These relations allow to transfer covering, homotopy and various versions of homology theory from digraph theory to $PC$-complexes.

title: Small classes have linear neighbourhood complexity
abstract: A hereditary graph class is small if it contains at most $n!c^n$ labelled graphs on $n$ vertices for some constant $c$. Small classes include proper minor-closed classes and classes of bounded twin-width. We prove that every small class has linear neighbourhood complexity, that is, in every graph in the class, vertex neighbourhoods intersect any $k$-vertex set in only $O(k)$ distinct ways. This resolves a conjecture of Bonnet, Duron, and the first two authors (ITCS 2025) and makes the algorithmic, structural, and representation consequences of linear neighbourhood complexity available for every small class. In particular, every small class admits an adjacency labelling scheme with $O(\log^2 n)$-bit labels, improving the previous $O(\log^3 n)$ bound.

title: Multicontinuum Poroelasticity Model. Analysis and Computation
abstract: In this work, we develop and analyze a macroscopic multicontinuum model for Biot poroelasticity. The full macroscopic multicontinuum system is derived by projecting the microscopic weak formulation onto continuum-dependent Galerkin spaces enriched with first-order multiscale corrections. This construction retains generalized pressure storage and coupling terms, with effective coefficients inherited from the microscopic bilinear forms. Under suitable coefficient assumptions, we establish well-posedness and energy stability of the macroscopic multicontinuum model. A fully discrete scheme combining the Galerkin finite element method in space with the backward Euler method in time is then developed. Its well-posedness and stability are proved, and a priori error estimates are derived using appropriate projection operators and energy arguments. Finally, numerical experiments for periodic and non-periodic high-contrast media demonstrate the accuracy of the multicontinuum model with respect to the averaged fine-scale solution.

title: A symmetry on Young tableaux with walls and holes
abstract: The Pons--Batle conjecture on tree-child networks was regarded as a specific and challenging problem in the phylogenetics community. We found an unexpected weighted symmetry for a class of three-row Young tableaux with walls and holes. This weighted symmetry implies the Fuchs--Yu identity, which together with the bijection of Chang, Fuchs, Liu, Wallner, and Yu leads to a simple proof of the Pons--Batle conjecture. We construct an involutive proof of this symmetry via introducing decorated binary networks as an intermediate structure. We also provide an elementary proof of this weighted symmetry using recurrence relations.

title: On shared responsibility, fish, and the strong law of large numbers
abstract: We give a new, short, and intuitive proof of the strong law of large numbers for i.i.d. random variables.

title: Sharp Liouville theorems for the Hardy-Hénon p-Laplace equation and classification of positive solutions for the critical Hardy p-Laplace equation
abstract: We prove subcritical nonexistence for $-Δ_pu=|x|^au^q$ in $R^N$, with $1<p<N$ and $a>-p$, in the positive locally bounded weak class. Continuous Steiner symmetrization of a nonlinear auxiliary potential yields a directional pressure inequality; a localized Pohozaev identity and scaling give the Liouville theorem. At criticality, for $N\ge3$ and $-p<a<0$, we classify all positive entire weak solutions in $W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(R^N)$, without assuming local boundedness, symmetry, stability, finite energy, or decay at infinity.

title: Exact Decisions and Certified Values in $L_\infty$-Norm Computation from State-Space Representations
abstract: Computing the $L_\infty$-norm of a time-invariant linear ordinary differential control system is a routine task in robust control, usually delegated to floating-point routines that perform well on most practical systems. Behind the numerical value, however, lies a discrete decision: whether a pole lies on the imaginary axis, and whether a mode of a realization is actually a pole of the transfer matrix. Floating-point arithmetic can only replace this decision with a tolerance. This paper explains, for a control audience, what reliable symbolic-numeric computation offers for this problem: exact arithmetic where a decision has to be made, and certified enclosures where a value has to be computed. We show how the problem is turned into a small polynomial system directly from state-space data, how this system is solved in practice, and what it costs. A benchmark on the {\tt COMPleib} library and on families of systems with known norms shows that two standard numerical routines err in opposite directions on the imaginary-axis decision, and never on the same system, while the certified method decides it correctly on every instance tested and computes the norm at a cost comparable to that of the numerical routines on most systems. We conclude with practical guidelines for users of numerical tools.

title: Inhomogeneous First-order Differential Operator Representations of $E_6$ and Graded Betti Numbers
abstract: We realize the restricted dual Verma modules of arbitrary highest weight for the complex simple Lie algebra of type $E_6$ by inhomogeneous first-order differential operators in $36$ variables. The construction is obtained by applying Xu's functor (2016) to the full conformal oscillator representation of $\mathfrak{o}(10)$. We construct polynomial bases for all six fundamental $E_6$-modules and obtain a finite spanning set for every finite-dimensional irreducible $E_6$-module $V(λ)$. The degree in $16$ selected variables gives $V(λ)$ a grading over the symmetric algebra of the opposite abelian nilradical. We compute its Hilbert series and graded Betti numbers, and verify the Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks conjecture for this family. The minimal graded free resolution of $V(λ)$ is pure precisely when $λ$ is a nonnegative multiple of the Weyl vector of $E_6$. Among nonzero dominant integral $λ$'s, the minimum total Betti number is $435204$, attained exactly at two minuscule weights $ω_1$ and $ω_6$.

title: Small cells in great-circle arrangements
abstract:
We study the areas of the cells determined by an arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ of $n$ distinct great circles on the unit sphere, with no three concurrent. Let $m(\mathcal{A})$ and $M(\mathcal{A})$ denote the smallest and largest cell areas, respectively. Our first result is the bound \[
  m(\mathcal{A})\le \frac{C_*+O(n^{-3/4})}{n^2},
  \qquad C_*=7.0666071493\ldots , \] where the implied constant is absolute. This improves the coefficient $π^2$ obtained from classical polygonal perimeter estimates. We also prove that $M(\mathcal{A})/m(\mathcal{A})>13$ for all sufficiently large $n$, improving the bound $7.43$ of L.~Fejes Tóth. The main tool is a perimeter inequality for planar polygons which takes account of their exterior angles. We combine this with a positive semidefinite kernel on the sphere and use gnomonic projection to obtain bounds for spherical cells.

title: Fast Subproblem Solving in Benders Decomposition for Affine Potential-Based Flow Problems with Topology Switching and Scenarios
abstract: Potential-based flow problems arise for a range of practical problems, like the operation of lossless power networks. The distribution of flows through the network is governed by the potential equation, which relates arc flows and node potentials following arc potential functions. We consider a general variant with affine potential functions, topology switching, and scenarios. It can be solved using a Benders decomposition algorithm, with each scenario corresponding to a subproblem. Subproblem solving time can then significantly contribute to overall running time. We present a fast algorithm to obtain Benders optimality and feasibility cuts from fixed master solutions. Problems with affine potential functions are reduced to equivalent problems where every potential function is the identity function. Optimal primal and dual solutions as well as unbounded dual rays are determined by systems of linear equations (SLE), resulting in a constant number of SLEs solved per subproblem. SLEs are solved using LU-factorizations, with the similarity between primal and dual, scenarios, and master solutions exploited by reusing factorizations via low-rank updates to significantly reduce theoretical complexity. We demonstrate the method on security-constrained optimal transmission switching instances, where subproblem solve time reductions of 97.98 percent compared to a standard LP solver are observed.

title: Volume asymptotics for a family of hyperbolic 3-manifolds with totally geodesic boundary
abstract: For the family $\{\mathcal{M}_{g,k}\}_{g\geqslant k\geqslant 0}$ of orientable hyperbolic 3-manifolds with totally geodesic boundary and cusps introduced by R.~Frigerio, B.~Martelli, and C.~Petronio, the volume of the manifolds depends only on the non-negative integer parameters $g$ and $k$; thus the volume function $Vol(g,k)$ is well defined. The main result of the paper is an asymptotic description of this function: it is approximated by a linear function of $g$ and $k$ whose coefficients are explicitly expressed in terms of the volumes of the regular ideal tetrahedron and the regular ideal octahedron; moreover, the volume does not exceed the linear approximation by a difference of order $O(1/g)$. As consequences, three theorems comparing volumes are obtained: monotonicity under coordinatewise increase of the parameters, estimates for the passage from parameter $g$ to $g+1$, and monotonicity along lines of constant complexity $g+k$. For small values of the parameters, approximate values of the volumes are computed and collected in a table used in verifying the cases $g<8$.

title: Congruence properties modulo powers of 3 for designated summands in partitions into odd parts
abstract: Let $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Using $3$-dissection identities and coefficient extraction, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of two infinite families of arithmetic subsequences of $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$. We establish lower bounds for the $3$-adic valuations of the coefficients in these expansions, thereby proving two infinite families of congruences modulo powers of 3 conjectured by Lin (J. Number Theory,~2018). We then estimate the $3$-adic valuations of two-by-two determinants formed from consecutive coefficient vectors. These estimates yield two infinite families of internal congruences modulo high powers of $3$.

title: A Chord-Arc Estimate for Graphical Hypersurfaces
abstract: We prove an interior chord-arc estimate for graphical hypersurfaces without an a priori gradient bound, which is not restricted to balls on the scale of their curvature. As a main application we derive an in-radius lower bound depending on the curvature which then also implies Heinz-type estimates for minimal graphs and uniform area bounds for graphical hypersurfaces.

title: Connection-twisted modules and logarithmic twisted modules of vertex algebras
abstract: We formulate the notion of connection-twisted modules for $\mathbb{C}$-graded vertex algebras, as suggested by Feigin and Lentner, and investigate their fundamental properties. Let $G$ be an algebraic group acting on a vertex algebra $V$ by automorphisms. We establish an equivalence between the category of $\nabla$-twisted $V$-modules and the category of $g$-twisted $V$-modules, where $\nabla$ is a regular singular $\mathfrak{g}$-connection and $g\in G$ is its monodromy. For symplectic fermion and affine vertex algebras, we explicitly compute the commutation relations and the action of the Virasoro algebra on connection-twisted modules, recovering the formulas obtained by Feigin and Lentner \cite{FL24,FL25}.

title: Computing extensions of flag-jump t-modules
abstract:
We study Anderson t-modules whose positive-degree coefficient matrices admit a flag-jump basis and extend the t-reduction algorithm to this setting. We prove that these t-modules are abelian, with motive rank equal to the sum of their jump degrees. If $Φ$ has jump degrees $j_1,\ldots,j_d$ and $deg_τΨ<\min_s j_s$, we compute the t-module structure on ${\mathbf{Ext}}^1_τ(Φ,Ψ)$, its subgroup ${\mathbf{Ext}}_{0,τ}(Φ,Ψ)$, and the associated exact sequence.
  The construction allows nonzero nilpotent constant terms and includes the strictly pure case. When $Ψ$ is the Carlitz module, $N_Φ=0$, and all jump degrees are at least two, the construction yields a dual t-module. We give complexity bounds for the algorithms and implementations in SymPy and Mathematica.

title: Solvability of $L^2$-Neumann Problems for Fractional Laplace Equations on Bounded Lipschitz Domains
abstract: Let $n\geq2$, $s\in(0,1)$, and $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. In this paper, we study the solvability of the fractional Neumann problem \begin{equation*} \left\{\begin{aligned} (-Δ)^su&=0 & & \text{in}\ \ Ω,\\ \mathcal{N}_s u&=g & & \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ, \end{aligned}\right. \end{equation*} with $\mathcal{N}_s$ denoting the nonlocal normal derivative in $\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ$ and $g:=a_sq$, where $a_s(z):=(1-s)\frac{δ(z)^{-s}}{1+δ(z)^{n+s}}$ with $δ(z):=\mathrm{dist\,}(z,\partialΩ)$ for any $z\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ$, and $q\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ,a_s\,dz)$ satisfies $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ}a_sq\,dz=0$. For the weak solution $u$, we obtain the non-tangential maximal function estimate \begin{equation*} \left\|\left(δ^{1-s}|\nabla u|\right)^*\right\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ,\,a_s\,dz)} \leq C\|q\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ,\,a_s\,dz)}, \end{equation*} where, for any function $f$ on $Ω$, $f^\ast$ denotes the non-tangential maximal function of $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ$. This result extends the classical $L^2$ solvability theory for the Neumann problem of Laplace equations on bounded Lipschitz domains to the setting of fractional Neumann problems, and also provides a Neumann counterpart to the $L^2$-solvability result for fractional Dirichlet problems established by Colombo, Fernández-Real and Ros-Oton \cite{CFR26}. In addition, we prove the fractional Sobolev estimate $\|u\|_{H^{3s/2}(Ω)}\leq C\|q\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ,\,a_s\,dz)}$ and the weighted gradient estimate \begin{equation*} \left(\int_Ωδ^{2-3s}|\nabla u|^2\,dx\right)^{\frac12} \leq C\|q\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΩ,\,a_s\,dz)}. \end{equation*}

title: VR-Net: Subarray-Level Inter-Cell Coordination for Multi-Cell XL-MIMO under Near-Field Spatial Non-Stationarity
abstract: Spatial non-stationarity in multi-cell extremely large-scale MIMO (XL-MIMO) confines each user to a visibility region (VR) of each array. VR-Net exploits these regions for subarray-level coordinated beamforming. A base-station (BS)-indexed conflict graph identifies overlapping VRs; gain-based association and a masked multi-cell weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) iteration restrict beam design and channel state information (CSI) uploads to the relevant subarray blocks. We establish conditions for exact per-cell decoupling, derive the expected CSI loads, bound the loss of designing on the VR-gated channel and the loss of the support constraint, and characterize single-edge visibility contrast through a closed-form Fresnel transition width. Simulations use a 3GPP TR 38.901 Release-19-based near-field UMi channel with modular facade arrays and pre-registered criteria. At a 30 dB threshold, VR-Net retains at least 99.6% of the full-aperture WMMSE sum rate in every tested setting while uploading 10-39% fewer complex CSI entries. It gains up to 3.5 bit/s/Hz over an all-user adaptation of the multi-cell scheme of Pérez-Adán et al. at moderate power and dense load, and inter-cell coordination adds up to 33% over per-cell design.

title: Multimodal Semantic Communication using Shared and Unique Representation Decomposition
abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) has emerged as a promising paradigm for bandwidth-constrained mobile and vehicular networks. This paper proposes a unified representation learning framework for multimodal SemCom (MSC), which encodes heterogeneous data into a compact semantic space for efficient transmission and source recovery. The framework addresses the multimodal semantic representation gap, which arises when at least one modality contains semantic information that cannot be fully inferred from the other. To preserve this information for reconstruction, the framework decomposes each representation into shared and modality-specific components. We formulate a mutual information objective for source reconstruction, cross-modal alignment of the shared components, and decoupling of the shared and modality-specific components. To enhance transmission efficiency, we introduce a shared knowledge base implemented as a compact codebook of semantic vectors learned during training. The shared components are transmitted digitally as codebook indices, while the modality-specific components are sent in analog form. We apply knowledge distillation during training, using a pretrained vision foundation model to guide the learning of quantized shared features. On image--text pairs over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Extended Vehicular A (EVA) channels, the proposed framework improves image reconstruction over conventional separate source-channel coding (SSCC) and representative multimodal and unimodal SemCom systems. Further evaluations show gradual degradation under channel-estimation mismatch, complementary effects of alignment, decoupling, and knowledge distillation on the shared representation, and alignment of shared features across modalities with separation of the modality-specific features.

title: K-stable Fano varieties can have obstructed deformations
abstract: We exhibit examples of K-stable Fano varieties with obstructed qG-deformations; more precisely, their miniversal qG-deformation spaces can be non-reduced. As a consequence, we show that both the K-moduli stack and the K-moduli space can be non-reduced, and hence non-smooth, at points corresponding to K-stable Fano varieties.

title: RPX: Certifying Agent-Generated MILP Reformulations at Scale
abstract: We present RPX, an independent certificate checker for AI-generated reformulations of mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs). RPX verifies that every feasible solution of either the original or the reformulated model can be converted into a feasible solution of the other with no worse objective value. This guarantees equal optimal values and enables solution recovery in the original variables. The checker derives the required checks directly from both models and verifies the certificate using exact arithmetic and reusable reconstruction rules. RPX certifies an agent-generated reformulation for each of the 240 instances in MIPLIB 2017 Benchmark v2. The source models contain up to 27.3 million matrix nonzeros. The median time to decode and check a certificate is 0.312 s, with a 95th percentile of 10.1 s.

title: Frank-Wolfe Theorems for Mixed Integer Quadratic Optimization
abstract: The Frank-Wolfe theorem states that a quadratic function bounded from below on a polyhedron attains its infimum. We study when this remains true in the presence of integer variables, for sets defined by quadratic inequalities. Our main result is a complete classification for sets defined by convex quadratic inequalities with rational coefficients and a rational affine hull, a condition that holds for all full- dimensional sets. One integer variable never destroys attainment: if every rational quadratic objective that is bounded from below attains its infimum over the set, even after adding rational linear constraints, the same holds with one integer variable. In dimension at most 2, integer variables never destroy attainment. In dimension at least 3 and with two or more integer variables, attainment holds for every such objective if and only if the set has bounded curvature, that is, it is bounded except along directions in which all constraints are linear. Without convexity, these results remain valid, except that bounded curvature is no longer necessary. Moreover, integer variables can destroy attainment only if there are at least two of them and at least one continuous variable. The result for one integer variable follows from a lifting theorem, which also extends known results for cubic objectives and convex polynomial constraints. Finally, for convex constraints and rational data, attainment holds when the objective is bounded from above, convex, or quasi-convex over a full-dimensional convex set containing the feasible region.

title: Reduced-Complexity WMMSE Approach for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems With Finite-Capacity Fronthaul Links
abstract: We propose a reduced-complexity weighted minimum mean squared error (R-WMMSE) framework for cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) systems with finite-capacity fronthaul links. To maximize the system capacity, we need to jointly design beamforming vectors at distributed access points (APs) and fronthaul quantization noise covariances. Such a task would be addressed using conventional WMMSE algorithms and their variants. However, existing WMMSE-based methods either assume ideal infinite-capacity fronthaul links or incur high computational complexity when jointly optimizing the network-wide beamforming and fronthaul compression variables. To this end, the proposed method jointly optimizes beamforming and fronthaul compression by leveraging a sequential per-AP optimization strategy. Since each subproblem is efficiently solved via Lagrangian duality with closed-form updates, the overall computational complexity can be significantly reduced compared to the conventional WMMSE method. To further reduce hardware cost, we extend the R-WMMSE framework to hybrid analog-digital beamforming systems, tackling the joint design of digital beamforming, fronthaul compression, and analog beamforming. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme achieves performance nearly identical to that of the conventional WMMSE while reducing the runtime by over 99%.

title: Higher order convergence rate in probability for approximations of the stochastic Burgers and Cahn-Hilliard equation
abstract: We consider temporal approximations of stochastic PDEs driven by additive space-time white noise, with nonlinearities that may lose both integrability and regularity. Our key examples are the stochastic Burgers equation in dimension 1 and the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation in dimensions $\leq 3$. We show that the accelerated exponential Euler scheme achieves a rate of convergence in probability that is well beyond the state of the art: arbitrarily close to $3/4$ in the case of Burgers and $1-d/8$ in the case of Cahn-Hilliard.

title: A Monotone Meshfree-Particle Method for Mean Field Games on Scattered Point Clouds
abstract: We develop a monotone meshfree--particle method for mean field games (MFGs). We discretize the backward Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation on a fixed scattered cloud, transport the forward Fokker--Planck law with reflected and killed particles, and close the fictitious-play loop by interpolation and mass-preserving kernel density estimation. Monotonicity is imposed row by row on two-dimensional clouds. Each row combines a positive generalized finite difference Laplacian with a nonnegative decomposition of the drift along rays to surrounding visible neighbors, with mirror images at reflecting walls, and every fixed-policy matrix is an M-matrix for arbitrary cell-Péclet number. We prove a discrete comparison principle and, on polygons with re-entrant corners included, that one HJB solve at a prescribed density converges to the viscosity solution off the boundary vertices, for convex Hamiltonians of at most quadratic growth under a structure condition. On a two-room floor plan with re-entrant door jambs, the computed HJB solutions converge to exact ones. A source-free exact MFG tests the fully coupled computation. At matched degrees of freedom on a grid domain, the meshfree HJB solve has a larger $L^2$ error and a smaller $L^\infty$ error than a five-point finite-difference solve, and is about twice as expensive including the stencil construction. On a non-convex evacuation game, the interior nodes of nine clouds receive monotone rows, apart from a few next to the boundary vertices that copy a neighbor.

title: Bergman Kernel Zeros on Generalized Hartogs Triangles
abstract: We study zeros of the Bergman kernel on the generalized Hartogs triangles $H_γ=\{(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2:|z_1|^γ<|z_2|<1\}$. For every real $1<γ<2$, suitable sections near the singular vertex contain exactly $\lceil(γ-1)^{-1}\rceil-1$ zeros in a prescribed disk, all of them simple. This answers a question of Edholm and Mathew [\emph{Math. Z.} \textbf{313} (2026)] and, together with the known cases, shows that $H_γ$ has a zero-free Bergman kernel precisely when $γ$ is the reciprocal of a positive integer. We also fix the second kernel argument and a complex line in the first argument, and prove that the total number of zeros on the admissible section is comparable to $(γ-1)^{-1}$ as $γ\to1^+$; a comparable number are simple and nonreal. For the sections near the vertex, all but at most one of the counted zeros concentrate near the unit circle, and the angular counting error is uniformly bounded.

title: Nonlinear selection in vanishing discount problems for Hamilton--Jacobi equations
abstract: We study the vanishing discount problem $G(x,Du_λ,λu_λ)=c_0$, where $G$ is convex and superlinear in the momentum and strictly increasing in its last variable. Assuming a leading-order expansion of the Lagrangian of order $q>0$, we prove uniform convergence and characterize the selected solution by nonlinear inequalities against Mather measures. In particular, our results cover discount terms whose first derivative at the origin vanishes, such as the cubic discount, beyond existing convergence results based on first-order nondegeneracy. Our proof uses truncated calibrated curves and time averages, without the exponentially weighted measures used by Davini--Fathi--Iturriaga--Zavidovique. In the linear case, it gives a short alternative proof of their convergence and selection theorem. An example shows that linear and cubic discounts may select critical solutions that do not differ by an additive constant.

title: Hyperbolicity Notions on Complete Non-Compact Complex Manifolds
abstract: Gromov's Kähler hyperbolicity, extended by McMullen to complete manifolds of finite volume and bounded geometry, has non-Kähler analogues (balanced, SKT, Gauduchon and divisorial hyperbolicity) that have so far been studied only on compact manifolds. We define these notions for complete Hermitian manifolds and prove the following. A manifold carrying a balanced metric and a Hermitian metric with bounded $(\partial+\bar\partial)$-potentials satisfies a Cheeger inequality, so its fundamental group is non-amenable in the compact case. Kähler and SKT hyperbolic manifolds are Brody hyperbolic, and balanced and Gauduchon hyperbolic manifolds are divisorially hyperbolic, without any compactness assumption. Products give complete non-compact non-Kähler examples. A non-compact surface may be divisorially hyperbolic without being Brody hyperbolic. Finally, no functorial pseudo-distance characterises divisorial hyperbolicity.}

title: On the Equivalence of Linear and $C^*$ Extremality for Unital Completely Positive Maps on Commutative Real $C^*$-algebras
abstract: Let $\mathcal A$ be a unital commutative real $C^*$-algebra and $\mathcal H$ be a finite dimensional real Hilbert space. In this article, an easily verifiable necessary and sufficient condition for a linear extreme unital completely positive (UCP) map $Φ:\mathcal A \rightarrow B(\mathcal H)$ to be C*-extreme, is obtained.
