As an application, the $C^*$-algebras $\mathcal A$ on which linear extreme UCP maps coincide with the $C^*$-extreme ones, are classified.

title: Sharp L^p and variation inequalities for maximal operators on finite connected graphs
abstract: Let $G=(V_G,E_G)$ be a finite connected graph (here $V_G$ and $E_G$ denote the set of vertices and edges of $G$ respectively). The primary aim of this paper is to study the sharp variation and $L^p$ inequalities of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator $M_G$ defined on $G$ and its fractional variant $M_{α,G}\,(0<α<1)$). Set $${\bf C}_{α,G}^{p,q}=\sup\limits_{{\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)>0}\frac{{\rm Var}_{q,G}(M_{α,G}f)}{{\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)},$$ where ${\rm Var}_{p,G}(f)$ denotes the $p$-variation of $f$ on $G$. We denote by $K_n$ (resp., $S^n$) the complete (resp., star) graph with $n\geq4$ vertices. When $α=0$, we prove ${\bf C}_{α,S_n}^{p,p} =1-\frac{1}{n}$ for $0<p<1$. This solve a question originally posed by Liu and Xue in 2021. In the fractional case $0<α<1$, we prove ${\bf C}_{α,S_n}^{1,q}=1-n^{-α}$ and ${\bf C}_{α,K_n}^{1,q} =(1-n^{α-1})(n-1)^{-α}$ for $q=\frac{1}{1-α}$, which provide some examples focusing on sharp variation inequalities of fractional maximal operators. The sharp variation inequalities of uncentered fractional maximal operators are also established. In addition, the sharp $L^p$ inequalities of uncentered fractional maximal operator $\widetilde{M}_{α,G}$ are also studied. More precisely, we obtain lower bounds and upper bounds for $C_{q,G}$ such that the inequality $\|\widetilde{M}_{α,G}f\|_q\leq C_{q,G}\|f\|_p$ holds and the complete graphs $K_n$ and star graphs $S_n$ are two extreme graphs that reach the lower bound and upper bound respectively.

title: Set-coloring Ramsey numbers with multiple intersections
abstract:
For integers $r\ge s\ge t\ge1$, we introduce the Ramsey number $R(G;r,s,t)$, defined as the least $N$ such that every assignment of an $s$-element subset of $[r]$ to each edge of $K_N$ yields a copy of $G$ whose edges have at least $t$ colors in common. This generalizes the classical set-coloring Ramsey number $R(G;r,s)=R(G;r,s,1)$, studied since the work of Erdos, Hajnal, and Rado. We show that $t$ cannot in general be eliminated by reparametrization: infinitely many quadruples $(G;r,s,t)$ satisfy $R(G;r,s,t)\ne R(G;a,b)$ for every $a\ge b\ge1$.
  Writing $α=\binom{r}{t}/\binom{s}{t}$, the shadow inequality $R(G;r,s,t)\le R(G;\binom{r}{t},\binom{s}{t},1)$ and the recent proof of the Erdos--Sos conjecture imply $R(T_n;r,s,t)\le\lfloorα(n-2)\rfloor+2$ for every $n$-vertex tree $T_n$. For stars, we obtain packing bounds and exact values under suitable divisibility conditions. For paths and even cycles $G$ of order $n$, we improve the upper bound to $R(G;r,s,t)\le(α-γ+o(1))n$ as $n\to\infty$, for fixed $r>s\ge t\ge1$ and some $γ=γ(r,s,t)>0$. We also prove that, for fixed $s,t$, the tree bound is asymptotically sharp for paths as $r,n\to\infty$, and for even cycles when $n\to\infty$ first and then $r\to\infty$.
  For cliques $K_n$, we transfer known bounds of Conlon et al. for ordinary set-coloring Ramsey numbers to the general parameter $t$, obtaining two-sided exponential bounds. For each fixed $n\ge3$, we identify an explicit piecewise-linear function $Φ_n$ that determines a growth threshold. If $s/r\toσ$ and $t/r\toτ$ as $r\to\infty$, with $0<τ\leσ<1$, then $R(K_n;r,s,t)=O(1)$ when $τ<Φ_n(σ)$, whereas $R(K_n;r,s,t)\ge\exp(cr)$ for some $c>0$ when $τ>Φ_n(σ)$.

title: Combinatorial results for semigroups of order-preserving mappings
abstract: We investigate combinatorial properties of the semigroup of all order- preserving mappings on {1, 2, . . . , n} and of its subsemigroup of all decreasing order-preserving mappings. We show that the cardinal of the latter is the nth Catalan number and obtain a new proof of the standard Catalan identity. Using ballot arguments and the Reflection principle we find the probability that a random order-preserving mapping is indecomposable, and via the Wallis product we show that the mean number of orbits is of order root n. By contrast, the mean number of orbits of a random decreasing mapping of this type never exceeds 3; we find the distribution of the orbit number explicitly in both cases and obtain the limiting distribution for the Catalan monoid.

title: Universal Realization of Milnor Attractors in Low Dimensions
abstract: We study the realization problem for Milnor attractors on compact metric spaces and establish a general sufficient criterion for universal realization. In particular, we prove that every smooth compact one-dimensional manifold, with or without boundary, and every smooth closed two-dimensional manifold has the property that each nonempty closed subset is the Milnor global attractor of a continuous self-map. If the manifold is connected, the realizing map may be chosen to be a homeomorphism. We also investigate the realization problem on selected one-dimensional continua and exhibit spaces for which universal realization fails.

title: Non-concordant knots with the same trace
abstract: Miller and Piccirillo demonstrated the existence of non-concordant knots that share the same 0-trace. In this short note, we generalize their result by showing that every smooth concordance class contains a knot K such that, for every nonzero integer n, there exists a knot $K_n$ whose n-trace is orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic to that of K, but for which $p[K_n] \ne p[K]$ in the topological concordance group for every positive integer p. Furthermore, $p[K_n]$ is distinct from $p[K']$ for any knot K' obtained from K by mirroring and/or reversing its orientation.

title: Classification of G-g.o. metrics on compact homogeneous spaces G/H with G simple
abstract: We classify the $G$-g.o. metrics on compact homogeneous spaces $G/H$, where $G$ is a compact connected simple Lie group and $H$ is an arbitrary closed subgroup. We give the complete list of nonnormal metrics, including their parameter conditions and the possible mixing between equivalent isotropy summands. The proof uses rigidity criteria for arbitrary cometric operators, reductions through centralizers, and the stabilizers of the relevant representations. For every fixed pair $(G,H)$, the space spanned by the $G$-g.o. cometrics has dimension at most three, and we determine the equality cases. We also compare the classification with the compact weakly symmetric pairs and explain why the choice of the transitive group is essential.

title: Duality and hidden symmetries for time-inhomogeneous Markov processes
abstract: We study the notion of duality in the setting of time-inhomogeneous Markov processes. We define duality with time-dependent duality functions. We establish the connection between duality and time-dependent symmetries and intertwinings. We illustrate the abstract results with examples from interacting particle systems and diffusion processes.

title: $2$-blocks with defect group of rank $2$
abstract: We classify all controlled $2$-blocks with defect group of rank $2$ up to Morita equivalence. This provides a proof of Donovan's Conjecture for resistant $2$-generated $2$-groups.

title: Surface evolution under conformal map and linearized energy-stable parametric finite element methods
abstract: In this paper, we aim to develop a linearized, energy-stable, second-order-in-time parametric finite element method without Lagrange multipliers for surface evolution equations on surfaces with or without boundaries, including (volume-preserving) mean curvature flow and surface diffusion. We first reformulate the original equations into a new unified form in which the tangential motion is determined by requiring the flow map to be conformal. Based on this new formulation, we present a family of parametric finite element schemes that employ a linearized Euler or Crank-Nicolson discretization in time. We prove the existence and uniqueness of the resulting linear system, as well as the energy stability of the schemes. Our discrete methods can be applied to general surfaces although the second-order scheme may degenerate to first-order accuracy in certain cases. Numerical results verify the robustness of our method and demonstrate its ability to preserve mesh quality.

title: Nearly Computable Numbers with Additional Properties
abstract:
A real number is called \emph{nearly computable} if it is the limit of a computable sequence of rational (or dyadic) numbers that has the additional property that for any computable subsequence the sequence of differences of consecutive elements converges to $0$ computably. The main result of this article provides methods for constructing nearly computable numbers with additional properties. The main result is proved by an infinite injury priority argument. Using these methods, we construct nearly computable numbers with several different additional properties:
  - a nearly computable number that is not divergence bounded computable,
  - for any left-computable number $α$ that is neither in the least nor in the highest Solovay degree, a left-computable, nearly computable number that is Solovay incomparable with $α$,
  - a nearly computable number $γ$ that can be written as the difference of two left-computable numbers but has the property that for any two left-computable numbers $α$ and $β$ wih $γ=α-β$ both $α$ and $β$ are Martin-Löf random.
  We also look at two classes of nearly computable numbers: the class $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ of differences of real numbers that are nearly computable and left-computable, and the class $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{wnc}}$ of nearly computable numbers that can be written as the difference of two left-computable numbers. Both classes form real closed fields, in fact, $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ is closed under computable functions with open domain that are Lipschitz continuous or differentiable. Finally, we show that $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{dlnc}}$ is a proper subset of $\mathbb{R}_{\mathrm{wnc}}$.

title: Self-similar cusp formation in a large class of nonlocal transport equations
abstract: We prove finite-time gradient blow-up with sharp $C^{(5-b)/(b+3)}$ Hölder regularity for a class of nonlocal transport equations extending the $b$-family, for all real $1<b<5$. This class includes the Camassa--Holm and Degasperis--Procesi equations and, after rescaling, the generalized hyperelastic-rod wave equation. In the blow-up regime, the nonlocal equations reduce at leading order to the generalized Hunter--Saxton (gHS) equation with parameter $\ell=2/(b-1)$, whose self-similar scaling and corresponding profiles depend on $\ell$. Consequently, standard approaches tailored to a fixed self-similar profile cannot be applied directly. To handle this parameter dependence, we develop a general framework for self-similar singularity formation in evolution equations whose leading-order dynamics are governed by the gHS family. The key ingredient is a family of profile inequalities established for all real $\ell>1/2$, which we combine with a generalized maximum principle to close a parameter-dependent bootstrap argument. We identify model-specific hypotheses adapted to this framework, under which this argument yields the required stability estimates. This leads to a general theorem on singularity formation, which we apply to the entire class of nonlocal equations, thereby establishing finite-time gradient blow-up and sharp Hölder regularity. The theorem can also be applied to other evolution equations once the corresponding model-specific hypotheses are verified, without repeating the profile analysis or the common stability argument.

title: Quadratic Elements in Finite $p$-Groups and Applications to Oliver's $p$-Group Conjecture
abstract: We establish a property of quadratic elements in faithful modules for finite $p$-groups. Let $p$ be an odd prime, and suppose that $a$ is a quadratic element of an abelian subgroup $L$ normalized by $b$. Writing $a_0=a$ and $a_i=[a_{i-1},b]$, we prove that if, for some $r$ with $2\leq r\leq(p+1)/2$, one has $a_{r-1}\neq1$ and $a_r=1$, then $a_{r-1}$ is quadratic. As an application, we prove that every finite $p$-group of nilpotency class at most $(p+5)/2$ satisfies the Quadratic Conjecture. Consequently, Oliver's $p$-group conjecture holds for a finite $p$-group $S$ whenever $S/\mathfrak X(S)$ has nilpotency class at most $(p+5)/2$.

title: Ehrhart Series and Transfer Matrices for Period-Two Polytopes with Consecutive Inequalities
abstract: We study a family of period-two polytopes that can be naturally realized as lattice polytopes. In contrast to polytopes defined by a uniform system of inequalities, this family is characterized by consecutive coordinate inequalities whose bounds alternate between $s+1$ and $s$. The lattice points of these polytopes admit an explicit transfer-matrix formulation, which provides an effective framework for their enumeration and analysis. Furthermore, by considering fixed dilations, we investigate the associated dimensional generating functions and derive rational forms for the generating functions of the lattice points in the $m$-th dilates of the polytopes.

title: On the Cauchy-Bunyakovsky-Schwarz Inequality in Pseudo-Euclidean Space
abstract: In a pseudo-Euclidean space, the Cauchy-Bunyakovsky-Schwarz inequality generalization is derived and studied. Complex vector space is considered as well. Generalizations of angles and dihedral angles in these spaces are studied.

title: On the moduli of distinct covering systems
abstract: In 2022, Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba proved that the least common multiple of the moduli in any distinct covering system with odd moduli is divisible by $9$ or $15$. We strengthen this necessary condition to divisibility by $45$ and prove that the minimum modulus of an odd distinct covering system is at most $9$. For arbitrary distinct moduli, we lower the upper bound of Balister et al.\ on the minimum modulus from $616000$ to $14000$. For distinct squarefree moduli, we lower the upper bound of $118$ obtained by Cummings, Filaseta, and Trifonov in 2025 to $7$. Our proofs combine the distortion method with a joint comparison based on directional convexity. The comparison uses independent random exponents to bound expectations of convex functions of sums of indicators of residue classes, while retaining the restrictions on the allowed moduli. A sharper bound for the conditional density on each fibre further improves the estimates for the subsequent stages of the distortion process.

title: Exact Output Steering with Vanishing Controls in Weighted Shift Dynamics
abstract:
Exploiting the rich dynamics of wrapped weighted shifts and their residualizations, we characterize exact projected steering with vanishing initial controls.
  For wrapped shifts, steering is characterized by an expansive cycle multiplier and a residue separating the source and control channels. For residual shifts, a distinct spectral--toral mechanism emerges: steering through selected conjugate planes is equivalent to radial expansion and an arithmetic parity condition on phase resonances, yielding bounded-gap steering times and quantitative control estimates. For structured machine-learning representations built from orbit dictionaries, we derive a two-scale gain condition for steering coefficients while preserving decoded outputs.

title: Well-Posedness for the Cauchy Problem with Free Boundary in Half-Space Arising from Combustion Problem
abstract:
In this paper, we address the local-in-time well-posedness of an obstacle problem arising from a combustion model. The equation under consideration is a linear inhomogeneous heat equation on the moving domain $(s(t),\infty)$, subject to homogeneous Dirichlet and inhomogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. Our main result establishes the existence and uniqueness of a positive classical solution.
  Although several results are known for the homogeneous heat equation, much less is known about the inhomogeneous case. We show that the boundary function $s(t)$ is $\frac{1}{2}$-Hölder continuous in time when the forcing term has a singularity of order $O(1/\sqrt{t})$ as $t \to 0$. We also prove that if both the initial data and the forcing term are smooth, then $s$ has higher regularity than $\frac{1}{2}$-Hölder continuity.

title: Quantum unique ergodicity and the critical crossover for 1-d Gaussian band matrices
abstract: We consider an $N\times N$ complex Gaussian random band matrix in one dimension with band width of order $W$, in the periodic block form of Yau and Yin. The $N$ sites are split into $n=N/W$ blocks of size $W$ on a ring, and the entries are nonzero only within a block and between adjacent blocks. The conjectured localization--delocalization transition occurs at $W\sim\sqrt N$. We prove quantum unique ergodicity for bulk eigenvectors at every deterministic rank whenever $W^2/N\to\infty$, with no power or logarithmic separation between $W^2$ and $N$. At the threshold $N/W^2\toτ\in(0,\infty)$, we show that the rescaled bulk eigenvalues and the block-mass profiles of their eigenvectors (the probability measures on the circle placing at $k/n$ the squared norm of the eigenvector on block $k$) converge jointly to a unique law. This law is encoded by a random entire function whose zeros give the limiting eigenvalues, and its derivatives there give the limiting profile integrals. The law of this function is determined by the Dorokhov--Mello--Pereyra--Kumar (DMPK) diffusion of the unitary class. In the critical law, the profiles have strictly positive variance against every nonconstant smooth test function, so they are not concentrated on the uniform profile. As $τ\to0$ this variance vanishes and the local spectrum tends to the sine process. As $τ\to\infty$ it tends to a Poisson process where both limits taken after the critical one. The critical family thus interpolates between the delocalized and localized regimes, confirming for this model the prediction of Fyodorov and Mirlin that at $W^2\asymp N$ the joint law of eigenvalues and eigenvectors depends only on $N/W^2$. The full content of this work has been autoformalized in Lean4 by AxiomProver.

title: Abelian covers and the index of the centre in a group
abstract: Let $h(n)$ be the largest number of abelian subgroups needed to cover a group in which every set of more than $n$ elements contains two distinct elements that commute, and let $ζ(n)$ be the largest index of the centre under the same constraint. Erdős asked for the growth of $h$, Neumann proved that both quantities are finite, and Pyber bounded both $ζ$ and $h$ exponentially. We determine $h(n)$ for every positive integer $n$ and prove that $h(n)=1+\sqrt{ζ(n)}$ whenever the constraint admits a nonabelian group. The covers are built directly from the commutator geometry of a scalar quotient, and the comparison with $ζ$ is made afterwards. Beyond finitely many small cases, both maxima are attained by the same groups, those isoclinic to an extraspecial $2$-group of order $2^{1+2\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}$, confirming Pyber's prediction for the central index in this range.

title: Face rings and the cohomology of unions of Schubert varieties
abstract: The cohomology ring of a union of Schubert varieties $X_{W}=\bigcup_{w\in W}X_w,$ for $W\subseteq S_n$, in the complete flag variety is well known to be a quotient of the coinvariant ring $R_n$. We determine exactly when the ideal defining this quotient is generated by squarefree monomials, i.e. when it can be identified with the image of a Stanley-Reisner ideal $I_Δ$ in $R_n$. We prove that a single Schubert variety $X_w$ has this property exactly when $w\in S_n$ avoids a set of seven patterns, and in this case we describe the corresponding doubly-pruned simplicial complex $Δ$. We then show this is equivalent to $X_w$ being cut out of the complete flag variety by particular inclusion conditions on the pieces of the flag. We prove these complexes are vertex decomposable, and are Cohen-Macaulay precisely when $X_w$ is smooth. We then give a closed formula for the Poincaré polynomial of $X_w$. For unions $X_W$, pattern avoidance is necessary but no longer sufficient, and we prove a necessary and sufficient condition we call prunable that describes how the individual complexes associated to each $w\in W$ may be glued in the union. Quotients of $R_n$ by squarefree monomial ideals appear naturally in the Adams-Reiner conjecture on resolutions of Stanley-Reisner rings over certain parameter rings. We prove their conjecture for a family of simplicial complexes that includes the doubly-pruned complexes.

title: Spectra of gcd-graphs over a matrix ring
abstract: In this short note, we calculate the spectra of gcd-graphs defined over a matrix ring. Using character sums, we show that this calculation can be reduced to certain counting problems. In particular, when the underlying ring is a matrix ring with coefficients in a finite field, we calculate these spectra explicitly.

title: The Merino-Welsh conjecture for sparse and dense graphs
abstract: The Merino-Welsh conjecture states that the Tutte polynomial $T_G(x,y)$ of a loopless and bridgeless graph $G$ satisfies the inequality $\max\{T_G(2,0),T_G(0,2)\}\geq T_G(1,1).$ It is known to hold for several graph classes, among them sufficiently sparse and sufficiently dense graphs. In this paper, we improve the previously known sufficient density conditions and show that the multiplicative version of the conjecture also holds for sufficiently sparse and sufficiently dense graphs. In particular, we show that for a connected graph $G$ with $m$ edges and $n$ vertices, the Merino-Welsh conjecture holds if either $m\leq1.64(n-1)$ and $G$ is loopless or $m\geq2.55(n-1)$ and $G$ is bridgeless, and the multiplicative conjecture holds if $G$ is loopless and bridgeless with $m\leq1.21(n-1)$ or $m\geq5.62(n-1)$.

title: Multiple-relaxation-time vectorial lattice Boltzmann schemes for incompressible flow: second-order consistency and parameter selection
abstract: We construct and analyze multiple-relaxation-time vectorial lattice Boltzmann schemes for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in two and three space dimensions. The same moment-space relaxation matrix is applied to all physical components, with independent rates for the flux, stress, and energy moments. A Maxwell expansion organized by moment parity establishes formal second-order consistency of the unforced interior schemes under diffusive scaling, assuming a smooth near-equilibrium Maxwell branch. The viscosity depends only on the flux rate; for the two-dimensional scheme, we identify the first contributions of the stress and energy rates to the second-order macroscopic truncation error. We further construct a positive definite symmetrizer for the collision Jacobian at rest and derive an exact weighted-norm identity for the nonlinear kinetic residual under local collision. At fixed viscosity, a finite Fourier search selects the free rates by combining transverse-mode accuracy with short-wavelength damping. The resulting rates are compared with those calibrated against flow errors on a coarse grid. Numerical experiments exhibit second-order convergence and illustrate how the free rates affect spectral properties and finite-time flow errors.

title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for the Kuramoto model on the sphere
abstract: We establish quantitative uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for a generalization of the classical Kuramoto model on spheres of arbitrary dimension. For $n$ particles that are initialized independently from a probability measure with an $L^p$ density, $p>1$, and a nonzero mean vector, we obtain an explicit high-probability bound for the supremum over all times of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical and mean-field distributions. In sufficiently high dimension, this bound has the same order as the standard empirical sampling rate on the sphere and is therefore optimal. The proof combines a finite-time propagation of chaos estimate, a quantitative synchronization result for the mean-field model, and a late-time stability estimate of the system.

title: Sharpness of the acceleration-dependent Hölder exponent for the integrated density of states
abstract: We prove that the acceleration-dependent Hölder exponent $1/(2ω)$ for the integrated density of states is sharp in the supercritical regime. For every positive integer $k$ and every Diophantine frequency, we construct a real even trigonometric polynomial potential of degree $k$ such that, at a spectral edge, the Lyapunov exponent is positive, the acceleration is $k$, and the exact local Hölder exponent is $1/(2k)$. In particular, the $1/2$-Hölder regularity of the subcritical regime for Diophantine frequencies does not hold in general in the supercritical regime. The proof uses Aubry duality and a KAM iteration that adjusts the potential coefficients to make the dual cocycle reducible to a principal unipotent matrix. A comparison with an explicit reference family and symplectic block diagonalization then reduce the IDS estimate to a two-dimensional rotation-number estimate.

title: Cleanness and real rank zero in $C^*$-algebras
abstract: A unital $C^*$-algebra is called clean if every element is the sum of an idempotent and an invertible element. We prove that cleanness is equivalent to real rank zero. More precisely, the invertible summand can be chosen with inverse norm at most $2+\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and the constant $2$ is optimal. In particular, every von Neumann algebra is clean, answering a question of Lam. Clean decompositions with uniformly bounded idempotent summands characterize real rank zero and stable rank one. Moreover, $*$-cleanness, defined by requiring the idempotent summands to be projections, is equivalent to real rank zero, stable rank one, and triviality of the $K_1$-group. Finally, sharp cleanness, defined by requiring clean decompositions with inverse norm at most $2$, is equivalent to real rank zero and the $SAW^*$ property.

title: Packing sets by rigid motions and similarities
abstract: For nonempty Borel sets $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $Θ\subset O(d)\times\mathbb R^d$, where $d\ge2$, let $Θ(E)$ be the union of the rigid copies $gE+z$, where $(g,z)\inΘ$. We prove that $Θ(E)$ has positive Lebesgue measure whenever $\dim_{\mathrm{SF}} E+\dim_HΘ>\frac{d(d+1)}2$, where $\dim_{\mathrm{SF}} E$ is the spherical Fourier dimension of $E$. This resolves a conjecture on packing by arbitrary Borel families of rigid motions. Our proof develops a discrete-to-continuous framework by adapting a finite-field averaging argument to $\mathbb R^d$ using Sobolev estimates on the group of rigid motions. We also obtain analogous packing results for similarities. The same framework can be used to show that if $τ$ is a compactly supported probability measure on the similarity group with finite $\bigl(\frac{d(d-1)}{2}+1\bigr)$-energy, then every compactly supported $τ$-stationary probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$ has a smooth density. We deduce that a nonempty compact set has nonempty interior if its family of similarity self-embeddings has Hausdorff dimension greater than $\frac{d(d-1)}{2}+1$.

title: Dirac eigenvalue comparison
abstract: We study how curvature bounds control the Dirac eigenvalues of closed spin manifolds, comparing the positive and negative eigenvalues separately. Within a fixed conformal class and spin structure, pointwise ordering of scalar curvature relative to a metric of negative scalar curvature implies comparison at every nonzero index. On the two-sphere, a holomorphic ladder on the half-canonical bundle proves the corresponding comparison in both directions under a Gaussian curvature bound. On surfaces of higher genus, the same bundle identities propagate comparison from the scalar and spinor levels to higher canonical powers. In the round conformal class on the higher dimensional sphere, a prescribed scalar curvature bound yields an upper bound in absolute value for the first $2^{[n/2]}$ Dirac eigenvalues. When the conformal class varies, we can show that the corresponding comparisons on hyperbolic surfaces and odd-dimensional spheres no longer hold; while on even-dimensional spheres, the first gap and all sufficiently high-index eigenvalues of either sign satisfy a one-direction comparison.

title: Harmonic functions and the topology of 3-manifolds under nonnegative scalar curvature
abstract: In this paper, we establish and recover some results about noncompact 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature and some topological assumptions. Firstly, we apply the work in Oronzio \cite{Oro1,Oro2} to obtain a nonexistence result of the harmonic function. Secondly, we use the argument in Yan-Zhu \cite{YZ} to establish a rigidity result, which states that such manifold is isometric to the warped product of a flat tours and a half line. Finally, we recover a topological result in Yan-Zhu \cite{YZ} via a different argument.

title: On least periods of a class of arithmetic functions
abstract: Let $k, a, c$ be positive integers, let $b$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $f$ be a nonvanishing complex-valued multiplicative function. Qian, Tan and Hong proved that $$G_f(n)=\frac{\prod\limits_{i=0}^k f(b+a(n+i c))}{f\left(\operatorname*{lcm}\limits_{0 \leq i \leq k}\{b+a(n+i c)\}\right)}$$ is periodic and asked for its least positive period. In this paper, we answer this problem by giving an explicit formula for this period in terms of finitely many values of $f$ at prime powers. In particular, we determine the least periods for $f(n)=σ_α(n)=\sum\limits_{d \mid n} d^α$ for every real $α$, and for $f(n)=n^{\varepsilon}$ for every real $\varepsilon$.

title: On the structure of the sets of connections between libration points and some applications
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for the global description of the sets of heteroclinic and homoclinic connections between the center manifolds of the collinear libration points of the spatial circular Restricted Three-Body Problem. The approach builds on high-order parameterizations of the center-stable and center-unstable invariant manifolds and uses them to extract global information on how connections are organized across broad energy ranges. It involves: (a) constructing connectivity maps at the level of invariant tori, which encode which tori in the neighborhoods of $L_1$ and $L_2$ are connected through heteroclinic and homoclinic trajectories; (b) refining this description to the level of individual connections by computing traces of torus--center manifold connections and using them to determine the number and distribution of distinct connecting trajectories between selected pairs of tori. Results are given for the Earth--Moon and Sun--Earth problems, together with examples illustrating how the resulting connectivity information can be used to design heteroclinic and homoclinic pseudo-trajectories with different purposes.

title: MetaCom: Meta Codebook Learning for Robust V2X Semantic Communications
abstract: Collaborative perception in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) networks faces dual challenges: strictly limited bandwidth and channel impairments. Existing static quantization schemes often suffer from feature manifold drift caused by highly non-stationary traffic environments. To address this, we propose MetaCom, a robust digital semantic communication framework featuring a Meta-Codebook Learning paradigm. First, we introduce a Differentiable Quantized Semantic Communications (DQSemCom) module trained with perturbations induced by the simulated digital modulation and channel via Gumbel-Softmax relaxation. Building on this, we design a Bi-Level Meta-Evolution Mechanism (Bi-MEM) that treats manifold drift as a sequence of rapid adaptation tasks, aligning the codebook via data-level smoothing and parameter-level meta-updates. Furthermore, we validate MetaCom under AWGN, Rayleigh, and Rician fading channels. Experimental results demonstrate that MetaCom achieves superior trade-offs between perception precision and communication overhead, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin under low-SNR conditions.

title: Numerical solution of the Cauchy problem for second-order evolutionary equations with damped sinusoidal memory
abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for a second-order evolutionary equation with an integral term containing the convolution of a memory kernel with the second derivative of the solution. The kernel is specified by a finite sum of damped sinusoidal functions with positive damping coefficients, amplitudes, and frequencies. A transformation of the original nonlocal problem into an equivalent local system of coupled second-order differential equations with additional variables is proposed. For the local system, an energy identity with a dissipative term is constructed and a priori estimates of the solution are obtained. On the basis of the local formulation, a three-level difference scheme with a weight parameter is considered. The decrease of the discrete energy under standard constraints on the weight parameter is proved, which ensures unconditional stability of the scheme in the corresponding energy norm. The theoretical consideration is supplemented by the results of numerical solution of a problem with memory for a one-dimensional wave equation.

title: Cumulants of Operator Semigroups for Hierarchies of Many-Particle Evolution Equations
abstract:
The paper presents a brief overview of recent advances in the mathematical theory of evolution equations for quantum many-particle systems.
  The structure of expansions representing non-perturbative solutions to the Cauchy problem for hierarchies of fundamental evolution equations for many quantum particles is outlined. It has been shown that the concept of cumulants of operator semigroups forms the basis for non-perturbative representation of solutions to hierarchies of evolution equations that describe the state and observables.
  It is proven that the constructed dynamics of correlations underlie the description of the evolution of the state, both for finitely and infinitely many particles, governed by the BBGKY hierarchy for reduced density operators or by the hierarchy of nonlinear evolution equations for reduced correlation operators. In fact, it is demonstrated that the behavior of particle correlations governs the dynamics of states in quantum systems with an infinite number of particles.

title: Growth function of the cactus groups
abstract: We determine the growth functions of the cactus groups of all degrees with respect to their standard generators, and provide explicit equations for specific degrees as examples.

title: Cyclic fibers and exponential lower bounds for Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constants
abstract: We show that for every integer $n\ge2$ that is not a power of two there are constants $c_n>0$ and $B_n>2$ such that $s(C_n^r)\ge c_nB_n^r$ for all $r\ge1$. For powers of two, Harborth's formula gives growth rate exactly $2$. For the remaining even exponents, the previous lower bounds were of order $r2^r$. When $n=2m$ with $m\ge3$ odd, we prove the transfer inequality \[ A_n(H\oplus C_n^5)\ \ge\ 12\,A_n(H\oplus C_n)+8\,A_n(H\oplus C_m), \] where $A_n(G)$ is the maximal length of a sequence over $G$ without an $n$-term zero-sum subsequence and $H$ is any finite abelian group whose exponent divides $n$. The transfer extends a configuration of Elsholtz to twenty full cyclic fibers. Combined with a nine-point binary construction for $2m$-term zero-sums over $C_m^r$, it gives bases at least $2.0341$ that tend to $2.0394\ldots$; combined with a finite-field construction, it gives $s(C_6^r)\ge c\cdot 2.0491^r$. For exponents divisible by $4$ that are not powers of two, we obtain a base above two from a weighted random construction on the eighteen-point configuration of Wang and Zeng.

title: Smooth weak log Fano orbifolds are Campana rationally connected
abstract: Let \(X\) be a smooth projective complex variety with a boundary divisor \(Δ=\sum_{i=1}^s(1-1/m_i)D_i\) of simple normal crossings support and integers $m_i$. We prove that, if \(-(K_X+Δ)\) is nef and big, then \((X,Δ)\) is Campana rationally connected. We do this by constructing a free Campana rational curve whose class lies in the interior of the nef cone of curve classes and whose contacts with \(D_i\) have order \(m_i\) and avoid deeper strata. We construct such a curve from a free Campana curve by attaching to it free rational curves which intersect positively with divisors that span the cone of effective divisors, and smooth the resulting comb.

title: Isomorphic embeddings of $L_q(0,1)$ into Lorentz--Schatten ideals
Canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction
abstract: We study canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction. For any number of species and any rank of the fast subnetwork, the derivatives that enter the Krupa-Szmolyan conditions and coefficient are rational functions of the fluxes and the reciprocal concentrations. For a fast subnetwork of rank one, the dynamics is planar on stoichiometric classes and these forms are linear in the fluxes, extending our planar flux criterion; the criticality is an explicit cubic. When one species is fast, these forms decompose over the slow species, weighted by their reciprocal concentrations. The elementary-mode criterion then carries over, and the criticality depends on the composition of the slow pool, so one network can explode in either way. The obstruction that the slow flux cannot vanish on the fold is characterised by a Farkas certificate and a yield diagram decided on configurations of at most three reactions. Under four conditions on the critical curve, a canard point with $A\neq0$ unfolded by a rate constant gives the full canard explosion; with one fast species and a fast equation affine in the slow variable, these follow from sign conditions on the reactions and injectivity on the class. For fast subnetworks of higher rank, a centre-manifold reduction adds corrections through the group inverse of the fast Jacobian; in the Oregonator they make both canard points change criticality between its planar reduction and the full model. All results are proved; exact computations and simulations serve as independent checks.

title: Affine Combiners for Reed-Solomon Proximity Gaps
abstract:
Reed-Solomon proximity gaps establish soundness guarantees for protocols that test received words through random combinations. For length-$n$ codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$, classical scalar combiners achieve error $O(n/q)$ in the unique-decoding regime, with larger known bounds near the Johnson radius.
  We prove smaller error bounds using affine combiners, which combine two received words $f,g$ as $f(x)+(α+βx)g(x)$, where $α,β$ are independent uniform elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$. For output degree bound $d=ρn$, fixed $ρ\in(0,1)$ and $0<η<1-\sqrtρ$, and sufficiently large block length $n$, we prove mutual correlated agreement (MCA) with one coordinate of agreement loss at threshold $A=\lceil(\sqrtρ+η)n\rceil$, with error $O_{ρ,η}\left(\frac{1}{q}+\frac{n^2}{q^2}\right)$. The result holds over arbitrary evaluation domains in every finite field, including prime and binary extension fields. The agreement threshold can approach the Johnson threshold, beyond unique decoding.
  For $q\ge n^2$, our error is $O_{ρ,η}(1/q)$, an asymptotic factor-$n$ separation from scalar combiners: we prove that their worst-case MCA error is $Ω_{ρ,η}(n/q)$ at the same agreement threshold and with the same one-coordinate loss. We also prove that affine combiners incur worst-case error $Ω_{ρ,η}(n/q)$ when no agreement loss is allowed. Thus one coordinate of agreement loss is necessary for our guarantee; this relaxation of standard MCA reduces the guaranteed common agreement fraction by at most $1/n$. We also extend the result to $k$-variate Reed-Muller codes on subfield grids, obtaining MCA error $O_{ρ,η,k}(q^{-k})$ for fixed $ρ,η,k$, sufficiently large $n$, and $q\ge n^{k+1}$, with agreement loss $n^{1-1/k}$.

title: Secular Dynamics and the LFL for $β$ Corner Process
abstract: In this paper, we consider the Gaussian $β$ corner process, whose edge particles are known to converge to the Tracy-Widom $β$ law. We study the almost sure behaviour of the extrema of the whole trajectory of the edge particles and establish a law of fractional logarithm (LFL) for the corner process for every fixed $β>0$, extending the previous known results in the case $β=1,2$. Our proof relies on the upward Gamma and downward Dirichlet secular equations, which can be regarded as two discrete dynamics to form the corner processes. The secular dynamics are used in both the correlation estimate and the decorrelation estimate, which are known as two key steps of proving LFL in \cite{BCEHK-LFL} for the Wigner minor process. Especially, in the decorrelation part, they are used as discrete analogues of the continuous Dyson Brownian motion.

title: Hyperexponential Stabilization of Nonholonomic Systems by Oscillating Controls
abstract: We address the problem of designing time-varying feedback controls that stabilize a given equilibrium of a nonholonomic system at a faster than the exponential rate. We consider systems with an arbitrary degree of nonholonomy and prove a theorem on practical hyperexponential stabilization under a suitable assumption on the parameterized dither signals. The convergence proof is based on a comparison equation with a prescribed power of logarithmic terms. We apply this result to stabilize a model of a car with two off-hooked trailers.

title: Lempert and pluricomplex Green functions near non-semipositive boundary points
abstract: We study the two-step Lempert function and the pluricomplex Green function near a non-semipositive boundary point of a bounded domain $D\subset\mathbb{C}^n$. We prove a sharp upper estimate for the two-step Lempert function in terms of the local boundary scale $H_D$, and obtain matching estimates for the pluricomplex Green function. As a consequence, these quantities have the same boundary behaviour as the Kobayashi distance. For the usual Lempert function, we prove an upper estimate of order $\sqrt{H_D}$, which implies the optimal local $1/4$-Hölder estimate, and determine its precise boundary behaviour along the real normal.

title: Higher order schemes for the numerical solution of integro-differential equation-based age-of-infection models with time-dependent contact rates
abstract:
Age-of-infection models, formulated as integro-differential equations (IDEs), provide elegant mathematical descriptions for the spread of infectious diseases. In contrast to ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based models, IDE-based models can accommodate general distributions of transition times between disease stages. Yet, the accurate numerical assessment of the solution of IDE models remains challenging.
  Here, we extend a recently proposed fixed-point method based on Gregory quadrature. We generalize the formulation to time-dependent contact rates whose changes at discrete time points are represented by continuously differentiable sigmoidal interpolants, and suggest additional finite difference approximations to obtain higher-order schemes for susceptible, infected and recovered subpopulations. The resulting numerical schemes achieve convergence orders of two, three and four for all three subpopulations, enabling accurate and flexible simulations of IDE-based epidemic models with general sojourn time distributions and changing contact patterns.

title: The Pólya--Szegő buckling conjecture in dimensions two through forty-seven
abstract: We prove the Pólya--Szegő buckling conjecture in dimensions $2\le n\le47$: among open sets of prescribed finite volume, a ball minimizes the first clamped buckling eigenvalue. More precisely, we establish the sharp comparison $Λ_1\left(Ω\right)\ge \left(j_{n/2,1}/j_{n/2-1,1}\right)^2 λ_1^{\mathrm D}\left(Ω\right)$, where $λ_1^{\mathrm D}$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue and $j_{ν,1}$ is the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_ν$ of the first kind. The proof extends a radial calibration to all Hessian directions; positive coefficient expansions and logarithmically convex Laplace integrals control the resulting matrix. A Lipschitz construction handles sign changes and arbitrary boundaries. Equality in the volume bound holds precisely for balls modulo sets of zero $H^2$ capacity. We prove that this calibration fails in every dimension $n\ge48$.

title: The loop-ensemble scaling limits of near-critical percolation in the plane
abstract: We prove that the collection of all cluster boundaries of near-critical site percolation (with a fixed parameter) on the triangular lattice has a unique scaling limit in the loop-ensemble space, as the mesh size tends to 0. This answers a problem proposed by Camia, Fontes and Newman (2006). Using this, we also prove that near-critical percolation exploration path in a disk converges in distribution to a continuous path as the mesh size goes to 0. The main idea of our proof is to construct the cut-off loop ensembles under the near-critical coupling, based on the enhanced networks and the quad-crossing scaling limits of near-critical percolation constructed by Garban, Pete and Schramm (2018); the proof also relies on the study of the geometry of cluster chains. Some properties of the limiting loop ensemble, including rotation invariance, scale covariance and finite chaining, are established. Moreover, a few applications of our scaling-limit result and proof strategy are discussed.

title: Hybrid Precoding and Combining for O-RAN Massive MIMO Systems
abstract: Recently, the radio access network (RAN) has been reimagined through open RAN (O-RAN) architecture to overcome the limitations of the traditional monolithic, black-box design philosophy and to leverage emerging technologies such as cloud computing, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. Although O-RAN disaggregates the base station (BS) into independent components to enable modular deployment, this paradigm introduces new challenges in signal processing and beamforming. In particular, beamforming in O-RAN must account for fronthaul link (FHL) capacity constraints, coordinated operation of multiple radio units (possibly from different vendors), and resource management, including transmit power allocation. To address these challenges, this work proposes novel beamforming techniques for a downlink multiuser hybrid massive multiple-input multiple-output system, in which hybrid architectures are deployed at both the users and at each BS radio unit. We formulate a sum-rate maximization problem incorporating transmit-power, unit-modulus, and FHL capacity constraints. The proposed algorithm integrates gradient descent and the Lagrange multiplier method to design analog beamformers and digital precoders, respectively, whereas digital combiners are designed to render the received streams parallel to each other. By avoiding computationally intensive operations such as eigenvalue and singular value decompositions, the proposed approach, as evidenced by simulation results, achieves superior performance with moderate computational complexity compared to existing benchmark schemes.

title: The Calderón Problem with Randomly Distributed Resonant Droplets
abstract: We study the recovery of an acoustic coefficient from boundary measurements made after the injection of a collection of small, highly contrasting droplets. This enters into the framework of quantitative ultrasound imaging using contrast agents. The centers are randomly distributed according to a prescribed strictly positive density $ρ\in C^1(\overlineΩ)$. We choose real incident frequencies near an active Newtonian resonance and prove a point-interaction approximation, followed by a comparison with the effective model $(-Δ+P^2ρ-ω^2n^2)u=0$. The constants are uniform as the amplitude $P^2$ increases, provided it is coupled to the size and distribution discrepancy of the droplets. A random rounding and displacement construction verifies the distribution assumption for each such given density. The effective Neumann-to-Dirichlet map is then linearized with a remainder of order $P^{-4}$. We derive reconstruction identities using complex geometrical optics solutions of the known reference operator $-Δ+P^2ρ$. We also estimate the amplification of the boundary-map error in these identities and give a boundary integral correction for reconstruction from the full (and not the linearized) measured map.

title: Moving Cut Loci and Gaussian Fluctuations of Intrinsic Huber Means on Compact Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: Moving cut loci can change the limiting covariance of sample Huber means even when the cut locus of the population mean has probability zero. On a closed connected Riemannian manifold, we prove that the averaged logarithm field is $C^1$ near a point $m$ whenever the sampling law has a continuous density near its cut locus. The result holds for every continuous weight depending only on the observation, and the covariant derivative includes an explicit integral over the regular cut locus. When $m$ is a Huber mean for a fixed positive threshold, assume that the distance to $m$ has no atom at that threshold. The Hessian of the population risk then equals the expected pointwise Hessian minus a positive semidefinite cut locus correction. If $m$ is unique and this Hessian is positive definite, every measurable selection of global minimizers for i.i.d. samples satisfies a tangent-space central limit theorem. The cut loci of points in a ball of radius $δ$ sweep out a region of volume $O(δ)$, uniformly in the centre. These results establish the volume and integrability conditions previously assumed in a central limit theorem for intrinsic Fréchet means. At each fixed centre, the volume measure on this region, divided by $δ$, converges weakly to an explicit measure on the regular cut locus. The Huber correction vanishes exactly when the region swept out about $m$ has probability $o(δ)$.

title: Rayleigh--Taylor instability and Hadamard ill-posedness for the rotating free-boundary Euler equations in three dimensions
abstract: The free-boundary incompressible Euler equations linearized at a rigidly rotating equilibrium on the flat product of the unit disk and a circle are Hadamard ill-posed in Sobolev spaces of order at least two. The equilibrium violates the Taylor sign condition, under which local well-posedness is known. Eulerian linearization retaining free-surface advection reduces the spectral problem to a modified Bessel equation; Rouché's theorem yields an unstable root whose real part grows as the square root of the axial frequency. Eigenmode Sobolev norms grow as the corresponding power of that frequency. Rescaling gives data tending to zero whose solutions are unbounded at any prescribed positive time. At zero axial frequency the analysis recovers Ebin's rotating-disk rate (Communications in Partial Differential Equations 12 (1987), 1175--1201). The product lift gives nonlinear ill-posedness on the invariant class of axially independent data.

title: Strict Monotonicity of the First Positive Steklov Eigenvalue on Eccentric Spherical Shells in Every Dimension
abstract: For $d\ge2$, consider the region between two nested spheres of fixed radii, with the inner sphere translated a distance $\varepsilon$ from the outer center. We prove that the first positive eigenvalue of the Steklov problem, with the spectral boundary condition imposed on both spheres, decreases strictly with $\varepsilon$ throughout the noncontact interval. This settles the planar monotonicity conjecture formulated by Nigam and establishes its higher-dimensional counterparts. In dimension two we use a double-center holomorphic expansion and a pair of positive compact coefficient operators. For every $d\ge3$, solid Gegenbauer harmonics yield analogous axisymmetric and transverse operators, with a positive rank-one monopole correction. Weighted angular-mode comparison for $d\ge3$ and a direct matrix comparison for $d=2$ identify the first positive eigenvalue as the unique level-one crossing of an associated spectral radius. The first eigenspace has dimension $d$ in the concentric case and dimension one for every nonconcentric configuration. Convergence and reconstruction estimates justify the coefficient reductions at the two boundaries.

title: Positivity in symplectic groups and electrical networks
abstract: We study the relation between electrical positivity introduced by Lam and Pylyavskyy $[9]$ and total positivity of symplectic matrices arising from circular planar electrical networks. A particularly convenient framework for our purpose is provided by a construction of an embedding of electrical network into the positive Lagrangian Grassmannian, see Section $1.1$. Employing this technique, we demonstrate that mentioned below two types of positivity do not coincide, see Theorem $2.2$. In Section $3$ we also derive explicit rational formulas recovering the parameters of the factorization from our symplectic matrix entries and minors, and prove uniqueness under explicit nonvanishing conditions.

title: Weight-Adjusted Entropy-Stable BR2 and CDG Viscous Discretizations with Wall Boundary Conditions for Compressible Flows on Curvilinear Grids
abstract: Entropy-stable discontinuous Galerkin schemes are known for their robustness. These schemes satisfy a semi-discrete entropy inequality, mimicking the entropy inequality of the continuous governing equations. Entropy-stable viscous discretizations with entropy-stable wall boundary conditions have been used in the literature, using a scheme similar to BR1. On the other hand, viscous discretizations with compact stencil, such as BR2 and CDG schemes, are more efficient for computation and for forming the Jacobian. Moreover, it is known that the weight-adjusted formulations have better efficiency with regard to the computational and storage costs. To that end, we derive the weight-adjusted entropy-stable BR2 and CDG schemes with modifications for the numerical flux at the boundary to account for the entropy-stable boundary conditions.

title: Rigidity of time changes of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flows on finite volume quotients
abstract: We study the rigidity phenomenon of the time changed unipotent flows on general Lie groups. Under some spectral gap assumptions, we prove that every ergodic nonsplitting $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow on a finite volume quotient space $\mathbf{G}/Γ$ is time changed rigid. We also prove that for $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow, the splitting condition is equivalent to loosely Kroneckerness. Our result in particular applies to $\mathbf{G}=\mathbf{S}\ltimes\mathbf{N}$, where $\mathbf{S}$ is the identity component of a real semisimple linear algebraic group without compact factors and $\mathbf{N}$ is simply connected and connected nilpotent Lie group. These are extensions of [KVW21,LW25].

title: Dual reflection groups of graded Ore extensions
abstract: We prove that the Artin--Schelter Gorenstein and Artin--Schelter regular properties descend from a graded Ore extension to its coefficient algebra, for every twisting automorphism and every skew derivation. We then determine the dual reflection groups of graded Ore extensions for all gradings compatible with the Ore structure. They are exactly the semidirect products of a dual reflection group of the coefficient algebra by the cyclic group generated by the degree of the new variable, meeting it trivially, and a nonzero skew derivation never contributes a new degree. For iterated Ore extensions we characterize the dual reflection groups by an order formula analogous to the theorem of Shephard, Todd and Chevalley, and we prove the binomial conjecture of Buzaglo and Rogalski for these algebras. We show that their covariant rings are complete intersections of growth type, whose Ext-algebras grow like a polynomial ring in as many variables as there are generators of nontrivial degree. This answers a question of Kirkman, Kuzmanovich and Zhang for these algebras. Finally, we describe the smash product as a Cayley quiver with relations, factor its matrix Hilbert series, and show that the extension becomes Hopf--Galois once the Jacobian is inverted.

title: Meta-Nested Recurrences
abstract: We study recurrences in which a previous sequence value determines the number of iterations of an inner map. Campbell's example has an explicit power-of-three formula and inner orbits of eventual period at most two. Its normalized lower and upper limits are $2/5$ and $3/4$. For a variable-depth Conway recurrence $C$, we prove the golden-ratio lower bound, its exact equality set, a Fibonacci upper cap, and the landing of the inner orbit at every Fibonacci index $F_k$ with $k\ge6$. These proofs are elementary and start from twenty-four initial values. The plateau of $C$ to the left of $F_k$ has width exactly $\lfloor(2k-9)/3\rfloor$, and $C(F_k+t)=F_{k-1}+t$ for $0\le t\le\lfloor(k-8)/6\rfloor$. A maximum principle turns a finite exact computation into the bound $\limsup C(n)/n<0.65446923$. We characterize the convergence of $C(n)/n$ to $α=(\sqrt5-1)/2$ in terms of negative selected orbit jumps and of a limiting convex profile, and we derive entropy and variance budgets for the recursive splits. Along inverse rays of the map $x\mapsto C(x)$, the relative errors are absolutely summable and the growth is asymptotically Fibonacci. For Grytczuk's fixed-depth recurrence, we give a Pascal-word proof of convergence with the sharp error order $n/\sqrt{\log n}$ along interval maxima. The full variable-depth limit remains open.

title: A negative answer to the final question in "Les petits cailloux"
abstract: We consider polynomial-time computation over arbitrary structures, with unit cost for the primitive operations and relations and with nondeterministic witnesses consisting of arbitrary structure elements. We prove that every finite-signature structure with two distinct available elements and containing a binary operation $*$ and total unary operations $L,R$ such that $L(x*y)=x$ and $R(x*y)=y$ satisfies $P\ne NP$. The proof encodes an exponentially long computation in one element. An incorrect transition has a polynomial-size binary address, and hence the existence of an error is an $NBP$ problem. Existence of a correct accepting trace belongs to the mixed second level $Σ_2^{S,B}$, with an arbitrary-element existential block followed by a binary universal block. We obtain $EXP\subseteqΣ_2^{S,B}\subseteq PH$. A hypothetical equality $P=NP$ would collapse this hierarchy to $P$ and imply $P=EXP$, contradicting a direct deterministic diagonalization over the same structure. A simulation by function graphs extends the obstruction to every jointly injective binary primitive under the same assumptions on equality and available elements. Consequently no unary predicate on Malcev's free binary-tree algebra yields $P=NP$, with or without the projections. In contrast, starting from the author's unary example, we construct five infinite structures with binary operations and $P=NP$. These include an algebra with one binary operation and one constant, an expansion with an associative rectangular-band operation, and an algebra with one binary operation whose every row and column has infinite image.

title: Space-Filling Hypersurfaces
abstract: We seek space-filling hypersurfaces of a projective space over a finite field. They are hypersurfaces contain all rational points. The main goal is to construct a smooth space-filling hypersurface of minimal degree. For each projective space over a finite field, we find a lower bound of the minimum degree of space-filling hypersurface, and construct an example without any singular rational points. Finally, over an odd-dimensional projective space or for fields of characteristic two, we provide a construction of a smooth space-filling hypersurface of minimal degree.

title: Minimizing Monotone Norms in Fractional Load Balancing
abstract:
We devise a fully polynomial time approximation scheme for minimizing a monotone norm $\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert$ over a convex set $X\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$. We study the multi-customer setting, where $X=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$ and the solution set $X_i\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$ is given by a linear minimization oracle for each customer $i$. Our algorithm computes, for any given $\varepsilon>0$, a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximate solution. With high probability, it uses $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( \varepsilon^{-2}(n+d) \right)$ single-customer linear minimization oracle calls and the same number of generalized KL projections to the dual space $Y=\{y\in \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}: \left\lVert y \right\rVert^* \le 1\}$. We assume no prior knowledge on $X$, and our running time depends only on $n$, $d$, and $\varepsilon$. Our result is robust in the sense that it allows for approximate linear minimization oracles and approximate KL projections. We show that the (approximate) KL projection can be performed efficiently for large classes of monotone norms, demonstrating the applicability of our approach.
  While such a result (with exact projection) is well-known for the $\ell_{\infty}$ norm via multiplicative weight updates and was recently obtained for ordered norms via a smooth norm approximation and a novel randomization, existing techniques do not extend to general monotone norms. In particular, a key feature used in previous proofs was dual price stability, which was derived from a global contraction property of the KL projection to the dual space $Y$. We show that this property does not extend to general monotone norms. Therefore, we use a different price mechanism, based on the well-known mirror descent paradigm, for which a local contraction property holds and guarantees stability.

title: Energy rigidity and weak--strong uniqueness for the anisotropic Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^2_+$
abstract: In this paper, we study the two-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with only horizontal dissipation in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{R}^2_+$. The combination of the missing directional regularity and the influence of the boundary presents an essential difficulty for the pressure estimates. We circumvent this difficulty by establishing an extension theorem for the weak formulation, based on the divergence-free condition and the homogeneous impermeability boundary condition. A key feature of this extension principle is that no boundary condition is required for the tangential velocity component. Consequently, every weak solution in the natural energy class on $\mathbb{R}^2_+$ admits a reflection extension that is a weak solution of the corresponding whole-space problem on $\mathbb{R}^2$. This extension allows us to transfer the energy rigidity and weak--strong uniqueness properties established by Demmel and Wiedemann \cite{E-W} to the half-plane setting. In particular, we prove the energy equality for weak solutions in the natural energy class and establish weak--strong uniqueness under the corresponding additional regularity assumptions.

title: Newton's Method and Policy Iterations for Viscous Hamilton--Jacobi Equations
abstract: We study Newton's method for the Cauchy problem for viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equations with Hamiltonians that need not be convex. Each Newton step solves a linear parabolic equation obtained by linearizing the equation at the current iterate. We prove that the iterates converge geometrically in \(L^\infty\) from any initial guess satisfying the initial condition, and quadratically in the parabolic Hölder space \(C^{2+α,1+α/2}\) from initial guesses close to the solution. When the Hamiltonian admits a control representation, the Newton iterates coincide with those of classical policy iteration, which therefore inherits both convergence rates. We extend the local quadratic convergence to uniformly parabolic fully nonlinear equations. For small viscosity, we introduce a Nash--Moser variant that smooths the iterate and the residual in space, and we give a convergence criterion with constants independent of the viscosity. Finally, we show how computable residuals certify the error of inexact Newton corrections computed with physics-informed neural networks.

title: A high-order recombination algorithm with adaptive scale selection for weak approximation of stochastic differential equations
abstract:
High-order recombination keeps weak approximation trees of diffusions small
  by a moment-preserving reduction of the measure on each patch of nodes.
  The weighted Litterer--Lyons (WLL) test of Ninomiya and Shinozaki
  sets the patch scale using a scalar \(λ>0\) chosen
  beforehand, whose appropriate value depends on coordinate units.
  First, the anisotropically weighted Litterer--Lyons (AWLL) rule
  selects the scale during recombination within a bounded factor of
  the measured increment amplitude. On a fixed set of nodes, expanding
  coordinate units leaves the AWLL patch-count bound unchanged but raises
  the WLL lower bound as a power until saturation. In Heston and shifted Stochastic-Alpha-Beta-Rho (sSABR)
  systems with initial price or forward rate 100, AWLL reduces
  the terminal supports of WLL with \(λ=1\) by factors of 137 and
  1488 at comparable errors, but enlarges them at smaller Heston initial
  prices. Second, \(λ\) is extended to a positive definite matrix
  with a joint error bound for prices and sensitivities, a bound on
  the gain of its shape, and patch-count bounds. Third, the elimination stage of batched basis
  exchange requires \(O(J)\)
  arithmetic operations for \(J\) nodes at fixed moment rank and panel width, against
  \(Θ(J^{3})\) for the direct kernel update of Ninomiya and Shinozaki.

title: Sampled resolvents of $C_0$-semigroups: aliasing and sharp rates on the Crandall-Pazy scale
abstract: For a $C_0$-semigroup $(S_t)$ with generator $B$, sampling the Laplace integral $(λ-B)^{-1}=\int_0^\infty e^{-λt}S_t\,dt$ on the grid $T\mathbb{N}$ gives $Q_T=T(I-e^{-λT}S_T)^{-1}$, the impulse-invariant discretization of the resolvent. The motivation is a dyadic series of Castillo, Costin and Costin for the resolvent of a self-adjoint operator: its partial sums are exactly $Q_{2^{-N}}$, so the series is a telescoped rectangle rule. By Poisson summation, on $D(B)$ the error of $Q_T$ is the scalar $T/2$ plus the symmetric limit of the resolvents at the alias points $λ-2πin/T$, $n\ne0$, and the dyadic levels remove these aliases according to the $2$-adic valuation of $n$. Our main result is a sharp scale of rates for the trapezoid correction $Q_T-\frac T2I$. If $(S_t)$ belongs to the Crandall--Pazy class with parameter $α\in(0,1]$, that is $\|BS_t\|=O(t^{-1/α})$ as $t\to0$, the error is $O(T^α)$ in operator norm, $O(T^{α+θ})$ on the interpolation space of order $θ$ between $X$ and $D(B)$, and $O(T^{1+α})$ on $D(B)$, the last requiring only resolvent decay of order $α$ along the line $\mathrm{Re}\, z=\mathrm{Re}\,λ$. This interpolates between unitary groups with unbounded generator ($α=0$, no convergence in norm) and analytic semigroups ($α=1$), and every exponent is attained. For smooth data an Euler--Maclaurin expansion justifies Romberg extrapolation. For self-adjoint generators we give closed forms for the contribution of each dyadic level to Stone's formula, and we translate the results into an explicit error bound and step-size rule for Green functions computed from sampled autocorrelations. Experiments, including a structurally damped string whose semigroup is of Gevrey class, confirm the rates.

title: Strictly Deza Graphs among the Prime Graphs of Solvable Groups
abstract: We study strictly Deza graphs that occur as prime graphs of finite solvable groups and admit a partition into two cliques. Using Gruber's characterization of the prime graphs of finite solvable groups, we relate this problem to bipartite $(0,2)$-graphs. We first show that a non-complete regular graph with a partition into two cliques has equal parts. For a graph of diameter two, writing $F$ for its $c$-regular complement on $2m$ vertices, the Deza condition is equivalent to every component of $F$ being a bipartite $(0,2)$-graph. Within this class, strongly regular graphs occur exactly when $c=1$; we give elementary descriptions for $c=2$ and $c=3$, and translate the existing classification of bipartite $(0,2)$-graphs of valency at most eight. A counting argument yields $m\ge1+c(c-1)/2$, with equality corresponding to biplanes. These observations recover the ten feasible parameter pairs for $m\le7$ without enumeration and give infinite families of strictly Deza prime graphs. We also exhibit a known eight-vertex strictly Deza graph whose complement is triangle-free and three-colourable but not bipartite, showing that clique cover number three occurs.

title: Integers with many divisors in a dyadic interval
abstract: We find the correct order of magnitude for the number of $n\leq x$ having at least $r$ divisors in the interval $(y,2y]$, uniformly in a wide range of the parameters $x,y,r$.

title: Every rank-three matroid is Z-Rayleigh
abstract: We prove that every matroid of rank or corank at most three is $Z$-Rayleigh: its multivariate Tutte polynomial satisfies the Rayleigh inequalities for every positive weighting and every parameter $0<q\le1$. This settles a conjecture of Mani and answers the rank-$3$ spanning-correlation question of Cocks and the correlated-matroid question of Semple and Welsh. For simple rank-$3$ matroids, we obtain an explicit decomposition of each spanning-set Rayleigh difference into the corresponding basis Rayleigh difference, positively weighted squares, and a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients. A second identity compares the normalized multivariate Tutte Rayleigh difference with $(1-q)^2$ times the spanning-set difference, with a remainder of the form $q(1-q)R(q,x)$, where $R$ has nonnegative coefficients. The proof uses the bipartite incidence graph of the lines through two fixed elements and Wagner's theorem that rank-$3$ matroids are basis-Rayleigh. The rank bound is sharp, since a rank-four matroid can fail even the basis Rayleigh inequalities.

title: Independent sets in regular uniform hypergraphs
abstract: We prove that, for all integers $r\ge 2$ and $d\ge 1$, every finite simple $d$-regular $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ on $n$ vertices satisfies \[ \operatorname{ind}(H)\le \operatorname{ind}(H_d^r)^{n/(rd)}, \] with equality if and only if $H$ is a disjoint union of copies of $H_d^r$. Here $\operatorname{ind}(G)$ denotes the number of independent sets in $G$, and $ H_d^r$ is the $d$-regular $r$-partite $r$-graph on $rd$ vertices obtained by taking all $r$-sets consisting of one vertex from a fixed $d$-vertex set and one of $d$ pairwise disjoint $(r-1)$-sets partitioning the remaining vertices. This settles the conjecture of Balogh, Bollobás and Narayanan, who proved the bound for quasi-bipartite hypergraphs.

title: On JT boundary algebras
abstract: We construct the canonical boundary algebras of Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity coupled to free bosonic matter. For a nonempty finite or countable family of species with lowest weights greater than one half, the two boundary algebras are mutual commutants and nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_\infty$ factors. Their nonzero finite corners are nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. The construction uses bounded heat-regularized fields and a Hilbert algebra, which gives a faithful normal semifinite trace without a path-integral argument. The weight restriction is sharp: elementary point fields remain unbounded after positive heat regularization when $0<d\leq1/2$. For one massless scalar, specified bounded observables and normal states have a high energy limit described by a hyperfinite continuous core. We explain why this limit does not preserve the nonhyperfiniteness of the exact algebra.

title: Specializations of frozen variables for Grassmannian cluster algebra
abstract: The homogeneous coordinate ring of a Grassmannian variety $\mathrm{Gr}_{k,n}$ is equipped with a structure of a cluster algebra. The frozen variables are identified with the Plücker coordinates corresponding to length-$k$ segments of ${\mathbb Z}_n$. We study two families of algebras: the first family is obtained by specializing all the frozen variables and the second corresponds to the specialization of the nonwrapping variables. We construct flat bases in both families and study their affine spectra. The special fibers of the families are cones over projective varieties. We identify the irreducible components of these projective varieties with certain positroid varieties.

title: Geometric structure of Green currents for holomorphic correspondences on projective surfaces
abstract: Let $f$ be a holomorphic correspondence on a complex projective surface $X$ such that $f^{-1}$ is also holomorphic. Assume that the action of $f^*$ on cohomology is simple and that the dynamical degrees of $f$ satisfy $d_1>\max\{d_0,d_2\}$. We prove that the Green currents $T^\pm$ associated with $f$ are woven. We also provide a large family of examples of holomorphic correspondences satisfying our assumptions, obtained as generic complete intersections in $X\times X$.

title: Constructing option portfolio
abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of constructing a portfolio composed of a set of financial options. We present a mixed-integer linear program. We apply our approach to index options for the S&P 500.

title: Lax Centers and Monoidal Functors for Comodule Categories Associated with Acyclic Quivers
abstract: In this paper, we study the monoidal category of finite-dimensional right comodules over the path algebra $\Bbbk Q$ of a finite acyclic quiver $Q$, equipped with the weak bialgebra structure in which every path is grouplike. We prove that the lax center of this category is monoidally equivalent to $\operatorname{Rep}^{\mathrm{fd}}_{\Bbbk}(Q)$, the category of finite-dimensional representations of $Q$. We also classify all $\Bbbk$-linear strong monoidal functors between any two such comodule categories, and all monoidal natural transformations between them. For the right adjoint of such a functor, we determine when the left or right projection formula holds. When both projection formulas hold, this adjoint will induce a functor between the lax centers, and we describe the induced functor explicitly on quiver representations.

title: Newforms as test vectors for representations of Saito-Kurokawa type
abstract: We study irreducible (admissible) representations $π$ of the split group $G_n=SO(2n+1)$, both over finite and $p$-adic fields, which are distinguished for the (unramified) nonsplit form of $K_n=SO(2n)$ and for one more subgroup $H_n$. Over finite fields, $H_n$ is the split $SO(2n)$ while over $p$-adic fields it is the Gross-Tsai paramodular subgroup (of minimal level for $π$). These are all multiplicity one situations. With $0 \neq \ell_{n,K} \in {\rm Hom}_{K_n}(π_n,1)$ and $0 \neq v_{n,H} \in π_n^{H_n}$, both being one dimensional spaces, we are interested in the vanishing/nonvanishing of $|\ell_{n,K}(v_{n,H})|^2$. Appropriately normalized, this defines the notion of the correlation coefficient $c(π;H_n,K_n)$ of $H_n$ and $K_n$ in $G_n$ with respect to $π$. Via the theta correspondence between ${\rm SL}(2)$ (or ${\rm Mp}(2)$), we establish a bijection $π_n \leftrightarrow π_1$ between representations of $G_n$ and $G_1$ under consideration. Our main results then prove that $d_n c(π_n;H_n,K_n)$ is independent of the rank $n$, where $d_n =\dim π_n$ for finite fields and is defined in terms of the index of $H_n$ in the standard maximal compact subgroup of $G_n$ in the $p$-adic case. We also highlight a conjecture from [Ana25] on Legendre polynomials modulo $p$. Its truth will have the arithmetic consequence that over $\mathbb F_p$, given $π_1$, we can choose $u \in \mathbb F_p$ such that, in every rank $n$, all the correlation coefficients $c(π_n;H_n,u_nK_n u_n^{-1})$ are simultaneously nonzero and moreover they belong to $\mathbb Z_p^\times$ under any identification $\mathbb C \simeq \overline{\mathbb Q}_p$, where $u_n$ is a specific unipotent element in $G_n$ corresponding to $u$.

title: Semigroups with periodic complex-time boundedness and holomorphy regions
abstract: We study the periodicity of complex-time boundedness and holomorphy domains of operator semigroups. We show that an imaginary-time covariance identity involving an isometry yields periodicity of these domains. The method is applied to the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator and the hypoelliptic Laplacian on the circle, providing a spectral explanation of periodicity independent of the explicit geometry of their boundedness regions. We also discuss the distinction between boundedness and contractivity, using the classical heat semigroup as an example.

title: Escaping the Curse of Dimensionality in One-Step Flow-Based Generative Models
abstract: Flow and diffusion-based generative models achieve state-of-the-art quality, but require multiple forward passes at inference time, making them computationally costly. Consistency models overcome this by learning a flow map directly, enabling few-step generation and dramatically reducing the computation needed at test time. However, formal statistical guarantees for such one-step generators are scarce. Existing results either suffer from the curse of dimensionality or rely on impractical loss functions. We investigate whether one-step flow-based models can escape the curse of dimensionality under the assumption that the data distribution is generated by a low-dimensional surface perturbed with Gaussian noise. In this setup, we derive approximation and generalization error bounds for the flow map estimate that circumvent the curse of dimensionality. Our findings provide the first principled explanation for practical success of one-step flow-based generative models.

title: Strongly reducible operators in factors
abstract: Let $\mathcal M$ be a factor acting on a separable complex Hilbert space. For every operator $T$ in $\mathcal M$ with dense generalized kernel and $T^2\ne 0$, we characterize the strong reducibility of $T$ relative to $\mathcal M$ based on a $3\times 3$ asymmetric matrix representation of $T$. As applications, we obtain criteria for the strong reducibility of algebraic operators in finite factors and type $\mathrm{III}$ factors. We also prove that every Hilbert space operator with an infinite-dimensional multicyclic direct summand is similar to an irreducible operator.

title: Generic equivariant simplicity of the spectrum of Laplace-type operators with finite symmetry
abstract: We prove that for generic elements in three natural families of Laplace-type differential operators on smooth manifolds, which are equivariant with respect to a finite symmetry group, all the eigenspaces are irreducible representations. In other words, the spectrum of these operators is generically equivariantly simple. The three families of operators with symmetry are Schrödinger operators parametrized by the potential, going back to the work of Wigner, Laplace-Beltrami operators parametrized by invariant Riemannian metrics and conformal Laplacians parametrized by invariant metrics in a given conformal class. The latter two results extend prior work of Zelditch for certain free group actions and resolve, for finite group actions, a well-known open question raised by Guillemin and Yau.
