Our approach stems from methods developed by Wendl and Doan-Walpuski to address equivariant transversality in symplectic topology.

title: A short route to Diening's averaging criterion in spaces of homogeneous type
abstract: We present a short, self-contained proof of the averaging-operator criterion for the boundedness of the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on variable Lebesgue spaces over unbounded spaces of homogeneous type. Building on techniques of Diening and Lerner, we establish a Jensen-type inequality with uniformly summable error, from which the criterion follows directly via a Calderón-Zygmund argument.

title: Asymptotically Optimal Bounds for Counting Near-Minimum Circuits in Regular Matroids
abstract: For a regular matroid on $m$ elements with positive weights and weighted girth $g_w$, we prove that the number of circuits of weight at most $αg_w$ is bounded by $(Km)^{2α}$, for every real $α\ge1$ and an absolute constant $K$. This improves the previous $m^{O(α^2)}$ bound of Gurjar and Vishnoi and matches classic graph cut and cycle counting bounds of Karger and Subramanian. We also show this is asymptotically optimal for all real $α\geq 1$ under the Erdős girth conjecture, while unconditional optimality holds for half-integer $α$ by prior results. As consequences, we resolve a recent conjecture by Khanna, Putterman, and Song implying the existence of a parallel basis search algorithm for regular matroids terminating in logarithmically many rounds of independence queries, and obtain improved bounds on the number of near-minimum weight codewords in regular codes and near-shortest vectors in totally unimodular lattices under $\ell_p$-norms.

title: Optimization of Finite Alphabet Message Passing Decoding on Fully Node-Parallel Architectures for 5G LDPC Codes
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel design method for the lookup tables (LUTs) of the minimum reconstruction, computation, and quantization (min-RCQ) LDPC code decoding algorithm. The proposed design method uses Bayesian optimization and samples from a subspace of the design space. The novel design method does not require knowledge about the channel or the modulation format and uses the frame error rate (FER) as loss function. The design method is applicable to irregular low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes with puncturing and shortening. Furthermore, the design method creates a set of iteration-agnostic LUTs that can be used over all iterations, which makes this approach suitable for fully node-parallel decoder architectures. We show that our proposed approach achieves a 38.6 % better energy efficiency than a state-of-the-art normalized min-sum (NMS) decoder without loss in error correction performance.

title: An Empirical Square-Root Law for the Degree Discrepancy of Binary m-Sequences
abstract: Let $k\ge 2$, $N=2^k$, $M=N-1$ and let $Δ(r)$ be the range, over all starting offsets, of the total-variation degree discrepancy of a length-$r$ window of a primitive binary linear feedback shift register (LFSR) of period $M$. Degree-discrepancy profiles for every $k\le 28$ support the scaling $\max_r Δ(r)=Θ(\sqrt{N})=Θ(2^{k/2})$. The tabulated peaks are maxima on a discrete grid, hence lower bounds on the exhaustive maximum. The normalized peaks $d_k=\max_{r\in R_k}Δ(r)/2^{k/2}$ oscillate between values near 1/2 and values that approach, but do not exceed, 1. The data suggest $\liminf d_k=1/2$ and $\limsup d_k\le 1$. We conjecture the same square-root law for the exhaustive maximum, with those normalized envelopes. A Brownian-bridge heuristic accounts for the square-root scale. The same profiles do not place the recorded maximizer at mid-path: after folding by the complement identity $Δ(M-r)=Δ(r)$, the median of $\min(ρ^*_k,1-ρ^*_k)$ is 0.35, and several $k$ (notably 16 and 28) peak on a short window. Mid-horizon $Δ$ remains a large fraction of the peak, so the square-root scale can still come from a Brownian-bridge envelope. The same range has two readings of the starting offset: a pairing fragment in serial-knockout scheduling, and a change to the plaintext on an LFSR orbit. The location of the maximizer is not part of the conjecture. Open questions that separate the conjecture from a theorem are listed.

title: Categorical orbifold theory
abstract: We investigate the orbifold theory for condensable algebras in fusion categories $\mathcal{C}$. We prove that the algebra automorphism group of a condensable algebra $A$ is finite and explicitly characterize its elements in terms of the fusion action and indecomposable $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$-bimodule decomposition of $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. We further show that a finite group action on $A$ gives rise to a group extension of the category $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$ in $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. Conversely, every such group extension arises from a finite group of algebra automorphisms of $A$. Finally, we also construct a canonical maximal group extension of $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$, thereby providing a categorical framework for the classical correspondence among finite group actions, fixed-point algebras, and twisted modules.

title: Density of periodic measures on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ with prescribed arithmetic information
abstract: Let $F$ be the diagonal flow on the modular space $X_2$, and let $\mathcal{S}_f$ be the set of positive square-free numbers, which is identified with the set of all real quadratic fields via the natural map $d\mapsto \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt d)$. In this paper, we prove that, for any finite subset $A\subseteq\mathcal{S}_f$, there exists a density-zero set $B\subseteq\mathcal{S}_f\setminus A$ such that the set of all $F$-periodic measures with associated quadratic fields from $B$ is dense in the set of all $F$-invariant measures on $X_2$.

title: Splitting Number at Singular Cardinals
abstract: We study the splitting number at singular cardinals with emphasis on what we call the reduction to the cofinality problem: whether $\mathfrak{s}_κ = \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(κ)}$ holds for a singular cardinal $κ$. Our main tool is the transfinite logarithm function $\mathrm{log}_{2}(μ) := \min \{ λ\in \mathrm{card} \colon μ\leq 2^λ \}$ defined for every infinite cardinal $μ$. We prove that the reduction holds, and in fact $\mathfrak{s}_κ = \mathrm{log}_{2}(\mathrm{cf}(κ))$, whenever $\mathrm{cf}(κ)$ is uncountable and not weakly compact. When $\mathrm{cf}(κ) = \aleph_{0}$, we show that $\mathfrak{s}_κ = \mathfrak{s}$ provided that $\mathfrak{s} \leq \log_{2}(κ)$, while the failure of the reduction is consistent with $\mathrm{ZFC}$. When $\mathrm{cf}(κ)$ is weakly compact, we use a model constructed by Ben-Neria and Gitik to prove that, under suitable large cardinals hypothesis, $\mathfrak{s}_κ < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(κ)}$ is consistent. Furthermore, we show that the consistency strength of $\mathrm{ZFC} \, +$"$\exists κ\in \mathrm{card} [\mathrm{cf}(κ) > \aleph_{0} \wedge \mathfrak{s}_κ < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(κ)}]$'' is at least that of the negation of the singular cardinal hypothesis. Finally, we study the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}_κ$, extending several results about the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}$ to the uncountable setting. In particular, we show in $\mathrm{ZFC}$ that there are regular cardinals $κ$ such that $\mathfrak{s}_κ$ is singular, partially answering an open question posed by Fischer and Soukup.

title: Quasicentral modulus for almost normal operators
abstract: In 1984, Voiculescu conjectured that the Hilbert--Schmidt quasicentral modulus vanishes for every almost normal operator. We prove this conjecture.

title: Semi-log canonical minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces
abstract:
We prove the existence of certain steps of the minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces in the semi-log canonical case, generalizing results of Ambro and Kollár. This is obtained by providing a sufficient criterion for the finite generation of the relative log canonical algebra. As a consequence, we prove demi-normal analogues of results of Hacon--Xu and Birkar. As a further application, we derive the existence of crepant semi-dlt modifications of analytic slc pairs whose irreducible components are normal in codimension 1, extending a result of Hashizume.
  The methods are new even in the algebraic case, providing streamlined proofs of the algebraic counterparts to the statements proved in this work, without relying on Kollár's gluing techniques.

title: Normality in generalized Rudin spaces
abstract: In \cite{Kojman2026}, Kojman generalized Mary Ellen Rudin's construction of a ZFC Dowker space to larger cardinals and gave a pcf-theoretic condition ensuring that the resulting spaces are collectionwise normal. A subsequent manuscript by Eisworth, Kojman, Lambie-Hanson, and Marun \cite{EKLM2026} develops the theory further and leaves open whether these generalized Rudin spaces can fail to be normal. We answer this question by proving that, for cardinals $μ<δ$ with $\operatorname{cf}(δ)=\aleph_0$, the generalized Rudin space $X(μ,δ)$ is normal if and only if $\operatorname{pp}(ν)<δ$ for every cardinal $ν\in(μ,δ)$ with $\operatorname{cf}(ν)=\aleph_0$. Given this characterization, known consistency results provide consistent examples of nonnormal generalized Rudin spaces.

title: Second homology of some quandles
abstract: We derive formulas from Eisemann's formula for the second quandle homology of quandles. We prove that for a finite injective quandle $Q$, the second quandle homology $H_2(Q)$ can be computed in a representation group of $Q$, which is a finite quotient of the enveloping group of $Q$, by giving a formula for that. We use this to compute $H_2(Q)$ for $Q$ the subquandle of $k$-cycles of $S_n$ and $Q$ the quandle corresponding to the conjugacy class of a diagonalizable element of $SL(n,q)$, with some exceptions. For $G$ a finite group with trivial Bogomolov multiplier, as many classical groups, simple groups and (with exceptions) quasi-simple groups, we derive a formula for $H_2(Conj(G))$ that can be computed in $G$ alone. The formula relies on conjugacy classes of $G$, centralizers in $G$ of representative of such classes and the derived group of $G$. If $G$ is moreover perfect this formula can be related to the first Hochschild homology of the group ring $\mathbb{Z}[G]$. As an application, we compute $H_2(Q)$ for $Q$ the conjugacy quandle of $GL(2,q)$ for $q\neq 2,3$.

title: Adaptive linear quadratic optimal control for discrete-time stochastic systems
abstract: In this paper, we consider the adaptive linear quadratic optimal control problem for a class of discrete-time stochastic systems, where the system matrix pair $(A,B)$ is unknown and the state weighting matrix $Q$ in the cost function is not necessarily positive semidefinite. Our proposed adaptive optimal control only assumes that the corresponding algebraic Riccati equation has a stabilizing solution, which weakens the standard controllable and observable assumptions used in the literature. To address this problem, we modify a weighted least squares algorithm by incorporating a random regularization method, which ensures the uniform stabilizability of the family of estimated models. Additionally, a diminishing excitation is introduced in the design of the proposed adaptive control to guarantee the strong consistency of the desired components of the estimates. Finally, by leveraging this family of estimates and employing a suitable switching method, we demonstrate that a certainty equivalence control with such a diminishing excitation is an optimal adaptive control.

title: Boij-S"oderberg and Harder-Narasimhan polygons of vector bundles on projective space
abstract: Eisenbud and Schreyer proved that the cohomology table of a vector bundle $F$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ is a unique positive combination of supernatural tables along a chain of root sequences. The slopes of the pieces, weighted by their ranks, form a concave polygon $Ψ_F$, the Boij-Söderberg polygon, with the same endpoints as the Harder-Narasimhan polygon $P_F$. We prove that $P_F\leqΨ_F$, in any characteristic, by testing subsheaves against sheaves with pure resolutions on thickened lines; the bound is optimal among bounds depending only on the ray of the table. The chain majorizes every other supernatural decomposition, and $Ψ$ is monotone under cancellations, hence upper semicontinuous in flat families. The comparison extends to coherent sheaves and, by linear projection, to sheaves of positive dimension. On $\mathbb{P}^2$ the defect is a sum of four cohomological terms; we characterize equality and show that the inequality survives the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability. For a smooth projective variety $X$ of dimension $n\geq2$ in characteristic zero, with $H$ ample and base-point-free, the mean normalized squared spread $G(\mathcal{E})$ of the roots in the cohomology table of every vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies $G(\mathcal{E})\geq(K_X^2-2c_2(X))\cdot H^{n-2}/((n+1)H^n)$, a bound independent of $\mathcal{E}$. Since $G(\mathcal{E})=1$ exactly for arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay bundles, when this bound exceeds $1$ it is a uniform form of their absence.

title: Counting eigenvalues below the lowest Landau level Robin Dirichlet boundary conditions in an annulus
abstract: We study a charged quantum particle confined to an annulus and subject to a strong uniform magnetic field. A Dirichlet condition is imposed on the inner boundary and a Robin condition on the outer boundary. We are interested in the number of bound states whose energy lies below the lowest Landau level, the threshold set by the magnetic field in the whole plane. In the semiclassical regime, we derive an asymptotic formula for this number. It shows how the count depends on the geometry of the annulus, through the length and curvature of the outer boundary, and on the strength of the Robin parameter. We treat both the repulsive and the attractive cases of the Robin condition and describe how the attractive case changes the boundary behavior that produces these low-lying states. The proof reduces the problem to an effective one-dimensional model near the outer boundary and relies on separation of variables in angular momentum.

title: Intersections, Equations, and Singularities of Lissajous Varieties
abstract: Lissajous varieties are affine algebraic varieties parametrized by sine and cosine functions. They generalize algebraic Lissajous curves in the plane to higher dimensions by applying a component-wise trigonometric map to a rational affine subspace and are motivated by applications in dynamical systems (Kuramoto model) and semidefinite optimization (graph elliptopes). We establish several algebraic and geometric properties of Lissajous varieties. In particular, we show that intersections of Lissajous varieties are finite unions of such varieties and describe them explicitly. We investigate algebraic properties of the defining polynomials of Lissajous hypersurfaces and describe the singular locus of Lissajous varieties.

title: Ideal polyhedral surfaces with prescribed cusped hyperbolic metric and their degeneration
abstract: Rivin showed that every cusped hyperbolic metric on a punctured sphere is uniquely realized by a convex ideal polyhedron in hyperbolic space with possible degeneration. We consider the analogous problem for cusped hyperbolic metrics on a punctured surface of positive genus: locally convex ideal polyhedral surfaces in hyperbolic space. Each such surface determines a complex projective structure on the underlying closed surface. With a cusped hyperbolic metric $h$ prescribed, we investigate the space $\mathcal{P}(h)$ of such ideal polyhedral realizations and their possible degeneration. Particularly in the case of tori, we show that the space $\mathcal{P}(h)$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^2$, and that the induced map to Teichmüller space of the closed torus is a $C^1$-embedding. This map extends to a bijection from the closure of $\mathcal{P}(h)$ onto the whole Teichmüller space, where the added points are degenerate surfaces. This is dual to the Kojima-Mizushima-Tan conjecture about circle patterns on closed surfaces with complex projective structures.

title: Critical L-values and genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants
abstract: We establish a period comparison for a two-dimensional rational Hodge summand of type $(3,0)+(0,3)$ in a smooth projective threefold over $\mathbb Q$ with $h^{3,0}=1$. Given an algebraic projector onto the summand and a correspondence whose action on the motive of a rational weight-four newform is nonzero after projection to the summand, restriction to the holomorphic de Rham lines identifies motivic morphisms with maps between these lines. Fixing rational generators of the holomorphic de Rham lines determines a unique isomorphism of homological motives. Its Betti realization then yields an exact relation between geometric periods and two critical modular $L$-values. For the Fermat sextic, we construct the correspondence over $\mathbb Q$ and compute its Betti and de Rham actions, determining the scale from algebraic traces and cup-product pairings. Critical-value evaluations and, under mirror comparison and explicit continuation hypotheses, a continued genus-zero Gromov--Witten partition identity follow as corollaries.

title: Algebraic coarsening of hierarchical splines with guaranteed error control
abstract: We present a purely algebraic coarsening operator for hierarchical spline spaces, obtained by inverting locally the refinement matrix that relates the coarsened basis to the current one. Only the B-splines that interact with the coarsened region are involved, so that a coarsening step reduces to one small least-squares problem followed by explicit corrections of the surviving coefficients, without mass matrices or numerical quadrature. The operator is a left inverse of the refinement matrix, hence exact whenever the fine spline belongs to the coarse space, and leaves the spline unchanged away from the coarsened region. The residual of the least-squares problem bounds the $L^\infty$-error with no unknown constants and is available before the mesh is modified, which yields an adaptive multi-level algorithm that guarantees a prescribed tolerance. The construction carries over to truncated hierarchical B-splines, where the corrections disappear. In numerical experiments, the bound is sharp within an order of magnitude, the local transfer is nearly as accurate as a global $L^2$-projection, and much of the refinement left behind a moving front is removed without degrading the solution.

title: Nagata dimension, separation modulus and stochastic embeddings into trees
abstract: The separation modulus of a metric space, introduced by Bartal in 1996, is related to different notions of dimensionality. Most generally, Naor and Silberman gave in 2011 an upper bound on the separation modulus in terms of Nagata dimension. We prove that this bound cannot be reversed; that is, there are metric spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension and stochastically embeddable into trees with uniform distortion, which therefore have uniformly bounded separation modulus. Similarly, we construct spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension whose spaces of probability measures endowed with the Earth Mover's Distance (equivalently, their Lipschitz-free spaces) are embeddable into $L_1$ with uniformly bounded distortion. By gluing these spaces together, we obtain infinite Nagata dimensional metric spaces whose separation modulus is finite and whose Lipschitz-free space is isomorphic to $\ell_1$, respectively. Finally, we provide relations between separation modulus and stochastic embeddability into trees, also known as random approximability by tree metrics, in particular for the case of snowflake metrics.

title: Determinant Identities and Branch Selection in the Stationary Multi-Horizon Balance Problem
abstract: We study the Hennig-Neugebauer family of stationary and axisymmetric vacuum multi-horizon candidates. The regularity conditions on the symmetry axis lead to quadratic determinant relations which leave an apparent ambiguity between two sign branches. Under explicit non-degeneracy assumptions, we prove that one of these branches is impossible. This branch selection yields a system of explicit determinant equations characterizing equilibrium within the family.

title: Weighted minimal surfaces in H2 x R invariant under hyperbolic translations
abstract: In this paper, we consider weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR, namely, surfaces that arise as critical points of a weighted area functional, where the corresponding weight depends only on the height function associated with the second factor R. We refer to these surfaces as φ-minimal surfaces. For a class of increasing and concave weight potential functions φ, we focus our attention on height-weighted minimal surfaces that are invariant under isometries of H2xR that act trivially on R and act by hyperbolic translations in H2. Through a detailed analysis of the corresponding three-dimensional system of ordinary differential equations, we present families of entire graphs, graphs over half-spaces of H2 that are asymptotic to vertical planes, winglike surfaces, and surfaces whose height function has no minimum. These families show that the hyperbolic-invariant setting is considerably richer than the rotational and parabolic settings. For the class of potential functions φ we consider, they also allow us to classify all weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR that are invariant under hyperbolic translations.

title: Hypercyclic Algebras for Weighted Double Shifts
abstract: Building on the approach of Bayart, Costa Júnior and Papathanasiou, we establish a Baire criterion for possibly noncommuting operator pairs to support hypercyclic algebras, with hypercyclicity defined through all finite compositions.We then study weighted double backward shifts under different multiplications and topologies.We characterize the existence of hypercyclic algebras for coordinatewise multiplication on sequence algebras admitting a continuous norm and, separately, on $ω^2=\mathbb C^{\mathbb N_0^2}$ with the product topology.For the noncommutative triangular product induced by upper triangular matrix multiplication, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of dense hypercyclic algebras on $ω^2$.In this setting, their existence is equivalent to that of one freely generated by countably infinitely many elements.Finally, we exhibit a pair on a fixed Fréchet space that supports a dense hypercyclic algebra for coordinatewise multiplication and a nonzero hypercyclic algebra, but no dense one, for the triangular product.

title: Equidistribution of Hecke neighbours and continued fraction patterns
abstract:
We prove uniform tightness of Hecke neighbours of any probability measure of positive entropy that is invariant and ergodic under the diagonal flow. As an application, we confirm a conjecture of Einsiedler concerning a homogeneous dynamics analogue of an equidistribution theorem of Johnson and Rudolph on the torus. We also obtain applications to continued-fraction patterns in arithmetic sequences and to the \(p\)-adic Littlewood conjecture.
  Our proof studies escape of mass using dynamics on the boundary of the Chabauty compactification of the space of lattices, together with averaging operators defined by leafwise measures along horospherical subgroups.

title: Solutions of the set-theoretic quantum Yang-Baxter equation arising from posets
abstract: Victoria Lebed observed that the map $(x, \, y) \mapsto (\min\{x, \, y\}, \, \max\{x, \, y\})$ on a totally ordered set is an idempotent solution of the braid equation. We extend this example in several directions, by constructing four families of solutions of the braid equation associated to posets. First, for a given poset $P$, the map $R_P$ which sorts the comparable pairs and fixes the incomparable ones is an idempotent solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is the automorphism group of the poset $P$. Combined with the classical theorem of Birkhoff, this shows that every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of an idempotent solution of the braid equation of the form $(P, \, R_P)$, for some poset $P$. Moreover, $R_P \cong R_Q$ if and only if $P \cong Q$, and the solutions of the form $R_P$ are exactly the idempotent solutions of the braid equation which permute the components of each pair. Secondly, we classify all the solutions $R$ of the braid equation on an arbitrary set $X$ such that $R(x, \, y) \in \{(x, \, y), \, (y, \, x)\}$ for all $x$, $y\in X$: they are exactly the solutions $R_{\mathcal{P}}$ associated to the decompositions $\mathcal{P}$ of $X$ into posets. Finally, we associate to any finite poset $P$ two involutive solutions $D_P$ and $E_P$ of the braid equation, whose automorphism groups are $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^P \rtimes {\rm Aut} (P)$ and, if $P$ is connected and has at least two elements, the group of automorphisms and anti-automorphisms of $P$.

title: Directional maximal functions along algebraic curves
abstract: We prove that the maximal operator over line segments in $N$ arbitrary directions on a real algebraic curve of degree $D$ in $\mathbb R^n$ has $L^2$ operator norm at most $C_{n,\varepsilon}D^{C_n}N^\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, with $C_n$ independent of $\varepsilon$. Combined with polynomial partitioning, this gives the sharp bound $N^{\frac14}$, up to a polylogarithmic factor, for $N$ arbitrary directions in $\mathbb R^3$. The first main ingredient is a new quantitative strengthening of the property that the curve crosses each affine hyperplane at most $D$ times. This condition controls the overlap of variable-width neighborhoods of hyperplanes. The width attached to each direction is a small multiple of its distance to the osculating hyperplane at an endpoint of its arc. The problem is projectively invariant, and a projective almost orthogonality principle turns the overlap control into the $L^2$ bound. The second main ingredient, building on the complex cellular preparation of Binyamini and Novikov, is a new effective decomposition of algebraic curves. Up to $D^{C_n}$ points, the curve is covered by $D^{C_n}$ arcs whose coordinates, in a suitable parametrization and projective frame, are monomials with distinct exponents times nearly constant units. In these charts we verify the quantitative crossing condition with polynomial dependence on $D$. The framework also applies to nonalgebraic curves with doubling Frenet curvature measures. Consequences include local Sobolev maximal estimates along measurable vector fields with values in an algebraic curve, and the same bounds, up to a logarithmic factor, for directional Calderón--Zygmund operators.

title: A Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem for Quantum Graphs
abstract: We propose natural definitions of cuts and flows for quantum graphs. For cuts we consider two notions: ordinary cuts, which partition the vertex set into two parts; and generalised cuts, defined as a continuous relaxation of the binary partition function. We show that our definitions satisfy a max-flow min-cut theorem: For any disjoint terminal sets $S$ and $T$, the maximum value of an $S$-$T$-flow of a quantum graph equals the minimum value of a generalised $S$-$T$ cut, while the minimum value of an ordinary $S$-$T$ cut can be larger. While for classical graphs the values of the minimum generalised cut and the minimum ordinary cut coincide---recovering the classical max-flow min-cut theorem---we also show how it is more natural to think of flows as duals of generalised cuts instead of ordinary cuts.

title: Optimal approximation results for non-standard growth functionals in the super-dimensional case
abstract: In the super-dimensional case $p>n$ we show that $W^{1,p}$-functions can be uniformly approximated by Hölder continuous functions with improved exponent $\frac {p-n}{p-1}$. We use this to show density of smooth functions and absence of Lavrentiev's phenomenon for $(p, q)$-growth with optimal conditions. The special cases of double phase and Musielak--Orlicz growth are also included. Finally, we improve the conditions for maximal regularity of the double phase minimizers. In each case the optimality of our range of exponents is shown by known examples.

title: Wiener-path-based exact and splitting simulation of linear and semi-linear SDEs with additive noise
abstract:
Strong, or pathwise, simulation of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) requires linking a generated SDE path to the corresponding realization of its driving Wiener process. In this work, we develop Wiener-path-based simulation procedures for multidimensional linear and semi-linear SDEs with additive noise that preserve this connection.
  Building upon a known Wiener-path-based exact simulation approach for linear SDEs, we extend this construction to generate coherent paths simultaneously on different time grids. We further propose an alternative exact simulation procedure that requires fewer random numbers and therefore provides a more efficient construction, while retaining a controlled approximation of the coupling between the SDE path and its associated Wiener path. The proposed methods are illustrated on a stochastic harmonic oscillator, a well-known model from classical mechanics, with the simulation results confirming the theoretical findings.
  We then extend the Wiener-path-based construction to semi-linear SDEs, which arise in many real-world applications. In contrast to linear SDEs, their solutions are generally not available in closed form, making numerical approximation methods necessary. For Euler--Maruyama-type methods, the relation between a given Wiener path and the corresponding approximate SDE path is explicit, whereas constructing Wiener-path-based simulations using structure-preserving splitting methods is less immediate. We address this challenge by incorporating the aforementioned Wiener-path-based constructions into splitting methods. Illustrations on the stochastic FitzHugh--Nagumo model and the stochastic Jansen--Rit neural mass model, two important models from neuroscience, demonstrate the applicability of the proposed procedures to non-linear stochastic systems.

title: Coset Geometries and Tameness of Certain Classes of Shephard Groups
abstract: For the class of Shepard groups (which contain Coxeter groups, Artin-Tits groups, and many finite complex reflection groups), we investigate the structure of the coset incidence systems defined using the standard parabolic subgroups. For the class of tame Shephard groups, which is when all the standard parabolic subgroups are equal to the corresponding Shephard groups, then the intersection of standard parabolic subgroups is also a standard parabolic subgroup. We show that when the Shephard group is either finite, right-angled, or rank two, then it is tame; this is further evidence that all Shephard groups are tame. Finally, we mix the Burau and the geometric representations to produce a representation for all Shephard groups, but we show it is not faithful in rank two unless the Shephard group is finite or an Artin-Tits group.

title: Markov Population Potential Game: An Alternative Framework for Markovian Traffic Assignment
abstract: Understanding the equilibrium behavior of large populations of interacting agents in transportation systems is challenging due to the high-dimensional state space and the coupled decision-making among agents. This study proposes the Markov population potential game (MPPG) that integrates Markov games, potential games, and population games as a unified framework for analyzing such interactions. The framework extends the classical Markov potential game to the population level and establishes theoretical conditions on stage rewards and state transitions under which the Markov population game admits a Beckmann-type potential function. Accordingly, every KKT point of the associated optimization problem yields an MPPG equilibrium. We further demonstrate that if only the reward condition holds, each KKT point of the optimization problem corresponds to a support-restricted $\varepsilon$-equilibrium, meaning the Q-values of any two active actions differ by at most $\varepsilon$, thereby significantly extending the applicability of MPPG. We further establish both priori and posteriori upper bounds of $\varepsilon$ to efficiently evaluate the approximation error. Inspired by the equivalent optimization problem, a projected-gradient (PG) policy iteration algorithm is developed. The theoretical bounds and PG algorithm are demonstrated through numerical experiments on a parametric Markov population game.

title: A note on equivariant twisted holomorphic analytic torsion
abstract: In this note, we introduce an equivariant version of twisted holomorphic analytic torsion for the twisted Dolbeault complex on a complex manifold equipped with an action of a compact Lie group. Our construction is motivated by Ray and Singer's holomorphic analytic torsion, by the equivariant analytic torsion developed for elliptic complexes with group actions, notably in the work of Donnelly and later in the holomorphic setting by Bismut, and by Mathai and Wu's twisted analytic torsion for the twisted de Rham complex. Using pseudodifferential operators and the equivariant noncommutative residue, we define the equivariant twisted holomorphic analytic torsion. We also state its variation formulas under changes of the metric and of the twisting element, and present its functorial properties.

title: Slicing a Doughnut at Random
abstract: Choose a random plane that hits a solid torus. How likely is the slice to be a single disk, and how fat should the doughnut be to make this as likely as possible? Answering requires saying precisely what a "random plane" is. We explain this from scratch, first for random lines in the plane and then for random planes in space, and then solve the problem with nothing more than calculus. Along the way we meet a two-dimensional cousin of the problem (the doughnut's shadow) and two tempting wrong turns. One wrong turn appeared in print; it turns out to be a correct solution of the two-dimensional cousin. The other was the author's own first attempt, which luckily stayed in a drawer.

title: The periodic Short-Pulse equation by the Riemann-Hilbert problem approach
abstract: In this paper, we formulate a Riemann--Hilbert problem framework -- based on the Unified Transform Method (Fokas method) -- for the Short Pulse equation posed on a periodic domain. Under the stated spectral and reconstruction regularity assumptions, we show that a local solution of the periodic initial-value problem can be reconstructed from the solution of a suitably defined Riemann--Hilbert problem, whose jump data are explicitly characterized by spectral functions associated with the initial condition.

title: An exact certificate-based enumeration of Rolle words of degree six
abstract: For a real polynomial of degree $n$ with $n$ distinct real roots, assume that no two different nonconstant derivatives, including the polynomial itself, share a root. Recording the derivative orders of all roots from left to right gives a Rolle word. We present an exact, computer-assisted classification in degree six: $2706$ words are realizable, with a word and its reversal counted separately. Starting from $33592$ formal interlacing words, published necessary restrictions leave $13404$ candidates. Integer realization certificates and $53$ exact exclusion stages classify every candidate. The surviving set agrees exactly with the set of certified realizations. All verification uses integer and rational arithmetic. The accompanying code, certificates, proof notes, and per-word exclusion ledger make the computation reproducible. The result concerns degree six; it does not resolve the classification problem in arbitrary degree or count connected components of coefficient space. Most of the mathematical development, code, certificates, and initial manuscript were generated using ChatGPT under the author's direction. No independent human audit of the complete proof chain has yet been completed.

title: Latroids on Young's Lattice
abstract: Latroids are a generalization of matroids and polymatroids, given by a submodular rank function on a modular lattice. We study integer-valued latroids whose length function is the height of a finite modular lattice, without assuming that the lattice is complemented. We show that their cyclic flats form a lattice and, together with their ranks, determine the rank function. We also characterize which families of lattice elements, together with prescribed rank values, occur as the cyclic flats of such latroids. We then focus on principal intervals of Young's lattice, where we classify the latroids with modular rank functions and characterize the sparse paving ones. Finally, we attach a latroid to every Ferrers diagram rank-metric code and show that its cyclic flats, together with their ranks, determine the dimensions of all shortenings to Young subdiagrams.

title: Rateless Coding for Efficient Model Broadcast in Federated Learning
abstract: Model broadcast in federated learning (FL) with wireless channels faces significant challenges due to large model sizes and heterogeneous, unreliable channel conditions. While rateless coding has been widely adopted in modern broadcast communications to handle channel heterogeneity, its potential for model broadcast in FL remains largely unexplored. To fill this gap, we propose a joint source-channel coding scheme based on rateless coding to improve the robustness and efficiency of downlink model broadcast in FL. Specifically, we establish a rigorous convergence analysis of FL to inform the rateless code and quantization design under noisy downlink channel conditions. Moreover, by observing that the iterative process of FL naturally provides prior information about client updates, we leverage client-side local models as conditional prior information to aid the decoding process, thereby reducing transmission costs. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our rateless coding scheme significantly enhances downlink model broadcast efficiency in FL, while retaining comparable training accuracies for both homogeneous and heterogeneous data distributions.

title: Extremal disc packings in compact hyperbolic surfaces of minimal genus
abstract: A compact hyperbolic surface is $k$-extremal if it contains $k$ disjoint embedded discs of the largest possible radius; such surfaces are uniformized by surface subgroups of the triangle groups $Δ^{\pm}(2,3,N)$. We determine all extremal $k$-packings in every $k$-extremal surface of minimal genus, orientable of genus $2$ and non-orientable of genus $3$: $373$ surface groups in total, all treated in a unified way; $264$ of them had never been studied before. The computation is automatic and verified in exact arithmetic, each packing being certified by an element $α\in\mathrm{PGL}_2$ over an explicit number field with $α^{-1}Kα<Δ^{\pm}(2,3,N)$. We also obtain the full isometry groups of these surfaces. In every surface but one, all the extremal packings are related by isometries. The exception is the genus two surface $X_6$ of Girondo and González-Diez, which has exactly five extremal $4$-packings, one invariant under all isometries and four forming an orbit; it is also the only one of these surfaces uniformized by two non-conjugate subgroups of the same triangle group, and we show that the two facts are equivalent. We find its equation, $y^2=x^6+2\sqrt{3}\,i\,x^3+1$. The results form a catalogue with detailed data and pictures of every surface (packings, isometries, Weierstrass points, Dirichlet domains), distributed with programs that allow the reader to consult it and to reproduce it completely.

title: Sharp Gaussian approximation for Polyak--Ruppert averaged linear stochastic approximation
abstract: We study how quickly the normalized Polyak--Ruppert average approaches its Gaussian limit in linear stochastic approximation with bounded i.i.d.\ coefficients. For step sizes decaying as $k^{-γ}$, with $1/2\leγ<1$, we prove an upper bound of order $n^{γ-1}$ on the approximation error over convex sets in fixed dimension. A matching lower bound holds for every fixed model. The fastest rate in this range is $n^{-1/2}$, attained at $γ=1/2$. We also obtain an $O(n^{-1/2})$ bound on the error of the recursive multiplier bootstrap procedure.

title: Point symmetries and Lie reductions of Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation
abstract: We compute the point symmetry pseudogroup of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation using both the direct and the algebraic methods. We also revisit the classical Lie symmetry analysis of this model in detail, concentrating on hidden infinitesimal and hidden point symmetries. Additionally, we re-examine the symmetry properties of each codimension-one reduced model and determine their point symmetry pseudogroups.

title: Optimal higher order convergence rates for the MUON optimizer
abstract: Gradient descent optimization methods are the key tools to train deep neural networks in artificial intelligence systems. In practice, one typically employs suitable accelerated gradient descent optimization methods such as the momentum optimizer, the Adam optimizer, or the MUON optimizer proposed by Jordan et al. in 2024. In 1964 Polyak showed that, in a neighborhood of a local minimizer, the momentum optimizer converges with the rate $(\sqrtχ+1)^{-1}(\sqrtχ-1)$, which is strictly faster than the rate $(χ+1)^{-1}(χ-1)$ of the standard gradient descent optimizer, where $χ\in(1,\infty)$ is the condition number (the ratio of the largest to the smallest eigenvalue) of the Hessian of the objective function at the local minimizer. Recently, the same faster rate has been established for the Adam optimizer. In this work we show that the MUON optimizer achieves the same higher speed of convergence and we establish the optimality of the obtained convergence rates. More specifically, we propose a precise concept for measuring the speed of convergence of gradient descent optimization methods, and we establish optimal convergence rates for the standard gradient descent, the momentum, the RMSprop, the Adam, and the MUON optimizers.

title: Statistical-to-computational gaps in central limit theorems for high-dimensional tensors
abstract: We study high-dimensional central limit theorems (CLTs) as hypothesis testing problems, comparing the number of summands needed for statistical and computational indistinguishability of the normalized sum from the limiting Gaussian distribution as the dimension and number of summands grow together. For the off-diagonal entries of sums of i.i.d. rank-one tensors formed from standard Gaussian vectors (equivalently, the problem of distinguishing Wigner from Wishart tensors), we prove total variation bounds sharpening previous estimates of Mikulincer (2020) and give matching polynomial-time tests. This shows that the statistical and computational thresholds coincide for this CLT, contrary to a proposal by Kunisky, Moore, and Wein (2024). On the other hand, we also show that, for tensors of order at least three, sufficient Gaussian dilution of the summands by adding independent Gaussian noise and rescaling gives a CLT model with a statistical-to-computational gap (in the above setting and ones with more general rank-one summand distributions). To the best of our knowledge, such a phenomenon has not been observed before in any high-dimensional CLT. In particular, in the relevant parameter regimes, we show that a brute-force search achieves strong detection, while polynomials of degree up to $n^{Ω(1)}$ cannot achieve strong separation. The latter lower bounds control low-degree $χ^2$-divergences by a novel method based on cumulant generating functions, and we further illustrate the use of these tools by applying them to masked tensor CLT models where only a prescribed subset of tensor entries is revealed.

title: Poisson and Jacobi structures on quadratic Lie algebras
abstract: We study Poisson and Jacobi structures compatible with quadratic structures on finite-dimensional Lie algebras, mostly over fields of characteristic zero. Building on the theory of generalized double extensions, we give necessary and sufficient reconstruction criteria for the skew operators preserving a marked isotropic ideal, allowing degenerate operators, a nonabelian quadratic quotient, and the full generalized extension data. Recalling the characterization of quadratic Poisson structures in terms of skew-symmetric solutions of the classical Yang--Baxter equation, we combine the ambient bracket reconstruction of Kostant and Meyer with prescribed symplectic leaf data to reconstruct Poisson structures whose characteristic subalgebra is nondegenerate for the quadratic form. We express the standard algebraic Jacobi equations through the invariant form and obtain analogous reconstruction results for nondegenerate characteristic subalgebras. Particular attention is given to the contact and locally conformally symplectic cases. A common cochain framework identifies the remaining scalar obstruction in third cohomology in the Poisson case and in the Jacobi branch whose Euler element belongs to the marked ideal, with coefficients in a one dimensional module in the latter case. Our reconstruction results yield systematic procedures for constructing quadratic Poisson structures in dimension $n+2k$ from those in dimension $n$, and recover the earlier quadratic symplectic extension formulas when the Poisson operator is invertible. Explicit examples illustrate the applicability of the theory, including oscillator algebras, the five-dimensional Lie algebra $A_{5,3}$, and Poisson structures associated with the curvature tensor of a bi-invariant metric.

title: GV-subschemes and hyperelliptic Jacobians
abstract:
We provide a solution to the hyperelliptic Schottky problem: a principally polarized complex abelian variety whose theta divisor has singular locus of codimension three is a hyperelliptic Jacobian. As a key step towards this criterion for hyperelliptic Jacobians, we prove a conjecture of Pareschi and Popa which predicts that if the ideal sheaf $I_X$ of a subscheme $X$ of an indecomposable PPAV $(A, Θ)$ satisfies that $I_X(2Θ)$ is IT$_0$, then $X$ is a GV-subscheme.
  As a corollary of the main result, the base scheme of an ample line bundle on a complex abelian variety is generically reduced along every irreducible component of codimension $2$, confirming a conjecture of Debarre. This corollary completes the algebraic-geometry proof by Arbarello-Codogni-Pareschi in \cite{ACP21, ACP25} of Novikov's conjecture, which characterizes Jacobians via the KP equation.

title: Entropic Ricci bounds at conic singularities and boundaries
abstract: We study synthetic Ricci bounds and related rigidity phenomena in conic and boundary neighborhoods through the behavior of entropy along optimal transports. For cones over manifolds, we show that two-sided entropic Ricci bounds at the vertex force the fiber to have constant sectional curvature 1, while non-trivial quotient singularities, such as Euclidean cones over spherical space forms, remain admissible. An analogous rigidity holds for Riemannian manifolds with conic singularities. We also give a local characterization of boundary convexity in terms of entropic lower Ricci bounds, based on a direct optimal transport argument.

title: Quadratic Convexification with Two Switching Variables via Extreme Rays
abstract: We consider the convex hull of the quadratic lift $(x,xx^\top,y)$ of the set $\{(x,y) \mid 0 \le x \le y,\ y \in \{0,1\}^n \}$. Descriptions of this convex hull provide convex relaxations for quadratic optimization with switching variables, including problems with indefinite quadratic objectives and constraints. For $n=2$, we completely characterize the extreme rays of the corresponding cone of nonnegative quadratic functions, which consists of two switching rays, six boundary-product rays, discounted affine-square rays, and a parameterized family of discounted rank-two rays. These families generate the cone, so their linearizations give a complete valid-inequality description of the convex hull in the lifted space. The discounted rank-two rays also show that rank-one liftings cannot generate all valid inequalities. Using this classification, we prove a conjecture of Anstreicher and Burer on an exact semidefinite representation of this convex hull.

title: Shuffles of permutations in cycle form
abstract:
We study a variation of the shuffle operation on permutations, which acts on their cycle structure instead of their one-line notation. Given two permutations $σ\in S_k$ and $τ\in S_{n-k}$, the $\textit{shuffle-by-cycle}$ $σ\mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c τ$ is the set of all permutations in $S_n$ whose set of cycles can be separated into two disjoint subsets: one whose standardization is $σ$, and one whose standardization is $τ$. One can think of the sets $σ\mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c τ$ as refinements of conjugacy classes.
  We show that if $σ$ and $τ$ have no order-isomorphic cycles, then the descent set has the same distribution, over the set $σ\mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c τ$ of shuffles-by-cycle, as over the set $σ\mathbin{\sqcup\!\sqcup} τ$ of standard shuffles; our proof is bijective. This result no longer holds when $σ$ and $τ$ have order-isomorphic cycles. For an arbitrary shuffle-by-cycle, we provide a description of the distribution of the descent set in terms of plethysm of quasisymmetric functions. For the set $σ\mathbin{\,\sqcup\!\sqcup}_c σ\subset S_{2n}$, where $σ$ is an $n$-cycle, we deduce explicit generating functions for the bivariate distribution of descent number and major index.

title: Stable irrationality of quartic hypersurfaces
abstract: We prove that a very general quartic hypersurface of any positive dimension over an uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic different from 2 does not admit an integral decomposition of the diagonal, and in particular it is not stably rational.

title: Artin-style characterizations of the multiple gamma and sine functions
abstract: We extend Artin's characterizations of the gamma function to the multiple setting by means of the Kubert identity. We obtain uniqueness theorems for positive continuous solutions of a difference equation $G(z + 1) = α(z)G(z)$ that also satisfy an Artin-type multiplication formula, remaining within the class of continuous functions under a modest initial condition. The results apply in particular to the Barnes multiple gamma functions and the Kurokawa multiple sine functions.

title: Meridional ranks of iterated Whitehead doubles
abstract: We prove that every iterated untwisted Whitehead double of a nontrivial two-bridge knot satisfies the meridional rank conjecture. More precisely, for such a knot $K$ and every $N\geq0$, the augmentation rank, meridional rank, and bridge number of $\operatorname{Wh}^N(K)$ are all $2^{N+1}$. We use microlocal sheaf theory and a doubling construction to produce a lower bound for the meridional rank of the Whitehead double, assuming the peripheral data satisfy suitable conditions. For two-bridge knots, the required curves arise from ideal points detecting nonzero boundary slopes. In contrast, the ordinary group rank of an $N$-fold Whitehead double is at most the rank of the companion group plus $N$. We also give a non-example when the doubling construction does not work -- the first Whitehead double of the square knot has augmentation rank at most 5, whereas its meridional rank and bridge number are 6.

title: Autonomous Neural Adaptive Control as a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator
abstract:
We study autonomous neural adaptive control, where the controller modifies the physical dynamics while the data generated by the physical dynamics itself drive subsequent parameter updates. We formulate the coupled evolution of the physical state distribution and controller parameters through a self-consistent transfer operator.
  Assuming that the physical dynamics under each fixed controller admits a unique invariant distribution, we characterize adaptive equilibria through a finite-dimensional self-consistency equation for the stationary mean learning update. We establish existence using Brouwer degree, without requiring global convexity, and reduce uniqueness to uniqueness of the corresponding zero.
  Under suitable differentiability and spectral-gap assumptions, we derive a finite-dimensional criterion for local exponential convergence of both the physical distribution and controller parameters at sufficiently small positive learning rates. The criterion involves the Jacobian of the reduced equation, computed using linear response to include the effect of controller-induced changes in the invariant distribution. The asymptotic slow relaxation time scales inversely with the learning rate.
  We rigorously verify the assumptions and apply the theory to a noisy Duffing-type system with a neural residual compensator, providing a nontrivial example of adaptive control with provable existence, uniqueness, and local stability of an adaptive equilibrium. Numerical experiments illustrate statistical feedback and the role of time-scale separation.

title: Calderón-Zygmund estimates and their failure for PDE with linear growth
abstract: We investigate when Calderón-Zygmund estimates hold for PDEs of the type \[ \operatorname{div}(A(\nabla u)) = \operatorname{div}(F) \] where $A: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ is a continuous map with linear growth. We show that, under natural assumptions, $L^p$-Calderón-Zygmund estimates hold for all $p \in (1,\infty)$ if and only if $v \mapsto \lim_{t \to \infty} A(tv)/t$ is linear and non-degenerate.

title: Metriplectic Lotka--Volterra systems with noise:interactions invisible at stationarity, visible in time
abstract: We show that a Lotka--Volterra system with an interior equilibrium admits a metriplectic structure, with a Volterra function $V_C$ as energy and an entropy variable for the environment, if and only if Volterra's dissipativity condition $CA+A^{\top}C\le0$ holds, and we construct it explicitly with a log-canonical Poisson bivector. Adding noise through the fluctuation--dissipation relation of stochastic GENERIC yields multiplicative environmental noise, with covariance fixed by the symmetric part of $AC^{-1}$, whose stationary law is an explicit Gibbs measure: a product of independent Gamma distributions. Unlike known Gibbs measures for stochastic Lotka--Volterra systems, this holds for nonsymmetric interactions, predator--prey included. The stationary law determines only the equilibrium and $C/k$: every interaction matrix in an open cone of dimension $n^2$, in particular any Poisson part, produces with its compatible noise the same law as uncoupled stochastic logistic equations. Gamma-distributed, uncorrelated abundance fluctuations, as observed in microbial communities, are therefore no evidence of absence of interactions. The interactions are, however, visible in time: the zero-lag derivative of the log-abundance covariance equals $A(C/k)^{-1}$, and its antisymmetric part is the Poisson part, which carries all the stationary entropy production, computed in closed form. Finally, for general noise we prove an exact Lyapunov-type identity $AK+K^\top A^\top+Q=0$ for $K=\mathrm{Cov}(x,\log x)$ at any stationary solution. It implies that the populations are independent if and only if the noise is metriplectically compatible, and gives an explicit lower bound on interspecies cross-covariances in terms of the distance of $Q$ to the compatible family. Simulations of a predator--prey model show that the bound is nearly sharp.

title: Gaussian fluctuations and moderate deviations for two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal flows
abstract: We study the small-noise behaviour of a two-dimensional stochastic nematic liquid crystal model, where the Navier--Stokes equations with multiplicative noise are coupled with a Ginzburg--Landau equation for the director field driven by geometric Stratonovich noise. While large deviations for stochastic nematic liquid crystal models have been studied earlier, the central limit and moderate deviation regimes have not been considered. We first prove a central limit theorem in the natural energy space and show that the rescaled fluctuations converge, in every $L^p$-norm and with rate $\sqrt{\eps}$, to the solution of a linear stochastic system. The limiting process is centred Gaussian. We then establish a moderate deviation principle with a quadratic rate function determined by the corresponding linearised skeleton equation, which coincides with the Cameron--Martin form of the Gaussian limit. We also show that the moderate deviation principle holds uniformly over bounded sets of initial data. The main arguments use a cancellation between the coupling terms, a one-sided estimate for the polynomial potential, and energy estimates with deterministic Gronwall coefficients, thereby avoiding exponential moment estimates.

title: Determination of a Bi-periodic Refractive Index for the Helmholtz Equation
abstract: We investigate an inverse problem for the Helmholtz equation in a three-dimensional half-space with a biperiodic medium above a sound-soft plane. We establish the uniqueness of a real-valued, bounded, biperiodic refractive index that depends only on the horizontal variables using spectral techniques. %The frequency and quasiperiodicity parameter are fixed. An orthogonality identity is first derived from near-field measurements. By constructing suitable separated solutions, this identity is reduced to relations involving eigenfunctions of two-dimensional quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators. To recover Fourier information from these relations, we project horizontal plane waves onto suitable high-energy spectral subspaces, obtaining finite combinations of eigenfunctions that approximate the plane waves with a quantified error. Combining these approximations with the orthogonality identity, we show that all Fourier coefficients of the difference of two refractive indices vanish, thereby establishing the desired uniqueness.

title: Shift-Symmetric Configurations in $d$-Dimensional Cellular Automata: Enumeration, Bounds, Irreversibility, and Detection
abstract: A configuration of a cellular automaton on the $d$-dimensional torus $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ is shift-symmetric if it is fixed by some nonzero translation. Banda, Caughman, Cenek, and Teuscher (Chaos 29, 063120, 2019) enumerated these configurations in two dimensions and drew dynamical and algorithmic consequences. We extend their results to every dimension. We give an explicit closed-form enumeration for all $n$, $d$, and alphabet sizes $σ$, in which the two-dimensional coefficients $1$, $p+1$, and $p$ become $r_d(p,v)=p^{\binom{v}{2}}\binom{d}{v}_p$, with $\binom{d}{v}_p$ the Gaussian binomial; it extends to configurations with a prescribed number of active cells and to all finite abelian groups. The case of prime $n$ recovers, in complement form, a result of Castillo-Ramirez and Gadouleau; the multi-prime closed form and the dynamical consequences beyond the stabilizer inclusion are new. We prove a lower bound attained exactly when $n$ is prime, and upper bounds, among them $(2^d-1+2\log_2 n)\,σ^{n^d/2}$. As $d$ grows, the symmetry probability decays as $σ^{-c\,n^d}$ with $c\to1-1/p_1(n)$, set solely by the smallest prime factor of $n$, and the symmetry advantage of the side $p+1$ over a prime side $p$ inverts within an explicit window around $d_c(p)\approx p\ln 2$. Under the necessary hypothesis of translation-equivariant neighborhoods, shift-symmetry is irreversible, the per-prime symmetry ranks never decrease, and non-symmetric tasks are unsolvable from symmetric inputs. We give a detection algorithm with worst-case cost $O(n^d\sum_{p\mid n}\frac{p^d-1}{p-1})$ and an average-case analysis, exact for each subgroup test. The mathematical content of every numbered statement is formally verified in Lean 4, and the correspondence between each theorem, lemma, proposition, and corollary and its formal statement was audited by hand.

title: A posteriori error estimates for the bulk--surface Cahn--Hilliard system with dynamic boundary conditions
abstract: This paper develops reliable residual-based a posteriori error estimators for the full discretization of a bulk--surface Cahn--Hilliard system with a two-parameter family of dynamic boundary conditions on a curved domain. The main novelty are theoretically justified computable temporal, coarsening and geometric error estimators. The numerical method combines a linear bulk--surface finite element method in space and a linearly implicit backward Euler method in time. Based on the derived error indicators, a space--time adaptive algorithm is proposed and numerical experiments illustrate and complement the theoretical result.

title: Gluing Geometric Chains Of Manifolds And Orbifolds With Corners
abstract: Geometric chains are formal combinations of smooth maps from compact oriented manifolds or orbifolds with corners. In earlier work the author showed that, modulo a relation D that kills degenerate chains, they compute rational singular homology. We show that D can be replaced by a gluing relation, which identifies a chain with the sum of its restrictions to finitely many pieces whenever its source is glued from these pieces along whole codimension-one faces. With this relation the comparison map from singular homology is an isomorphism in all degrees for compact polyhedra and smooth manifolds without boundary, with rational and with integer coefficients. Unlike D, the gluing relation is defined through the sources alone, and chain-level identities such as the equivalence of a degree d covering with d times its base, which fails modulo D, and the correction terms of the chain map from a Morse complex, which are degenerate modulo D, become gluing relations. The proof is axiomatic; injectivity comes from integration or dual cells, surjectivity from cutting along regular levels, where the cut of a gluing relation is again one, and at the point we use Whitehead triangulations of manifolds with corners subordinate to their corner strata. The gluing relation, read on underlying spaces, also suffices for orbifold sources, with integer coefficients modulo classes with an orientation reversing automorphism, and for effective orbifold targets.

title: Controlling avalanche sizes in the Abelian sandpile model
abstract: The Abelian sandpile model is a classical framework for studying large cascading events, such as those arising in models of forest fires and earthquakes. This work studies the control of such avalanches through the targeted removal of sand grains. We formulate this sequential control problem as an average-cost Markov decision process in which, before each grain addition, a controller may remove a sand grain from a selected vertex. The objective is to balance the long-run expected avalanche size against the cost of intervention. We analyze local intervention policies, which remove grains from a prescribed set of vertices whenever possible, and establish structural results for the recurrent classes and stationary distributions of the induced Markov chains. When the intervention set satisfies a property called topple-freeness, we sharpen these results, derive expressions for the gain and bias functions, and give necessary and sufficient conditions for optimality on general finite graphs. Finally, we apply the general theory to several specific graph classes and obtain a complete characterization of optimal policies on the one-dimensional lattice, the complete graph and the star graph for every value of the intervention cost.

title: A Rigorous Fredholm Framework and Stabilized Equal-Order Finite Element Methods for the Time-Harmonic Biot Model
abstract: We investigate the well-posedness and finite element approximation of a three-field formulation of the time-harmonic Biot model, motivated by frequency-domain magnetic resonance elastography. The underlying complex-valued mixed variational problem is noncoercive because of the inertial elasticity term and the coupled three-field structure. Continuous well-posedness is established under a non-resonance condition by decomposing the variational operator into an invertible principal part and a compact perturbation and applying the Fredholm alternative. We then develop stabilized equal-order finite element methods based on momentum-residual stabilization and local projection stabilization of the pore pressure. For the discrete problem, we establish mesh-uniform stability and well-posedness on sufficiently fine meshes via an a priori stability estimate and a Schatz-type compactness argument, without invoking discrete $T$-coercivity. Optimal-order a priori error estimates are derived in the natural energy norm. We also develop systematic selection principles for the stabilization parameters. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates and demonstrate stable approximations for heterogeneous low-permeability media and anatomically realistic brain geometries relevant to magnetic resonance elastography.

title: Probabilistically Exact Convexification of Mixed-Integer Quadratic Optimization with Indicators
abstract: We study the convexification of mixed-integer quadratic optimization with indicator variables. The problem remains NP-hard even when the quadratic matrix has bandwidth two, posing a fundamental obstacle to tractable exact convexification. To overcome this challenge in realistic settings, we introduce probabilistically exact (inner) convexification, a framework that relaxes the requirement of exactness for every objective while preserving exact optimality for statistically relevant ones. Our approach is motivated by inference applications, where the objective is determined by a data vector drawn from a distribution and a regularization vector chosen from a prescribed family. Our convexification preserves the exactness of the optimal value with high probability over the data distribution, simultaneously for every regularization vector in this family. We apply this notion to quadratic matrices of any fixed bandwidth. Despite their worst-case NP-hardness, we construct probabilistically exact convexifications that admit exact extended second-order cone formulations of size polynomial in the dimension $n$ and the inverse failure probability $1/δ$. The required assumptions for their high-probability exactness are surprisingly mild: they accommodate both light-tailed and heavy-tailed data, including distributions without finite mean, as well as arbitrary nonnegative regularization coefficients.

title: Finite Element Approximation of Three-Dimensional Elliptic Optimal Control Problems with Curve-Supported Controls
abstract: We consider a linear-quadratic elliptic optimal control problem in three dimensions with a box-constrained control supported on a compact embedded $C^{1,1}$ curve strictly contained in a bounded convex polyhedral domain. The right-hand side of the state equation is a measure supported on the curve, and the state is singular along it. We establish well-posedness and first-order optimality conditions and derive curve-adapted weighted inequalities and finite element error estimates for the singular state. For continuous piecewise linear finite elements on quasi-uniform tetrahedral meshes and variational discretization of the control, assuming exact integration over the curve, we prove the almost quadratic estimate $\|\bar q-\bar q_h\|_{L^2(γ)}\le Ch^2(1+\abs{\ln h})^3$. The proof of this estimate requires new results, which are of independent interest. The convergence rate observed in a numerical experiment is consistent with the predicted algebraic order.

title: On the orders of irreducible subgroups of finite classical groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite almost simple classical group over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with socle $G_0$ and natural module $V$ of dimension $n$. Let $H$ be a core-free maximal subgroup of $G$. By a well-known theorem of Aschbacher, either $H$ is contained in one of eight subgroup collections that are defined in terms of the geometry of $V$, or $H$ is almost simple and the embedding of $H$ in $G$ arises from an absolutely irreducible representation of a covering group of the socle of $H$. We write $\mathcal{S}$ for the latter collection of irreducibly embedded almost simple subgroups. Determining the subgroups in $\mathcal{S}$ is an intractable problem, in general, which has only been fully resolved in low dimensions. However, many applications require some control on the subgroups in $\mathcal{S}$, expressed in terms of their order, or properties of their elements, for example. Extending a theorem of Liebeck from the 1980s, and building on later work by Burness, Guralnick and Saxl, in this paper we determine all the subgroups $H \in \mathcal{S}$ satisfying the lower bound $|H| \geqslant q^n$. We also highlight a recent application of our main result to a problem in finite geometry.

title: $q$-$γ$-positivity of two $q$-Narayana polynomials
abstract: We address the question of $q$-$γ$-positivity of $q$-Narayana polynomials for $q$-super Catalan numbers $A_{n,m}(q)$ and their duals, $B_{n,m}(q)$. We offer three main results. First, both the $q$-$m$-Narayana polynomials, whose coefficients refine the q-super Catalan numbers, and the dual q-Narayana polynomials are $q$-$γ$-positive of index one. Second, the dual $q$-Narayana polynomials are also $q$-$γ$-positive of index two. Third, both the $q$- Narayana numbers and their duals are coefficient-wise $q$-unimodal.

title: Exponential Multiple Riordan Arrays
abstract: We extend exponential double Riordan arrays to exponential multiple Riordan arrays $[g;f_1,\ldots,f_\ell]$, whose columns are generated, in exponential form, by a function $g$ of $t^\ell$ and $\ell$ multipliers $f_1,\ldots,f_\ell$ used cyclically. We prove an $\ell$-case fundamental theorem, define the exponential multiple Riordan group, and determine its identity, inverses, and its Appell, associated, and $\ell$ Bell-type subgroups; the group is the semidirect product of its Appell and associated subgroups. We compute the production matrix in terms of $2\ell$ sequences, the $c_r$- and $r_r$-sequences ($0\leq r\leq \ell-1$), give its bivariate generating function in terms of generalized hyperbolic functions, and derive recurrence relations for the entries. Finally, we give two sequence characterizations: one by $\ell-1$ one-step $A$-sequences, an $\ell$-step $A$-sequence, and a $Z$-sequence, and one by a single $\ell$-step $A$-sequence and $\ell$ $Z$-sequences. For $\ell=2$ all results reduce to those for exponential double Riordan arrays.

title: Affine Grassmannian from divisors
abstract: We generalize Mirković's construction of Zastava spaces. These spaces form an inductive system, giving a generalization of affine and Beilinson--Drinfeld Grassmannians as indschemes, defined for any integral symmetric matrix $κ$ with even diagonal entries. When $κ$ is the Cartan matrix from a simply-laced Kac--Moody algebra, we also construct an action of the Tits group on the generalized affine Grassmannian.

title: The One-Skeleton of Multilinear Polytopes and Their Standard Relaxations
abstract: Edge-following methods, such as the simplex method, move along edges of a polytope. Their behavior depends on which vertices are adjacent and on the diameter. We study both for the two polytopes of binary polynomial optimization: the multilinear polytope and its standard linear relaxation. For quadratic polynomials, Padberg showed that two integral vertices are adjacent in both polytopes if and only if the variables where they differ induce a connected subgraph. For higher degree, we replace this subgraph by a contracted hypergraph on the same variables, built from the monomials whose constraints tie these variables together. We show that its connectivity decides adjacency in the relaxation but, unlike in the quadratic case, not always in the multilinear polytope. Adjacency is the same in both polytopes exactly when the relaxation has the Trubin property. We investigate when this property holds and characterize it for cubic polynomials. The contracted hypergraph also yields short paths. The diameter of the multilinear polytope is at most the number of variables, and that of the relaxation is linear in the numbers of variables and monomials. Similar linear bounds hold for the number of pivots between bases of the relaxation.

title: Skew Zero Forcing Matroids
abstract: Matroid theory and skew zero forcing (SZF) in graphs are both topics of mathematical interest, but very little is known about their overlap. When a matroid arises from a graph in the traditional way, the edges of the graph correspond with the elements of the matroid. However, the SZF color change rule for graphs can be viewed as a closure operator on the vertices of a graph. As such, when a matroid arises from a graph via SZF, the vertices of the graph correspond with the elements of the matroid. We call such a matroid SZF-realizable. Notably, unlike the traditional method of obtaining a matroid from a graph, skew zero forcing in a graph does not always give rise to a matroid. This paper establishes fundamental results in graph and matroid theory with respect to (1) which matroids are SZF-realizable, and (2) what kinds of graphs do and do not give rise to SZF matroids. The main result of the paper focuses on cycle matroids of outerplanar graphs.

title: Exceptional parameters in the Erdős similarity problem
abstract: The Erd\H os similarity conjecture says that for every infinite set $A \subset \mathbb{R}$, there exists a set $E$ of positive Lebesgue measure which does not contain any affine copy of $x + tA$ of $A$ (with $t \neq 0$). Kolountzakis proved that for every infinite $A$, there exists $E$ of positive Lebesgue measure so that the exceptional sets $D_E(A)$ of scales $t$, and $\mathcal E_E(A)$ of affine maps $(x,t)$, for which $x+tA\subseteq E$, are both Lebesgue null. We show that these exceptional parameter sets are small in two finer senses. First, given any countable family of Fourier decay rates, a single $E$ can be constructed so that $D_E(A)$ is null with respect to every measure whose Fourier transform decays at one of these rates. Consequently, there are compact sets $K$ of measure arbitrarily close to $1$ for which $D_K(A)$ and $\mathcal E_K(A)$ have modified Fourier dimension zero. Second, we give a criterion, depending both on the growth of a gauge function $h$ and on the gaps between elements of lacunary sequences in $A$, which guarantees that $\mathcal H^h(D_E(A))=0$ for gauges with $h(u)/u\to\infty$, as well as a similar result for $\mathcal E_K(A)$. For sets such as $A = \{1/n!\}$ and $A = \{e^{-n^q}\}$, this yields explicit gauges of the form $h(u) = u\exp((\log 1/u)^θ)$ with $0 < θ< 1$.

title: The Fourier dimension conjecture for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos on the circle
abstract: Bonnefont, Rajamäki and Vargas conjectured that, for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos built from a single real Gaussian field, the Fourier dimension at $α+iβ$ equals the dimension of the real chaos at $α$ minus $β^2$. We prove the conjecture on the circle throughout their stated parameter range. For the canonical holomorphic family, the identity holds on one event of probability one for all $γ=α+iβ$ in the union of the open unit disk and the region $1/\sqrt2<|α|<\sqrt2$, $|α|+|β|<\sqrt2$. For each fixed parameter on the conjecture's sloping boundary, where $1<|α|<\sqrt2$ and $|α|+|β|=\sqrt2$, the Fourier coefficients decay at a logarithmic rate almost surely and the Fourier dimension is zero. For nonzero interior parameters with $|α|\ne1/\sqrt2$, the critical Sobolev index is half the Fourier dimension minus $1/2$. The chaos fails to belong to the corresponding space when $|α|<1/\sqrt2$ and belongs to it when $|α|>1/\sqrt2$. For $1/\sqrt2<|α|<\sqrt2$ and $|β|\le\sqrt2-|α|$, we bound the Fourier coefficients at the decay power predicted by the dimension formula, up to logarithmic factors. For $0<|γ|<1$ and $α^2<1/2$, the measures obtained by multiplying the squared modulus of the smoothed chaos by $ε^{|γ|^2}$ converge weakly almost surely along $ε=e^{-m}$, uniformly on compact parameter sets, to explicit multiples of the real chaos at $2α$.

title: Dynamic Prandtl-Reuss Thermoplasticity with Degenerating Yield Constraints
abstract: We study a three-dimensional dynamic thermoplastic system with a temperature-dependent convex yield set whose deviatoric section may collapse completely at a finite temperature. The underlying constitutive model is rate-independent Prandtl-Reuss perfect plasticity, without Kelvin-Voigt viscosity, hardening, or a safe-load condition. We construct global approximation-generated relaxed entropy-energy states by a one-parameter Temam-Norton-Hoff-Galerkin scheme with an undiscretized heat equation and untruncated plastic heat production. The logarithmic temperature is strongly compact in $L^2(0,T;L^q(Ω))$ for every $q<6$ and in $L^p((0,T)\timesΩ)$ for every $p<8/3$. An entropy-weighted work estimate yields convergence of the overstress at rate $O(\sqrt{\log n/n})$ in every fixed finite Lebesgue space and identifies stress admissibility. The constitutive limit comprises a distributional plastic balance, finite support-weighted measures, and compact-fibre lifts carrying exact normality and maximum plastic work. A locally finite lift on the positive-radius fibres unifies the level-restricted limits at every continuity level. At the macroscopic level, however, the available compactness does not identify a canonical stress-plastic-flow pairing. Moreover, an explicit smooth state satisfying the intrinsic relaxed balance conditions shows that these conditions do not imply macroscopic Prandtl-Reuss normality. In the fully collapsed regime, an energy-entropy rigidity argument determines the evolution and yields approximation-generated examples in which the plastic flow need not be a finite measure or the displacement need not retain its full boundary trace. Thermal concentration and plastic entropy production remain explicit throughout.

title: HKT-Einstein metrics on circle bundles
abstract: We consider a construction of hyper-Hermitian structures on total spaces of circle bundles over 3-quasi-Sasakian manifolds. We study the HKT-Einstein equation in this setting, proving that a large family of non-homogeneous hyper-complex manifolds admit compatible HKT-Einstein metrics with positive Einstein factor. We also show that the hyper-Hermitian structures on such circle bundles are quaternionic balanced or quaternionic Gauduchon if and only if they are HKT. Finally, the HKT-Einstein condition is investigated under the twist construction.

title: A posteriori space error estimates for the finite element approximation of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations based on the variational multiscale framework
abstract: This study introduces a novel a posteriori space error estimator derived within the variational multiscale (VMS) framework for the stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. In this framework, the continuous problem is decomposed into coarse and fine scales. The fine scale, often referred to as the sub-grid scale (SGS), is modeled as proportional to the component of the residual orthogonal to the finite element (FE) space.
