This modeled SGS then serves as a reliable error estimator. Specifically, the approach employs a scaled norm of the SGSs as an a posteriori error estimate, evaluated within the stabilized norm associated with the problem. This methodology was previously applied to the stationary convection-diffusion-reaction equation (Codina et al., 2025) and is now extended to the stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. The accuracy and robustness of the proposed space error estimator are assessed through a series of numerical experiments on both manufactured and benchmark incompressible flow problems. Additionally, its performance is compared in selected cases with the space error estimator proposed by Irisarri and Hauke (2021).

title: Asymptotic behaviors of solutions to the critical fractional $p$-Laplace equations with Hardy potential
abstract: In this paper we consider positive weak solutions $u\in\mathcal{D}^{s,p}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$ to the critical fractional $p$-Laplace equation with Hardy potential $(-Δ_p)^s u-μ\frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{ps}}=u^{p_s^{*}-1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{N}$, where $N\geqslant 2$, $s\in(0,1)$, $p\in(1,\infty)$ satisfying $ps<N$, $p_s^{*}=\frac{Np}{N-ps}$ and $μ\in(0,\mathcal{C}_{N,s,p})$, $\mathcal{C}_{N,s,p}$ denotes the sharp constant of the fractional Hardy inequality. By means of a suitable comparison principle for weak subsolutions and supersolutions of the equations $(-Δ_p)^sf=\big(\fracμ{|x|^{ps}}+a(x)\big)f^{p-1}$ on general open set $Ω$, with nonzero exterior data and $a\in L^{\frac{N}{ps}}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$, combined with careful constructions of the weak subsolutions and supersolutions, we prove that every positive weak solution $u$ of the above problem satisfies $C^{-1}\leqslant|x|^{μ_1}(1+|x|)^{μ_2-μ_1}u(x)\leqslant C$ for a.e. $x\in\mathbb{R}^{N}$, where $μ_1<μ_2$ are the two roots of the indicial equation associated with the Hardy operator and $C\in[1,\infty)$ depends on $u$. Also, we show that the constant $C$ cannot be chosen to depend only on $N$, $s$, $p$ and $μ$.

title: Base Change Of Local Fundamental Group Schemes
abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $K/k$ a field extension, $X$ a geometrically reduced connected scheme proper over $k$, and $x\in X(k)$. We study when the natural homomorphism $π^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrowπ^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. If $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated, then it is an isomorphism for every algebraic extension $K/k$. If $π^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then it is an isomorphism if $K/k$ is purely transcendental or $k$ is algebraically closed. Combining these results, if $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated and $π^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then the natural homomorphism $π^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrow π^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. As an application, if $X_{\bar k}$ is smooth and rationally chain connected, then the natural homomorphism $π^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\longrightarrowπ^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism.

title: Representation Theory and the Algebraic K-Theory of Geometric Fields
abstract: We apply a derived completion construction for commutative ring spectra to give a description of the K-theory spectrum of a geometric field F (i.e. containing an algebraically closed subfield $k$) of characteristic zero purely in terms of the representation theory of its absolute Galois group $G_F$. A result that follows is that the l-adically completed Milnor K-theory of F is isomorphic to the derived completion of the representation ring of $G_F$. The main result, from which this follows, is that $K(F)$ completed at l is equivalent to the derived completion of the K-theory of the category of finite dimensional representations of $G_F$ in $k$.

title: Covering numbers of metric spaces
abstract: We propose and provide evidence for the following conjecture: the covering number of a product of metric spaces with the sum metric is greater than or equal to the product of their covering numbers. This generalizes Vizing's conjecture in graph theory. We prove an infinitesimal version of the conjecture for Finsler manifolds of dimension at least six.

title: Trust-region high-index saddle dynamics for ill-conditioned saddle-point computation
abstract: We propose a trust-region high-index saddle dynamics (TRHiSD) framework for computing high-index saddle points in ill-conditioned problems. To address the deterioration of high-index saddle dynamics caused by inappropriate step sizes and search directions, we exploit its intrinsic local min--max structure and construct separate trust-region subproblems on the maximization and minimization subspaces to adapt the two trust-region radii to different local curvature scales. Under suitable assumptions and with exact spectral subspaces, we prove local linear convergence of the Cauchy-point variant and local quadratic convergence of the Newton-step variant. Numerical experiments on modified Rosenbrock functions are consistent with the predicted convergence rates. For the Landau--de Gennes model, a TRHiSD variant using a truncated conjugate-gradient step for the minimization subproblem substantially reduces the outer-iteration count and the wall-clock time in the tested cases.

title: Counting circles in Kleinian circle packings
abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a bounded Kleinian circle packing with symmetry group $Γ$, and let $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ denote the number of circles in $\mathcal{P}$ of radius at least $T^{-1}$. We obtain an asymptotic formula for $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ in which the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator below the continuous spectrum contribute a finite sum of main terms, with an error term having the same exponent as in the counting theorem of Lax--Phillips for $Γ$-orbits in $\mathbb H^3$.

title: Integral Exponential Series: Fibonacci Weights and Implicit Equations
abstract: We apply classical prime-power congruence criteria to two families of exponential series. For the Fibonacci numbers $F_n$, we characterize the polynomials \(P\in\Z[T]\) for which $\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}P(F_n)x^n/n)$ has integer coefficients: this holds if and only if $P$ is even and $P(0)\equiv P(1)\equiv P(2)\pmod5$. In particular, $5$ is the least positive multiplier for each positive even power of $F_n$, and the series with weights $5F_n^{2k}$ has degree $5^{k-1}$ over \(\Q(x)\) for $k\ge1$. For \(R_n(y)\in\Z[y]\) satisfying $R_{pn}(y)\equiv R_n(y)\pmod p$ for every prime $p$ and every $n\ge1$, we prove that $H(x,y)=\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}R_n(y)^n x^n/n)$ belongs to \(\Z[y][[x]]\) and that $A(x)=H(x,A(x))$ has a unique integral solution. For \(q\in \Z\), taking $R_n(y)=q^n+y$ proves the conjecture in OEIS A163138; the Fibonacci result proves the conjecture in A207969 and A207970. For the implicit family with indeterminate $q$, the coefficient of $x^n$ has degree $n^2$, leading coefficient $1/n$, and nonnegative integer coefficients in the binomial basis, for every $n\ge1$.

title: On the reduction of GAP Conjecture to certain classes of groups and around
abstract: In this note we revise our approach from [Rostislav Grigorchuk. On the gap conjecture concerning group growth. Bull. Math. Sci., 4(1):113--128, 2014] to the reduction of the Gap Conjecture on Group Growth to the class of just-infinite groups. For this purpose we introduce the class of groups that we call \emph{(GAPSY)} as well as some other classes. The properties of these classes are discussed in the relation with growth, elementary amenability, and just-infiniteness. Additionally, we discuss the GAP type problems for cancellative semigroups. A number of (old and new) open problems and few historical remarks is included in the note as well.

title: Auslander-Reiten relations and local finiteness in extriangulated categories
abstract: Let $\mathcal C$ be a Hom-finite Krull--Schmidt extriangulated category over a commutative artin ring. Write ${\rm Rel}(\mathcal C)$ for the subgroup of the split Grothendieck group generated by the relations of all $\mathbb E$-triangles, and ${\rm AR}(\mathcal C)$ for the subgroup generated by those coming from Auslander--Reiten $\mathbb E$-triangles. We first prove that either one-sided finiteness condition on Hom supports implies ${\rm Rel}(\mathcal C)={\rm AR}(\mathcal C)$. For incoming Hom supports, the proof uses a Jordan--Hölder filtration of the contravariant defect. The outgoing case follows by duality. This gives a new proof of the implication from local finiteness to generation by Auslander--Reiten relations. Our argument uses defects and induction on their composition length. In this way, it avoids the radical filtration argument used by Zhu and Zhuang. We then sssume that $\mathcal C$ has enough projectives and injectives, and prove that $\mathcal C$ is locally finite if and only if its projective and injective subcategories are locally finite, the Euler functions associated with Auslander--Reiten relations have finite support, stable and costable morphisms detect ordinary morphisms away from the projective and injective boundary, and ${\rm Rel}(\mathcal C)={\rm AR}(\mathcal C)$. Our results recover the classical module and triangulated cases. They also explain why the two one-sided support conditions are equivalent in the triangulated setting, but may differ in a general extriangulated category.

title: Strong error estimates for finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise
abstract: This paper is concerned with strong error estimates for fully discrete finite element approximations of the stochastic Burgers--Huxley equation with multiplicative noise. We use the implicit Euler--Maruyama scheme for time discretization and continuous piecewise linear finite elements for spatial discretization. Moment bounds and exponential integrability estimates are established and used with the discrete stochastic Gronwall inequality to derive error estimates in full expectation. Sub-second-moment error estimates are first obtained in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm and the discrete $L^2$-in-time $H^1$-norm. Second-moment error estimates in the discrete maximum-in-time $L^2$-norm are then established using a higher-moment argument. The convergence rates are of order $k^{1/2}$ in time and $h$ in space, with the spatial rate being optimal in the $H^1$-norm. Finally, numerical experiments are provided to examine the convergence rates and the influence of multiplicative noise on the solution.

title: The graph $a$-Turán theorem
abstract: We prove analogues of Turán's theorem and the Erdős--Stone theorem for graph $a$-numbers. The $i$th $a$-number $a_i(G)$ equals the $i$th rational Betti number of the real toric manifold associated with the graph associahedron of $G$. We show that the Turán graph $T_r(n)$ maximizes every $a$-number among $K_{r+1}$-free graphs on $n$ vertices. We also show that for any fixed graph $H$ with at least one edge and each fixed $i\geq1$, the limiting extremal density of the $i$th $a$-number among $H$-free graphs depends only on the chromatic number of $H$. Since $a_1(G)$ is the number of edges of $G$, these results recover the two classical theorems in degree one and extend them to higher $a$-numbers.

title: Stationary Phase along Rays and the Determinant of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families
abstract: We study the top-weight sheaf $\mathcal W_n$ of linearly constrained Kloosterman sums over finite fields of odd characteristic, of rank $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$. A local Fourier-transform analysis describes wild monodromy at infinity along rays through nonescaping critical points and their quadratic characters, giving explicit Swan conductors and the escape locus. The resulting stationary-phase description yields a ray-theoretic proof of the geometric determinant. A reflection pairing and a Frobenius calculation at the tame endpoint recover the arithmetic determinant $\det\mathcal W_n\simeq\mathcal L_ψ(-2^{n-1}λ^{-1}\sum_i h_i)\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell(-(n+1)r(n)/2)$. We obtain reciprocity for exterior-power Frobenius traces, the exact distribution of normalized determinants, and spectral compression on symmetric loci. Assuming the ambient connected-monodromy theorem from companion work, we determine the monodromy of the geometric generic ray. Further results include bounds for complete exponential sums, conductor identities for selected parameter curves, and the Euler characteristic of the parameter torus. Rank-two boundary conormal calculations are separated from higher-codimension characteristic-cycle recursions, which remain conditional on explicit microlocal hypotheses.

title: A Lower-envelope Eikonal Neural Operator
abstract: We propose the Lower-envelope Eikonal Neural Operator (LENO), a physics-informed neural operator for eikonal equations with heterogeneous velocity fields and general source sets. LENO encodes the variational minimum principle of viscosity solutions by constructing source-wise candidate fields and taking their pointwise minimum. This lower-envelope structure enforces the source condition exactly and represents nonsmooth multi-source solutions without a soft boundary penalty. The model is trained without precomputed solution data, using a Godunov upwind residual as the sole training signal. Experiments on point sources and curve sources, sample-dependent piecewise velocity fields, and OpenFWI CurveVel-A and Style-A media show accurate agreement with references of Fast Marching Method (FMM). Additional validation shows that the Godunov residual outperforms conventional finite difference residuals on a high-resolution test, that velocity conditioning and the lower-envelope transform are essential in realistic heterogeneous media, and that the trained operator supports efficient batched evaluation and resolution transfer.

title: Counterexample to Flow-Transfer Conjectures
abstract: An edge map $f:E(G)\to E(H)$ between graphs is called an $FT_M$ map if the pullback of every $M$-tension on $H$ is an $M$-flow on $G$; equivalently, the pullback of every $M$-valued 1-coboundary is an $M$-valued 1-cycle. The correspondence between restricted tensions and homomorphisms to Cayley graphs motivates two flow analogues. An $(M,B)$-flow (or tension), is an $M$-flow (resp. $M$-tension) taking values in $B$. For subsets $B=-B\subseteq M$ with $M$ an abelian group, Šámal conjectured that a graph admits an $(M,B)$-flow if and only if it admits an $FT_M$ map to the Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(M,B)$. DeVos conjectured that, whenever there is a graph homomorphism $\operatorname{Cay}(M,B)\to\operatorname{Cay}(M',B')$, every graph admitting an $(M,B)$-flow also admits an $(M',B')$-flow. We prove that these conjectures are equivalent and give a counterexample using the Petersen graph.

title: MA(1) processes with uniform innovations conditioned to stay positive in the expanding regime
abstract: We study MA(1) processes with uniform innovations conditioned to remain positive for a long time when $|θ|>1$, where $θ$ denotes the coupling parameter. We show that, for a fixed starting point, the finite-dimensional distributions of the conditioned process converge and identify the limiting process as a Doob $h$-transform with explicit function $h$. We also obtain precise asymptotics for the corresponding persistence probabilities. The limiting process exhibits qualitatively different behaviour depending on $θ$ and on the support of the innovation distribution. We also determine stationary distributions of the limiting conditioned processes for all $θ\ne 1$.

title: Tautological generation of preprojective BPS cohomology
abstract: Let $Q$ be a quiver and let $\mathbf{d}$ be a dimension vector. We prove that the affinized BPS cohomology of the stack of $\mathbf{d}$-dimensional representations of the preprojective algebra $Π_Q$ is generated by its reduced virtual fundamental class under the action of tautological classes. This is a generalisation to singular quiver varieties of the Kirwan surjectivity statement of McGerty-Nevins for smooth framed quiver varieties. We prove that the statement holds for every King stability condition. To prove this, we attach legs to vertices of $Q$ and construct a correspondence with a smooth quiver variety for the extended quiver. This correspondence sends the reduced virtual fundamental class of the singular preprojective quiver stack to the Vandermonde determinant capped with the fundamental class of the smooth preprojective quiver stack for the leg-extended quiver. We construct the Weyl group action by the simultaneous Springer resolution of Dobrovolska-Ginzburg-Travkin, providing a comparison of the cohomology of fibres. This comparison preserves the tautological Chern classes. The sign-isotypic formula involving Kac polynomials of Hausel-Letellier-Rodriguez-Villegas, combined with Kirwan surjectivity for smooth framed quiver varieties of McGerty-Nevins, then implies the tautological generation theorem. We also describe the sign isotypic component of the cohomology of quiver varieties using the real-root subalgebras of the BPS Lie algebra. The tautological generation result can be extended via similar methods to deformed preprojective algebras of Crawley-Boevey-Holland at central parameters.

title: Fréchet structure over AF algebras I: The compact case
abstract: This is the first of two papers devoted to spatial Fréchet structures on AF algebras and their derivations. Here, we study the simplest example of such a structure: the Fréchet algebra of almost-local compact operators associated with a fixed orthonormal basis. We revisit the characterization of its continuous derivations in terms of infinite matrices and their operator-theoretic implementation on rapidly decreasing vectors. Reformulating this description in the language of 0-chains, borrowed from the theory of quantum many-body systems, we establish a sufficient condition for continuity in terms of spatial growth. Finally, we construct a Fréchet-continuous symmetric derivation that does not generate a one-parameter group of automorphisms of this algebra that is strongly continuous with respect to its Fréchet topology.

title: On the algebraic Mackey deformation
abstract: This paper provides a conceptual understanding of the Mackey bijection from the admissible dual of a real reductive group $G$ into the admissible dual of its Cartan motion group $G_0$, by studying the primitive spectrum of a Hecke algebra over $\mathbb{C}[t]$ arising from the contraction of $G$ to $G_0$. If $K$ denotes a maximal compact subgroup of $G$, our approach leads to the following two results: the admissible Mackey bijection is a piecewise homeomorphism, each piece being defined by the length of the lowest $K$-types; the Hecke algebras of $G$ and $G_0$ have, up to $K$-types not exceeding a certain length, the same periodic cyclic homology.

title: Recurrence and Transience in Monotone Environments: Increasing Conductances and Growing Domains
abstract:
We study discrete-time random walks on a locally finite graph whose conductances are non-decreasing in time and bounded on each edge. We compare their hitting probabilities with those of the time-homogeneous walk obtained by fixing the conductances at the starting time. These estimates give proofs of two results established in greater generality by Li and Park: if the upper network is recurrent, every vertex is visited infinitely often almost surely; if the initial network is transient, the expected number of visits to each vertex is finite.
  In a finite domain, the difference between the two exit probabilities is bounded by the square root of the product of a capacity increment and a dual energy. We obtain a corresponding infinite-volume estimate for the probability of never hitting a given vertex. To prove these estimates, we compare two Dirichlet forms and use a contraction property of the killed transition operators.
  We also consider walks on increasing finite sets. On each prescribed time interval, called a plateau, the transition operator is fixed. A lower bound on transition probabilities after mixing and an upper bound on the expected number of returns give a sufficient condition for every vertex to be visited infinitely often almost surely. For uniformly elliptic lazy walks on boxes of radius $R_n$ in $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\geq3$, it is enough that $\sum_n(L_n-b_n)_+/R_n^d$ diverges, where $L_n$ is the duration of the $n$th plateau and $b_n=\lceil aR_n^2\rceil$.

title: A projective Calabi--Yau threefold in characteristic 5 non-liftable to characteristic 0
abstract: We construct a smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold $X_5$ over $\mathbb F_5$ with $b_3(X_5)=0$ and $b_2(X_5)=31$. Consequently, $X_5$ has no smooth proper lifting to characteristic zero, including over ramified bases. To our knowledge, this is the first smooth projective Calabi--Yau threefold with this property in characteristic $p>3$. The threefold is a crepant resolution of the Kummer quotient of the self-fiber product of a rational elliptic surface. We prove the vanishing of its third Betti number by semistable reduction and point counts. A birational double-octic model gives a direct obstruction to lifting to the ring of Witt vectors of length two, through an explicit inconsistent system of linear equations for the branch data. We also determine the Hodge and crystalline cohomology: the threefold is infinitesimally rigid, its crystalline cohomology is torsion-free, and its third de Rham cohomology vanishes. Its Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence has exactly two nonzero differentials, both of rank one on the second page.

title: Wasserstein Stability of the Nerve Map
abstract: Given a locally finite open cover of a paracompact space, a subordinate partition of unity defines a map into the geometric realization of the nerve. When the cover is good, the nerve theorem asserts that this map is a homotopy equivalence. In applied topology, one specializes this construction to covers of metric data by open balls centered at finitely many landmarks. The corresponding nerve map represents the data inside the Čech complex, enabling one to pull cohomological or spectral invariants back to the data. Since point cloud data often comes equipped with weights encoding domain-specific importance, we introduce a weighted version of the nerve map and study its stability under perturbations of the landmarks and weights using metrics from optimal transport. Our main result is a Lipschitz stability theorem for the weighted nerve map under a uniform nondegeneracy assumption. We state the bound in terms of a scale-dependent optimal transport distance, and give an example where our estimate is attained. Since this distance is dominated by a multiple of the $1$-Wasserstein distance, Wasserstein stability follows as a corollary. We also give geometric conditions ensuring nondegeneracy, obtain explicit estimates of the Lipschitz constant for closed Riemannian manifolds, and sketch applications to Laplacian eigenvector cascading and Eilenberg--MacLane coordinates.

title: Concatenated Codes with One Inner Code: Low-Rate Gilbert-Varshamov Asymptotics from Algebraic-Geometric Codes
abstract: Constructing codes that attain the Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound while admitting efficient encoding and decoding is a fundamental problem in coding theory. We study concatenated codes that reuse a single binary inner code across all outer coordinates. To exploit existing encoding and decoding algorithms, we restrict the outer codes to random subcodes of scaled copies of prescribed algebraic codes and investigate their minimum distance. Our first contribution is a general upper bound on the minimum-distance failure probability that separates two terms controlled by the inner code's bias moments and the dual weight distribution of the prescribed code, together with sufficient conditions for exponential decay. Our second contribution is a concrete construction satisfying these conditions using algebraic-geometric codes from the Garcia-Stichtenoth tower. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, we construct a family of random binary codes $C_m$ whose rates approach $\varepsilon^2$ and satisfy \[ \Pr\left[δ(C_m)\geq\frac12-\sqrt{\frac{\ln 2}{2}}\left(\varepsilon+\frac{\varepsilon^3}{2}\right)\right]\geq 1-2^{-c\varepsilon^4N_m}, \] for all sufficiently large $m$, where $N_m$ is the block length and $c>0$ is independent of $\varepsilon$ and $m$. Thus, the distance guarantee matches the leading coefficient of the GV bound at low rates. For each fixed $\varepsilon$, the construction uses a single inner encoding map throughout the family and admits polynomial-time encoding and unique decoding within a guaranteed radius. This answers the question of Doron, Mosheiff, and Wootters for subcodes of scaled algebraic geometry codes at low rates.

title: Null designs and switching in polynomial spaces
abstract: Null designs are finite point configurations with real weights whose polynomial moments vanish up to a given degree. In Godsil's framework of polynomial spaces, we give elementary proofs of sharp lower bounds on the number of points in the Euclidean and spherical cases. We characterize the spherical null designs attaining the bound and give explicit formulas for their weights. We then study how null designs can be used to replace part of a weighted design while preserving its polynomial moments. We give conditions ensuring nonnegative weights and apply the minimum-size classification to switching on circles. Examples on spheres and in Hamming and Johnson spaces illustrate these results, including a replacement between noncongruent spherical $5$-designs that preserves equal weights and the number of points.

title: Congruences Modulo 16, 32 and 64 for a Restricted Overpartition Function
abstract: Let $\overline{t}^{(3)}(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$ in which consecutive parts differ by a multiple of $3$ unless the larger part is overlined, and the smallest part is overlined unless it is divisible by $3$. Using dissections of theta functions, we establish two infinite families of congruences modulo $32$ and $64$. We also obtain two residue formulas modulo $16$ and use them to derive four further infinite families of congruences modulo $16$. In particular, for every positive integer $M$ and nonnegative integer $n$, the residue of $\overline{t}^{(3)}(M^2(18n+12))$ modulo $16$ is $8$ if $6n+4$ is a square and $0$ otherwise.

title: Fast circular convolution with periodic kernels
abstract: We study the periodic circular convolution or PCC, where the convolution kernel depends periodically on the spatial location. We introduce two fast algorithms to compute the PCC that rely on the Discrete Fourier Transform. One of the algorithms reveals that the matrix representation of the PCC is unitarily equivalent to a block diagonal matrix, which facilitates the analysis of PCCs and operations such as their product and inversion. We present two sample applications. One to deconvolve the action of an optical system whose point spread function depends periodically in space. The second is to compute dispersion relations for a periodic chain of masses.

title: The lower boundary of the $\{K_2,K_{p},K_{q}\}$-profile
abstract: We determine the asymptotically sharp minimum number of $q$-cliques that appear in any $n$-vertex graph with $γn^2$ edges and $δn^{p}$ $p$-cliques for $q>p>2$. The question of determining the minimum number of $r$-cliques that appear in any $n$-vertex graph with $γn^2$ edges was previously resolved by Razborov for $r=3$, Nikiforov for $r=4$ and Reiher for all $r\geq 5$. For all $r\geq 3$, the minimum is attained by a complete multipartite graph where all parts are equal except for one that can be smaller or by a limit of such graphs. Very recently, Ma, Wang and Zhu as well as Li, Liu and Zhang showed that the same construction is also a minimizer for the number of $r$-cliques when the number of $s$-cliques is fixed for any $2\leq s<r$. A minimizer in our setting is the disjoint union of the same complete multipartite graph with an independent set. This establishes the lower boundary of the three-dimensional $\{K_2, K_p, K_q\}$-profile.

title: A Diophantine definition of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $\mathbb{Q}$
abstract:
We prove that the integers form a Diophantine subset of the rational numbers. More precisely, there exist an integer $n\ge1$ and a polynomial $P\in\mathbb{Z}[T,W_1,\dots,W_n]$ of total degree at most four such that $q\in\mathbb{Q}$ is an integer if and only if $P(q,\mathbf w)=0$ for some $\mathbf w\in\mathbb{Q}^n$. Consequently, any recursively enumerable subset of $\mathbb{Q}^r$ is Diophantine, and Mazur's conjecture on the topology of rational points fails.
  The proof is inspired by OpenAI's work on Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb{Q}$. It does not use the $2$-converse or the $2$-adic Fontaine--Mazur results announced and employed by OpenAI. We define the rational numbers with square denominator using rational points on certain quadratic twists of the congruent number elliptic curve. The criterion of Tian, Yuan and Zhang, in Smith's formulation, implies that these quadratic twists have analytic rank one. A height estimate for rational points on a fixed quotient of a Shimura curve allows us to express multiplication of elliptic-curve indices. We obtain this estimate by bounding the modular levels of the associated quaternionic abelian surfaces. The level bound is based on a compatible system of Galois representations over $\mathbb{Q}$ with controlled ramification and on Khare--Wintenberger's proof of Serre's conjecture. Green--Tao--Ziegler's theorem on linear patterns of primes supplies the rational solutions needed for a Diophantine model of integer arithmetic.

title: Visibility graphs of irregularly sampled two-dimensional fields via Voronoi tessellations
abstract: Visibility graphs map a time series into a network by linking two data whenever the straight line between them is not obstructed by intermediate data. Their extension to two-dimensional fields has so far been restricted to regular lattices, where visibility is checked along a finite number of lattice directions. We propose a definition for scalar data sampled at arbitrary, irregularly scattered points of the plane. Each point is assigned its Voronoi cell, so that the data become a landscape of prisms, and two points are linked when the line of sight between them clears the cells crossed by the connecting segment. This yields horizontal ($\HVGV$) and natural ($\NVGV$) Voronoi visibility graphs that reduce exactly to the classical horizontal and natural visibility graphs when the points are collinear, contain the Gabriel graph of the point set, and can be built by an exact walk through the Delaunay triangulation. For uncorrelated heights, the horizontal graph depends only on the ranks of the data, so its statistics are independent of the marginal distribution. The probability that two points see each other is $2/[(M+1)(M+2)]$, where $M$ is the number of Voronoi cells crossed, which reduces the problem to the geometry of the tessellation. For Poisson points this gives a degree distribution with a scale-free tail $P(k)\simeq(π^3/4)\,k^{-2}$ and a mean degree that grows as $(π^3/8)\ln N$, in contrast with the finite value $\langle k\rangle=4$ of one-dimensional series. Two dimensions are therefore the marginal case in which isotropic horizontal visibility ceases to be local. Numerical simulations with up to $N=1.28\times10^5$ points support these predictions.

title: Global-in-time dynamics of the pressureless Euler/incompressible non-Newtonian equations
abstract: This paper addresses a two-phase fluid system on the periodic domain $\mathbb{T}^3$, consisting of the pressureless Euler equations and the incompressible non-Newtonian equations coupled through a drag force. We prove the global-in-time existence of strong solutions to this system for a certain class of stress tensors in the non-Newtonian fluid. Our proof combines a priori large-time behavior estimates for classical solutions with a bootstrapping argument on the $L^2$-Sobolev norms, which effectively handles the difficulties caused by the lack of dissipation in the density of the Euler equation.

title: Polynomial Swap Coboundary Expansion with Applications to LTCs and PCPs
abstract:
Swap coboundary expansion, introduced independently by Bafna--Minzer and Dikstein--Dinur, is a local-to-global property that underlies agreement tests in the low-acceptance regime and recent constructions of succinct PCPs. Previous works obtained bounds of $\exp(-O(\sqrt{r}))$ for the $r$-swap coboundary expansion of Chapman--Lubotzky complexes. We establish the first inverse-polynomial bounds for bounded-degree complexes: suitable skeleta of Kac--Moody--Steinberg (KMS) complexes have $r$-swap coboundary expansion at least $r^{-O(1)}$.
  Our theorem supplies a key ingredient in forthcoming work of Ben Yaacov--Dikstein--Liu, which obtains local tests for sparse algebraic codes with guarantees even at arbitrarily small acceptance probability. These tests use $\exp(\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon))$ queries and guarantee that any word accepted with probability at least $\varepsilon$ agrees with a codeword on an $\varepsilon^{O(1)}$ fraction of coordinates. Separately, substituting our bound into the existing analysis of Bafna--Minzer--Vyas--Yun improves the soundness dependence of their two-query PCP construction, giving perfect completeness, soundness $\varepsilon$, and proof length $n(\log n)^{\exp(\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon))}$.
  Our proof exploits the product structure of the groups arising in KMS complexes. The main new ingredient is a decomposition lemma for Dehn functions, which separates the analysis of group relations into independent problems on much smaller factors, with only polynomial overhead.

title: Nondifferentiability on Irrational Invariant Graphs of Smooth Area-Preserving Twist Maps
abstract: For a fixed irrational rotation number and every $1\le r<\infty$, we construct an exact area-preserving $C^r$ twist map preserving a Lipschitz graph. The set of nondifferentiability points has Hausdorff dimension $d=2/(r+1)$ and zero $d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. At the same rotation number, we construct a $C^\infty$ twist map whose invariant graph is nondifferentiable on exactly one two-sided orbit. The dynamics on these graphs has wandering intervals.

title: Beyond Curvature Bias: Higher-Order Manifold Fitting via Multiscale Cancellation
abstract:
Local manifold-fitting procedures smooth noisy observations
  over neighborhoods of scale $h$, inducing a systematic normal bias of order $h^2+σ^2$ that persists at the population level. We develop geometric bias cancellation (GBC), a multiscale framework for higher-order manifold recovery under ambient Gaussian noise. For procedures admitting a normal-bias expansion $c(h,σ)b(x)+O(h^4)$, we construct cross-scale correspondence using estimated normal fibers and show that second-order normal accuracy suffices for fourth-order correspondence accuracy. Canceling the leading geometric bias yields $O(h^4)$ population Hausdorff accuracy while preserving an embedded manifold diffeomorphic to the underlying manifold. We establish the required expansions and finite-sample recovery guarantees for successive tangent-space projection and Gaussian density ridges. For STSP, geometric bias cancellation also achieves an asymptotically vanishing Hausdorff error ratio relative to oracle bandwidth-tuned single-scale fitting. For the local contraction estimator of \citet{yao2023manifold}, we identify an obstruction to scalar bias cancellation and develop a directional cancellation achieving $O(σ^4)$ population Hausdorff accuracy with uniform positive reach, as well as fourth-order finite-sample accuracy when $n\gtrsimσ^{-(d+6)}\log(1/σ)$. Simulations confirm the predicted improvement from second- to fourth-order population bias.

title: A Polynomial Bound on Split Rank
abstract: We prove that the split rank of a rational pure-integer polyhedron is polynomially bounded in its input length, resolving a conjecture of Basu, Conforti, Di Summa, and Jiang. If the defining system has dense binary encoding length $L$, then $O((L+1)^9)$ split rounds suffice to reach the integer hull in arbitrary dimension.

title: Asymptotic analysis of infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with squared Bessel arrival intensity
abstract: This paper introduces a model for infinite-server queues driven by a Cox process with stochastic intensity given by a squared Bessel (BESQ) process. Exploiting the affine structure of the underlying dynamics, we derive a closed-form expression for the joint moment-generating function (MGF) of the arrival intensity, the number of customers in the system, and the integral of the number of customers in the system over a time interval. The asymptotic properties of the model are also analysed. We establish laws of large numbers, central limit theorems, large deviation principles, and moderate deviation principles for several quantities of interest. More precisely, these results are obtained for three important settings: cumulative occupancy over a finite time interval, system occupancy under a diverging long-run mean arrival intensity, and the superposition of independent infinite-server queues with Cox-BESQ arrival intensities. Numerical experiments illustrate the associated rate functions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the resulting rare-event approximations.

title: Congruence density under sublattice inclusion
abstract: Gábor Czédli introduced congruence density and investigated how it changes under sublattice extensions. We prove that density cannot increase: if $S$ is a sublattice of a finite lattice $L$, then $\cd(L)\leq2^{-d}\cd(S)$, where $d$ is the larger of the increases in the numbers of join-reducible and meet-reducible elements. We also determine when equality holds: $\cd(L)=\cd(S)$ precisely when every element of $L\setminus S$ is comparable with every element of $L$. The theorem of Czédli and Szabó relating quasiorders to pairs of congruences gives the corresponding results for quasiorder density.

title: Gradient Flows over Convex Bodies for Learning Optimal Regularizers
abstract:
We consider the question of describing gradient flows over the collection of convex bodies. This is motivated by foundational questions arising in inverse problems. Suppose we wish to solve an ill-posed inverse problem using regularization techniques. Can we learn an optimal choice of a convex regularizer directly from prior data? Given a numerical algorithm that computes such an optimal regularizer, is there a principled manner for describing the evolution of its iterates? The objective of this paper is to lay the foundation towards answering these questions.
  To this end, we consider a criterion of an optimal regularizer based on seeking a convex body that minimizes the expected gauge evaluation with respect to a prior data distribution subject to a volume constraint. The formulation is initially nonconvex, but admits hidden convexity by passing to its polar. We characterize the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions that certify global optimality. We also analyze the $L^2$-gradient flow as well as a minimizing movement scheme with the Hausdorff penalty. Our results show that the objective gap decays exponentially along the gradient flow and we obtain dimension-dependent rates for both the objective gap and distance to the optimal body for the Hausdorff scheme. Finally, we apply the KKT conditions to identify explicit optimal convex bodies. For data where the optimal nonconvex regularizer is the $\ell_p$-quasinorm, $p \in (0,1)$, the optimal convex regularizer is the volume-normalized $\ell_1$-ball. For data described by paired basis atoms, the optimal convex regularizer is the polar of a shifted zonotope.

title: Quantization of Betti Mapping Stacks
abstract: We describe a quantization procedure for Betti mapping stacks with shifted Poisson targets by combining factorization homology and formal geometry. We quantize derived stacks of local systems of low-dimensional manifolds.

title: Subgroup distortion in free-by-cyclic groups with linearly growing monodromy
abstract: Let $G=F\rtimes_φ\mathbb Z$ be the mapping torus of a linearly growing UPG automorphism $φ$ of a finitely generated free group $F$. We compute the distortion of every finitely generated subgroup $H$ of $G$, and we show that it is linear, quadratic or exponential. In contrast, for each $d\ge2$, Dison and Riley constructed an automorphism of polynomial degree $d$ whose mapping torus contains a free subgroup with distortion equivalent to the Ackermann function $A_{d+1}$, which grows faster than every iterated exponential function. Using the natural splitting of $G$ over $\mathbb Z^2$ subgroups and its topological representative, we associate to $H$ a family of \emph{horizontal components}, together with \emph{dilation homomorphisms} defined from slopes along these components. We prove that $H$ is undistorted in $G$ if and only if every horizontal component of $H$ consists of only one piece. Otherwise, the distortion of $H$ is quadratic if all dilation homomorphisms are trivial, and exponential if one of them is nontrivial. Along the way, we show that the distortion of $H$ is determined, up to superadditive closure, by the distortions of the stabilizers of its horizontal components.

title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties
abstract:
Building on Liu's and Liu--Sheshmani's systematized description of Kontsevich's localization methods in toric varieties, we develop a computational framework for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of smooth projective toric varieties and their smooth complete intersections. This is grounded in equivariant localization and the combinatorial structure of toric fans. We describe how the geometric data required by the localization formulas can be recovered directly from the fan and extend the existing software for flag varieties to compute the small quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. The implementation also incorporates cyclic determinants and regularized-exponent multisets, providing computational tools for investigating the atomic decomposition of quantum cohomology.
  Using this framework, we obtain the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^5$. Also applying new methods to study Hodge atoms in Fano fivefolds, we recover the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^7$, due to Cavenaghi--Katzarkov--Kontsevich, and we prove the nonrationality of every smooth quartic double fivefold and every smooth quartic fivefold.

title: Non-counital Frobenius algebras and QF-3 algebras
abstract: We show that non-counital Frobenius algebras with injective comultiplication coincide with QF-3 algebras, thereby providing a new characterization of QF-3 algebras. As an application, we recover that gendo-Frobenius algebras, self-injective algebras, and more generally Morita algebras, all admit an injective non-counital Frobenius algebra structure. Furthermore, we construct a canonical family of injective comultiplications on QF-3 algebras that admit a counit if and only if the algebra is Frobenius. This settles a question of Hernandez--Walton--Yadav and unifies a wealth of results in the literature. We conclude with applications to topological quantum field theories and Poincaré duality algebras.

title: Pointwise Convergence and Approximation of Matrix-Transform Means of Vilenkin--Fourier Series
abstract: We study convergence, divergence, and approximation of matrix-transform means of Vilenkin--Fourier series. For bounded groups, we prove convergence along ${M_n}$ at Vilenkin--Lebesgue points without additional diagonal conditions. For arbitrary bounded or unbounded groups, every regular matrix-transform method admits divergence on any prescribed null set along any increasing sequence. We also obtain $L_p(G_m)$ approximation estimates in terms of the modulus of continuity.

title: Affine Springer Fibers and Slodowy varieties
abstract: In this paper, we study the geometry of certain affine Springer fibers. In particular, we generalize the construction of Lusztig in "Remarks on affine Springer fibres" to identify a locally closed subvariety in terms of some Lagrangian in the resolution of the nilpotent Slodowy slice. We use this description to prove some geometric properties of these affine Springer fibers, including existence of affine pavings and equidimensionality of affine Spaltenstein varieties.

title: Entire boosted hypersurfaces of vanishing mean curvature in Schwarzschild spacetime
abstract: We prove the existence of entire maximal hypersurfaces, asymptotic to suitable coordinate-dependent boosts in the two asymptotically flat ends of maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime. As a corollary, this generates a foliation of maximal hypersurfaces in exterior Schwarzschild, which corresponds to a geometric choice of time function associated with any boost parameter. As a crucial step in the proof, we introduce a novel rotationally symmetric time function in maximally extended Schwarzschild, which is Cauchy and has properties of independent interest.

title: Many more odd zeta values are irrational
abstract: We prove that for any sufficiently large odd integer $s$, there exist at least \[ 2.78 \, \sqrt{\frac{s \log\log s}{\log s}} \] irrational values among $ζ(3), ζ(5), \dots, ζ(s)$, where $ζ$ is the Riemann zeta function. This improves on the best known estimate by a constant factor times $\sqrt{ \log\log s}$. The proof combines the elimination technique and an arithmetic lemma of Fischler--Sprang--Zudilin, the hypergeometric constructions of Lai--Yu, and the Hankel determinant method that appeared in the proof that $ζ(5)$ is irrational posted by Fauzan on September 17, 2026.

title: Floating Body Asymptotics via Fractal Strings
abstract: Schütt and Werner associated an almost polygonal planar convex body with a decreasing convex sequence and obtained two-sided estimates for the area removed by its floating body. We reinterpret the gaps of the defining sequence as the lengths of a normalized fractal string. Our main result shows that the area deficit, that is, the difference between the area of the set and its floating body, is comparable to an integral transform of the inner tubular volume of this string. As a consequence, if the string has Minkowski dimension $D$, then the principal power exponent of the area deficit is $1-D/3$. We also derive refinements for regularly varying tube functions, establish a realization criterion extending the almost polygonal case of the theorem of Schütt and Werner, and discuss several examples. As an application, we obtain corresponding asymptotic rates for the expectations and variances of the missed area and the number of vertices of random polygons, including new intermediate behaviors between the classical polygonal and smooth cases.

title: An Optimized Expansion Auction Integrating Energy, Flexibility, and Network Constraints
abstract: Auction mechanisms are widely used to support generation investments. In the US, capacity auctions serve as supply-adequacy instruments to address the missing-money problem, whereas in Latin America, energy and capacity auctions procure long-term contracts to support generation expansion. In both settings, accreditation metrics, such as Firm Energy (FE) and Effective Load Carrying Capability (ELCC), are used to approximate the reliability contribution of selected units and winning projects are selected based on a financial offer. This approach fails to recognize the actual contribution of winners to the multiple services they provide to the system. This limitation becomes more significant with high shares of renewables, as the value of each resource increasingly depends on network and technological constraints, as well as on complementarities within the generation portfolio. Inspired by short-term auctions, such as day-ahead markets, this paper proposes a joint optimization-based auction for generation and transmission investments that internalizes these interactions, capturing the intrinsic value of generation candidates without requiring the computation of FE or ELCC metrics. The auctioneer determines the winning portfolio through an expansion-planning model that explicitly represents network constraints, operational interactions, reliability standards, and multiple scenarios. A case study of the Brazilian system indicates lower system costs, lower risk, and a more diverse portfolio relative to the stylized decoupled procurement approaches currently deployed in many systems.

title: Every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra has an untwisted étale groupoid model
abstract: We show that every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra is isomorphic to the $C^*$-algebra of a second countable, locally compact Hausdorff, principal étale groupoid. Equivalently, every such $C^*$-algebra has a $C^*$-diagonal whose Weyl twist is trivial. Together with Evington and Sibbel's recent result for all UCT Kirchberg algebras, this provides untwisted principal groupoid models for every classifiable $C^*$-algebra.

title: Simple Length Multiplicity on X(n)
abstract:
We study multiplicity among lengths of simple closed geodesics on the principal congruence surfaces $X(n)=Γ(n)\backslash\mathbb{H}$. We show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are positive constants $n_\varepsilon,C_{\varepsilon}$ so that, for $n\ge n_\varepsilon$, there are at least $\exp((\frac{π^2}{12}-\varepsilon)n)$ simple closed geodesics on $X(n)$ of the same length $\ell<C_\varepsilon n$. We produce the same multiplicity for $λ$-length of simple arcs with distinct endpoints via the McShane identity, which is immediately relevant as the size of a McShane gap around such an arc is roughly the reciprocal square of its $λ$-length. Our method of proof relies on an independently interesting theorem about the McShane identity for $X(n)$: the total mass of the gaps of pants with two cusps tends to 1 as $n\to \infty$. We present a proof of this latter fact that relies on estimates for the speed of mixing provided by Selberg's 3/16-Theorem (discovered with the help of ChatGPT).
  We indicate several avenues for further investigation.

title: Comparing grade restriction windows to Cox windows
abstract: We introduce a new class of toric varieties which admit an HKKN stratification compatible with the combinatorics of the GKZ fan. This class includes all smooth projective toric varieties of Picard ranks 1 and 2. We show that the grade restriction windows due to Halpern-Leistner and Ballard--Favero--Katzarkov arising from our HKKN stratifications agree with the intrinsic window categories appearing in work of Ballard--Berkesch--Brown--Cranton Heller--Erman--Favero--Ganatra--Hanlon--Huang. On the other hand, we provide an example of a smooth projective toric DM stack where this intrinsic window is never a grade restriction window despite the many possible choices. As an application, we demonstrate that reordering and/or taking a subset of an HKKN stratification sometimes changes the grade restriction window and sometimes does not.

title: Zero detection via Cox random measures
abstract: Using point process theory we propose and investigate a probabilistic identification of zeros of a deterministic real valued function. We construct a random atomic driving measure for a Cox point process whose mass at a candidate location depends explicitly on the value of the function at that location. We study the properties of the constructed random measure, including its exact asymptotic properties, its Laplace functional and related random processes. We also give an important application involving zero detection for Riemann's ξ function.

title: Path Components of Almost Doubly Commuting Fredholm Tuples
abstract: In this article, we prove that the Fredholm index classifies the norm-path components of almost doubly commuting Fredholm n-tuples on a separable infinite dimensional Hilbert space. Using Kasparov's technical theorem, we join each tuple to an essentially normal one by a straight-line Fredholm path and applying the Douglas-Curto theorem.

title: Finiteness properties of Bestvina-Brady kernels for graph products with torsion
abstract: We study Bestvina-Brady kernels associated to graph products whose vertex groups are either infinite cyclic or finite. Using a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ cubical complex constructed by Ruane and Witzel, on which the graph product with defining graph $Γ$ acts, together with an equivariant Morse function, we establish sufficient conditions for homological finiteness properties in terms of the topology of the flag complex $Γ^\blacktriangle$, the subcomplex $Γ^\blacktriangle_\infty$ spanned by the infinite vertices, and the ascending and descending links of certain vertices. We also prove a partial converse, showing that, under additional vanishing hypotheses on homology in the next degree, non-vanishing homology of these complexes obstructs higher finiteness properties of the Bestvina-Brady kernel. The main new features are the presence of finite stabilizers and the resulting additional link conditions, which are expressed in terms of the flag complex of $Γ$. When the finite vertex groups are abelian, we characterize when the kernel has finitely many conjugacy classes of finite subgroups, describe the normalizers of its finite subgroups as Bestvina-Brady kernels of smaller graph products, and obtain a criterion for the kernel to be of Bredon type $\underline{\mathrm{FP}}_n$.

title: Proximal random reshuffling with inexact gradients for nonconvex composite optimization
abstract: We design and justify a proximal inexact random reshuffling method for minimizing sums of the finite average of functions with Lipschitz continuous gradients and lower semicontinuous regularizers that may be nonconvex. Each epoch visits every component once, using inexact gradients with a prescribed tolerance, and ends with a single proximal step. Our analysis is pathwise: it holds for every sequence of permutations and does not depend on how the reshuffling is performed. We show that when the stepsizes and error tolerances satisfy suitable summability conditions, the objective values converge and every accumulation point is stationary. Furthermore, under the Polyak--Łojasiewicz--Kurdyka condition at a single accumulation point and sufficient decrease of stepsizes, the entire sequence has finite length and converges to that point. For polynomial stepsizes and power-type desingularizing functions, we derive convergence rates for objective values and iterates. Finally, faster objective-value rates are derived when the limit is a local minimizer.

authors: Matheus Andrade Ribeiro de Moura Horácio
title: Rigidity of compact quasi-Einstein manifolds with boundary and low-dimensional focal sets
abstract: In this article, we investigate nontrivial compact m-quasi-Einstein manifolds with boundary, m > 1 and constant scalar curvature. We first prove that such a manifold is rigid whenever the set of critical points of its potential function is totally geodesic, which extends to quasi-Einstein manifolds a theorem of Li, Li, Ou, Qu, Wu and Zhou for shrinking Ricci solitons. Then, we prove that, in every dimension, this set is totally geodesic whenever it has dimension two or three, so that the manifold is rigid in this case. The proof is based on a Bochner identity for the covariant derivative of the Ricci tensor at the points of this set. In particular, every such manifold of dimension five is rigid. Finally, we obtain rigidity in arbitrary dimension under an integral Weyl pinching condition when the set of critical points has dimension four.

title: Improved Lower Bounds for Mutually Orthogonal Latin Squares (MOLS) at 33 Orders
abstract: A Latin square of order $n$ is an $n\times n$ array over symbols $\{0,1,\ldots n-1\}$, such that the same symbol does not appear twice in any row or any column. Two Latin squares of order $n$ are orthogonal if, when superimposed, they yield each of the $n^2$ ordered pairs of symbols exactly once. A set of two or more Latin squares are mutually orthogonal Latin squares (MOLS) if each pair of distinct squares is orthogonal. Let $N(n)$ be the maximum size of a set of MOLS of order $n$. For most $n$ which are not prime powers, there is a wide gap between known upper and lower bounds on $N(n)$. This has led to interest in constructing new larger sets of MOLS for explicit values of $n$, to incrementally improve the lower bounds on $N(n)$. This paper provides MOLS that improve the lower bound on $N(n)$ for 33 values of $n$ in the range from 22 through 494. The constructions were found by GPT-6 Astra, and use established techniques including difference matrices, quasi-difference matrices, orthogonal arrays, and projective planes. A highlight is 4 MOLS of order $n=22$; combined with pre-existing results, this establishes $N(n) \geq 4$ for all $n>10$.

title: A geometric characterization of weighted homogeneity for reduced complex analytic germs
abstract: We prove that a reduced complex analytic germ is weighted homogeneous if and only if, in suitable local coordinates, it admits a holomorphic vector field vanishing at the origin and pointing strictly outward along a single sufficiently small link. On a connected link, transversality suffices. The criterion applies in arbitrary codimension, including to non-isolated singularities. The proof uses a compact composition operator to control the spectrum on the Zariski tangent space and obtains a positive grading from the resulting spectral condition.

title: Sharp Bounds for Near-Maximizers of Gaussian Processes
abstract: For a centered Gaussian process $G$ with continuous sample paths on a compact metric space $T$, a continuous drift $f: T \mapsto \mathbb{R}$, a noise level $σ>0$, and $ε\ge 0$, let $A_ε$ be the set of points at which $f+σG$ is within $ε$ of its maximum. Writing $\mathbb{E}\sup_TG$ for the expected supremum of $G$, we prove that the expected squared diameter of $A_ε$ in the canonical pseudometric of $G$ is at most $8ε\mathbb{E}\sup_TG/σ$ and that the expected maximal squared distance from a point of $A_ε$ to an exact maximizer is at most $4ε\mathbb{E}\sup_TG/σ$. The constants cannot be improved uniformly over index sets, processes, and drifts, and no logarithmic factor in $ε$ appears, unlike in bounds integrated from tail estimates. At $ε=0$ the bounds give the almost sure uniqueness of the maximizer in the canonical pseudometric without nondegeneracy assumptions. Given this uniqueness, both bounds follow from a bound with constant $2$ on the mean square of the largest increment of an independent copy of $G$ from an exact maximizer to a point of $A_ε$. The proof rests on an identity for the mean squared support function of the $ε$-subdifferentials of a smooth convex function at a standard Gaussian vector, obtained from two Gaussian integrations by parts.

title: On subgroup regular sets in generalized Cayley graphs
abstract: A subset $D$ of the vertex set of a graph is called an $(a,b)$-regular set if each vertex in $D$ has exactly $a$ neighbors in $D$, and each vertex outside $D$ has exactly $b$ neighbors in $D$. A proper subgroup $H$ of $G$ is called an $(a,b)$-regular set of $(G,α)$ if it is an $(a,b)$-regular set of $GC(G,S,α)$ for some generalized Cayley subset $S$ of $G$ induced by the involutory automorphism $α$. This paper investigates subgroup $(0,b)$-regular sets in generalized Cayley graphs. We first obtain some necessary and sufficient conditions for a proper subgroup of a group $G$ to be a $(0,b)$-regular set of a generalized Cayley graph. In particular, we show that a proper normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ is a $(0,b)$-regular set of $(G,α)$ if and only if $H$ is a perfect code of $(G,α)$ for some odd integer $b,$ which generalizes the result in [F.S. Seiedali, Z. Akhlaghi, B. Khosravi. Generalized Cayley graphs and perfect code. Discrete Math. 2026]. Furthermore, for connected generalized Cayley graphs with $α$-normal generalized Cayley subsets, we characterize subgroup $(0,b)$-regular sets via equitable partitions.

title: Evolution of Internal Waves on Surfaces of Revolution with Flat Ends
abstract: We generalize the 2D linear internal wave equation to non-compact surfaces of revolution with flat ends. We show that the leading profile of this equation with oscillatory forcing is the unique incoming solution to the corresponding stationary equation. This is done by proving a limiting absorption principle via propagation of semiclassical defect measure.

title: Rational contractions in quasi-Banach spaces: convergence, multiplicity of fixed points and applications
abstract: We study self-maps $f$ of a complete $b$-metric space $(U,d)$ (constant $b\ge1$) satisfying the rational contractive condition \[ d(fu,fv)\le\frac{d(u,fv)+d(v,fu)+κ}{b\,[d(u,fu)+d(v,fv)]+1}\,d(u,v)\qquad(u,v\in U), \] with $κ\in[0,1)$. We first observe that the two-parameter family of conditions studied in our earlier work reduces, after a rescaling of the $b$-metric, to this one-parameter form. We then prove: (A) every Picard sequence converges to a fixed point, with an explicit a~priori estimate whose geometric ratio depends only on $b$, $κ$ and $d(u_0,fu_0)$, an a~posteriori estimate, and asymptotic rate at most $κ$; (B) a structure theorem: such maps are automatically continuous, every fixed point attracts the whole ball of radius $(1-κ)/2$, distinct fixed points are at distance at least $(1-κ)/2$ (sharp), basins of attraction are clopen, and the number of fixed points does not exceed the number of connected components of $U$; in particular the fixed point is unique on connected spaces; (C) Ulam--Hyers stability of the fixed-point problem. The class of such maps is not invariant under passing from a quasi-norm to the equivalent $p$-norm metric, so the quasi-Banach results are not formal consequences of the metric ones. A gluing principle shows that the multiplicity permitted by (B) occurs. As applications we obtain existence, exact multiplicity and error estimates for infinite nonlinear systems with relay-type forcing in $\ell^p$, $0<p<1$, and for nonlinear perturbations of Volterra-type equations $f=\pm a+T_gf+ψ(f(z_0))k$ in the Hardy space $H^p$, $0<p<1$, where $T_gf(z)=\int_0^z f(ζ)g'(ζ)\,dζ$ and $g\in\BMOA$.

title: Enumerating Pyranim Isomorphisms
abstract: We study a Nim-adjacent poset game, where chips are arranged in a pyramid and two players take turns removing chips that do not currently support chips to the upper-left and upper-right; upon removing this chip, all supported chips above are also removed. Play continues until the final chip is removed. We use a bijection between the game states, Dyck paths, and unit interval graphs to count the number of possible game states up to isomorphism.

title: Two-Stage Secret Sharing
abstract: We give an information-theoretic formulation of two-stage secret sharing for situations in which secret information becomes available progressively. In the proposed model, shares for an initial part of the secret are distributed before the remaining part becomes available, and additional shares are distributed to new participants after the remaining part becomes available, without updating the shares already distributed and without using any additional information other than shares. To characterize this setting, we propose the notion of a two-stage access structure and provide its characterization. We further quantify the amount of information about the first-stage secret that the dealer must retain between the two distribution stages, derive a universal lower bound, and present a construction that achieves this bound for every two-stage access structure. We also position advance sharing as a special case of the proposed model and give its characterization and a related construction in classical information-theoretic secret sharing.

title: A global rigidity criterion for Coxeter $3$-polytopes
abstract: We give a combinatorial condition ensuring global projective rigidity of simple hyperbolic Coxeter $3$-polytopes. As an application, we prove that every right-angled Löbell polytope is globally rigid.

title: $(r,s)$-Designs in the Nonbinary Johnson Scheme: Constructions and Linear Codes
abstract: Using factorizations of complete graphs, we determine the existence conditions for $(2,1)$-designs in the nonbinary Johnson scheme where each $3$-element subset appears exactly once as a support. Furthermore, by utilizing large sets of Steiner triple systems, we construct designs with index $1$ that cannot be obtained from the known construction combining block designs and orthogonal arrays. For linear codes, we express multiplicative character sums over specified nonzero coordinates as sums over the codewords of the dual code. Using this identity along with the rank of a matrix formed by Krawtchouk polynomials, we provide a sufficient condition for the set of all codewords of a given weight to form an $(r,s)$-design. In this matrix, we can utilize not only the rows corresponding to weights absent from the code, but also the rows corresponding to weights for which the set of codewords already forms a design. Moreover, let $q>2$ be a prime power, and let $0 \neq C \subsetneq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a linear code with exactly two nonzero weights. For $t \geq 2$, the set of all codewords of weight $w \geq t$ forms a non-empty $(t,t)$-design if and only if the dual minimum distance is at least $t+2$. Consequently, this provides a negative answer to the Wu--Zhou problem concerning two-weight codes with a dual minimum distance of $3$.

title: Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operator and Separation of Variables for BC-type open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ spin chain
abstract:
We construct two-parameter Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators for the transfer matrices of noncompact open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ BC-type spin chains with general boundary interactions, treating both one-boundary and two-boundary models. The $\mathbb{Q}$-operators are defined as traces of general monodromy matrices over infinite-dimensional auxiliary spaces carrying principal series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$.
  At specific values of parameters the two-parameter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators degenerate into simpler one-parameter Baxter operators. We prove that the general transfer matrices factorize into products of these one-parameter $Q$-operators. We provide both an algebraic derivation based on local operator identities and a diagrammatic proof using Feynman diagrammatic techniques.
  Finally, we apply the quantum Separation of Variables (SoV) method to the spectral problem of the one-boundary transfer matrix. We derive the system of separated difference equations for the transfer matrix eigenfunctions and show that, under the assumption of kernel factorization, it reduces to a one-dimensional difference equation coinciding precisely with the Baxter equation for eigenvalues of appropriately normalized one-parameter Baxter $Q$-operator.

title: Addendum to "Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds"
abstract: In the paper ``Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds'', the same authors introduced a geometric object called Pontryagin-type $C^0$-Finsler structures, which includes Finsler structures on a smooth manifold $M$. Such a structure is defined locally by a control system of $C^1$ unit vector fields on an open subset $U$ of $M$, such that Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) is applicable. As a result of PMP, we obtain the extended geodesic field $\mathcal{E}$, which is a multivalued vector field on the slit cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}U\backslash 0 = \{(x,α): x\in U, α\in T^{\ast}_x U\}$, such that every minimizing path $x(t)$ on $(U,F)$ is an extremal (projection of a Pontryagin extremal $(x(t),α(t))$). Some time after its introduction, its use and external comments, it is useful to provide remarks that clarify the applicability and limitations of this theory. In addition, we point out two errors contained in that work which, although discernible from the context, we believe should be pointed out. Finally, we prove some cases where the property that a minimizing path is the projection of a Pontryagin extremal can be extended beyond a coordinate system, sometimes to $M$. We also work on the problem of determining when $\mathcal{E}$ does not depend on the control system chosen to represent $F$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies these two properties globally for left-invariant $C^0$-Finsler structures on Lie groups, and for $C^1$-Finsler structures (without the condition of strong convexity).

title: Convergence rates for truncated and discretised signature expansions
abstract: Linear expansions in Brownian Stratonovich signatures, which originate in stochastic Taylor expansions, are increasingly used to represent and model processes with memory. Their numerical use requires truncating the signature at a level $M$ and discretising the driving path along $N$ steps. Under a simple growth condition on the coefficients of the linear expansion, we establish strong and weak convergence rates for both approximations, uniformly in time. The strong truncation error decays like $(B^M/(M!)^\varepsilon)^a$ for some constant $B$, uniformly in $N$, where $\varepsilon$ measures the growth of the coefficients and $a$ the regularity of the test function; the weak error does not improve on it. The discretisation error is of order $N^{-a/2}$ in $L^p$, and $N^{-1}$ weakly for polynomial test functions, uniformly in $M$. All these rates are sharp for polynomial test functions, and $M$, $N$ can be chosen independently. We extend the estimates to errors in probability, on distribution functions and on risk measures, and illustrate them on stochastic delay equations, Volterra processes and option pricing in signature volatility models.

title: Minimal Finite Non-Commutative Centrally Essential Rings
abstract: A ring $R$ with nonzero unity is called centrally essential if for every nonzero element $a$ of $R$ there exist nonzero central elements $x$ and $y$ such that $ax = y$. In this paper we obtain a complete classification, up to isomorphism, of non-commutative centrally essential rings of minimal order $64$.

title: Rigid Theories
abstract: A structure is rigid if it admits no non-trivial automorphisms. We investigate an analogous invariance property for first-order theories, with relative interpretations playing the role of morphisms. A theory $T$ is called rigid if and only if every self-interpretation of $T$ is definably isomorphic to the identity interpretation. Extending work of Pakhomov and Zapryagaev (2020) on Presburger Arithmetic, we establish rigidity for Successor Arithmetic and Skolem Arithmetic (with respect to one-dimensional interpretations), True Arithmetic, and the theories of fields $\mathrm{RCF}$ and $\mathrm{ACF}$. By contrast, $\mathrm{PA}$ and $\mathrm{ZF}$ admit infinitely many self-interpretations, though both remain rigid with respect to (co-)retractions. Our main negative result is that $\mathrm{ZFC}$ has no consistent rigid extension in its own language. We compare rigidity with categoricity, model rigidity, completeness, and solidity, showing it to be independent of the first three, and indicate the relevance of rigidity to questions about semantic determinacy.

title: Prime values of linear forms and a quadratic form: one proof and two arithmetic applications
abstract:
Let $L_1,\dots,L_k\in \mathbb Z[x,y]$ be a system of linear polynomials whose homogeneous parts are pairwise linearly independent. Let $K=\mathbb Q(α)$ be an imaginary quadratic field. Utilizing the higher order Fourier analysis machinery of Green and Sawhney in their breakthrough work on the Gaussian prime conjecture, we show that if there are no local obstructions, then there are infinitely many $(x,y)\in \mathbb Z$ such that $L_1(x,y),\dots,L_k(x,y),$ and $N_{K/\mathbb Q}(x+yα)$ are simultaneously prime. We further establish an asymptotic formula which matches the prediction by the multivariate Bateman-Horn conjecture.
  We present two arithmetic applications of this prime counting result. First, we show that the Brauer--Manin obstruction is the only obstruction to weak approximation on a new family of varieties, including diagonal conic bundles all of whose degenerate fibres are defined over $\mathbb Q$ except one fibre that may be defined over an imaginary quadratic field. Second, we construct elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$ with infinitely many quadratic twists of rank exactly two.

title: Fully Explicit Stabilized Runge--Kutta Methods for Allen--Cahn and Cahn--Hilliard Dynamics
abstract: Stiff phase-field dynamics are typically solved by semi-implicit or fully implicit time discretizations, since the interfacial scales in the Allen--Cahn and Cahn--Hilliard equations impose severe step-size restrictions on standard explicit methods. In this paper, we investigate a different strategy based on stabilized Runge--Kutta solvers, in particular the Runge--Kutta--Legendre (RKL) and Runge--Kutta--Gegenbauer (RKG) families. These schemes possess enlarged stability regions and therefore provide a natural explicit framework for diffusion-dominated gradient flows without requiring implicit solves. For the Allen--Cahn equation, combined with Strang splitting, we establish a maximum principle in 1-dimensional case, and prove energy dissipation in all the dimensions. For the modified energy dissipation analysis, we further introduce two new first-order stabilized schemes of RKL and RKG type and derive a novel eigenvalue estimate for the second-order RKG method. We also conduct extensive numerical experiments with both constant and adaptive time stepping, on regular domains as well as on an L-shaped irregular domain. The numerical results show that stabilized explicit Runge--Kutta methods provide an effective and flexible approach for the numerical simulation of Allen--Cahn and Cahn--Hilliard dynamics while preserving key structural properties. The Python implementation is available at https://github.com/ZT220501/SRK-for-Gradient-Flows.

title: A One-Sided Chord Trim of Wetzel's Sector Covers Unit Arcs
abstract: Wetzel conjectured, and Panraksa and Wichiramala proved, that the circular sector of radius one and angle $30^\circ$ contains a congruent copy, reflections allowed, of every arc of length one. We show that half of its arc is not needed: replacing the arc between the angles $15^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ by its chord gives a convex cover of area $π/24+(\sqrt6-\sqrt2)/8=0.2603092\ldots$. As in the proof for the sector, we place an arc in two supporting wedges. A sum of support, cap and radial inequalities, with vector coefficients summing to zero, shows that an arc with no copy in the trimmed sector is longer than one. One two-parameter family of configurations is checked by rational interval arithmetic; programs and data are supplied. No chord that starts below $3.6^\circ$ gives a cover. We also reduce the inclusion-minimality of the trimmed sector to two families of cuts.

title: Triply conservative schemes for degenerate convection-dispersion equations
abstract: It is well known that for numerically solving hyperbolic conservation laws, even a convergent numerical scheme still may not always converge to a weak solution. The remedy is the famous Lax-Wendroff theorem. In a recent work on degenerate convection-diffusion equations, an analogous phenomenon was identified and doubly conservative schemes were introduced. In this paper, we address the same issue for solving the following nonlinear degenerate dispersive or convection-dispersion equations: \begin{equation*} u_t+f(u)_x+A(u)_{xxx}=0. \end{equation*} The resulting equation is regarded as degenerate if $A'(u)$ is allowed to vanish. An important example is the Rosenau-Hyman $K(m,n)$ equation. In contrast to classical KdV solitons possessing exponentially decaying tails, $K(m,n)$ equations can admit compactly supported solitary waves, known as compactons, whose regularity can deteriorate at the boundary of their support. We first give an example in which both a classical conservative and doubly conservative scheme converges to a limit that fails to satisfy the ultra-weak formulation. To address this issue, we introduce the notion of a triply conservative (TriC) scheme and prove a Lax-Wendroff type theorem for consistent TriC schemes. Under suitable assumptions, a convergent sequence generated by a consistent TriC scheme will converge to an ultra-weak solution. Several existing high-order schemes are shown to have a TriC structure. We further introduce a new high-order TriC finite volume scheme based on a connection between triple cell averages and quadratic B-splines. The theory and the scheme are also suited for two-dimensional anisotropic problems and non-uniform meshes. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions confirm the high-order accuracy on smooth solutions and illustrate the behavior of the schemes for compactons and traveling fronts.

title: Your PID Is Already a Neural Network: Learning Its Gains with Only Three Weights and No Teacher
abstract: A discrete PID controller is exactly a recurrent neural network, a classical state-space fact: a fixed linear memory of the running integral and the last error, read out by three trainable weights that map one-to-one to the PID gains. Networks with bounded hidden states, such as LSTMs of any width, only approximate it. Trained only on a one-step physical cost (the expected cost of one transition from a fixed state distribution), with no demonstrations, teacher controller, or known gains, the network solves a strongly convex least-squares problem, so gradient descent converges from any initialization to the unique one-step optimal PID gains; the limit network is that PID, with the same action on every error sequence. Partitioned regression then shows what extra capacity buys. Orthogonal residual features keep these gains and improve on the PID if and only if they correlate with the part of the optimal action outside the PID span. On a nonlinear second-order example the gap is 5.88% of the optimal PID cost, and 4.00% against PID with a bias; no controller can improve on PID by more on this objective. A residual started at a tuned PID begins exactly at that PID; at the one-step optimal PID, a fixed-feature residual's first gradient step lowers the cost if and only if its features can improve on the PID. Experiments confirm the realization, recovery, and gap results to numerical precision. On held-out plants of three families, under a protocol frozen before the test data existed, a residual warm-started at a heavily tuned PID and trained with it lowers the long-horizon cost by 3.5%, 3.5%, and 1.9%, with family-wise 95% bounds excluding zero, also under distribution shift; a post hoc comparison with the PID tuned alone suggests that most of it comes from the recurrent part in two families. The primary endpoint, a gain of at least 5% from a generic PID start, is not met in any family.

title: The Wasserstein cost of the Girsanov Theorem
abstract:
This is an expository note on the asymptotics of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of infinite-dimensional random paths and their common distribution. We present the classical proof for these asymptotics in the case of the Wiener measure, unifying quantization arguments from Dereich and coauthors or Boissard and Le Gouic, and we adapt it for Itô diffusions sampled through the Girsanov theorem.
