abstract: Dynamic time-to-collision (TTC) is the first contact time of a prediction flow and defines a feedback map implicitly. We study its capped value function $\VV$ for Carathéodory dynamics with bounded, measurable forcing. A self-contained argument establishes local Lipschitz continuity on the transversal collision domain. A derivative-free stopped-step Bellman equation then characterizes $\VV$ uniquely: it advances the prediction for a fixed duration or until contact and adds the elapsed time. A two-sided error bound uses only the candidate's residual along complete stopped trajectories and its error at their endpoints. Exact continuum iteration recovers $\VV$ after finitely many sweeps, including one additional sweep for initializations that violate the boundary condition. We also characterize an optional-duration infimum operator: its fixed points are the dynamic-programming subsolutions, so its residual alone does not identify $\VV$. Finally, on compact subsets of the transversal domain, an optimization-free ReLU construction has explicit size, controlled local residual, and robustness to errors in its nodal TTC values. The optimal velocity model provides the running application.

title: Exact Turán densities of even zycles
abstract: We determine the exact Turán density of the $3$-uniform zycle $Z_\ell$ for every even integer $\ell\ge 4$ with $3\nmid\ell$, showing that $π(Z_\ell)=5/9$. More generally, we prove that $π(Z_\ell)\le 5/9$ for all even $\ell\ge 4$. In the range of equality, we also establish a stability theorem, showing that every almost extremal $Z_\ell$-free $3$-graph is close in edit distance to the classical Turán construction.

title: Information Spectrum Methods for Multiple-Access Channels --Part II : $\varepsilon$-Capacity Regions in the Mixed Finite-Alphabet Case
abstract: In a nonergodic channel such as a slowly fading link, the channel law is drawn once and held fixed for the whole codeword, and the relevant performance measure is the $\varepsilon$-capacity. We study the $\varepsilon$-capacity regions of two-user mixed multiple-access channels (MACs) with finite alphabets, additive cost constraints and an arbitrary mixing measure. The direct parts are derived from a single information spectrum formula; the converse parts use, in addition, Fano's inequality and Ahlswede's strong converse applied to each component. Without knowledge of the realized component, we prove a single-letter inner bound for every $0\le\varepsilon<1$, in which one input serves all components; for $\varepsilon=0$ it is tight, and the capacity region is given by the essential infima of the component mutual informations. We prove a single-letter outer bound, the outage region, in which each component may use its own input; it holds with or without channel state information (CSI) at either terminal, and it is the $\varepsilon$-capacity region when the encoders know the component and the parameter space is countable. Both bounds coincide, in all four CSI scenarios, for well-ordered mixed MACs, which include degradedly ordered families and mixtures with a common optimal input, such as mixed additive MACs. Without CSI the outer bound can be strictly loose, and the no-CSI $\varepsilon$-capacity region for $0<\varepsilon<1$ remains open in general. Finally, we extend Ahlswede's strong converse to $K$ users with cost constraints and show that most of these results extend to $K$-user mixed MACs.

title: Bloch groups of local rings with residue field $\mathbb{F}_2$
abstract: We give a generic presentation of the pre-Bloch group of a local ring with residue field $\mathbb{F}_{2}$. We apply this to the calculation of pre-Bloch groups and Bloch groups of some local rings.

title: Quantitative flocking of Cucker-Smale flocks under time-delay and noise
abstract: We study the asymptotic flocking dynamics of the delayed stochastic Cucker-Smale (in short, DSCS) model driven by agent-wise independent, component-wise multiplicative Brownian noise. The simultaneous interplay of stochastic perturbations and time delay yields fundamental challenges to asymptotic stochastic flocking analysis, as the communication weight may lose a uniform positive lower bound, while the velocity moment is no longer monotone. To overcome these difficulties, we present a sufficient framework and an analytical tool combining the method of time-varying effective region and Lyapunov functional approach with time-delay corrections. This approach avoids any reliance on uniformly positive communication weights or monotone velocity moments. The proposed approach recovers sufficiently strong effective velocity alignment despite stochastic fluctuations and delay effects. As a consequence, we establish the mean-square stochastic flocking with an explicit polynomial convergence rate. The admissible decay exponent is determined by the communication kernel exponent and the orders of the spatial and velocity history moments. These results establish a quantitative theory for long-time stochastic flocking under simultaneous delay and multiplicative noise, and we provide a positive answer to an open problem raised by~[R. Erban, J. Haskovec, Y. Sun, SIAM J. Appl. Math., 76, 1535--1557 (2016)]. We also develop robust analytical tools applicable to delayed stochastic collective dynamics with degenerate communications.

title: The dynamical Seppäläinen-Johansson model and the Brownian web landscape
abstract: The dynamical Seppäläinen-Johansson first passage percolation defines a random directed metric on $\mathbb Z^2$ where the environment is updated according to a Poisson process. We show that its finite dimensional distributions converge after $0:1:2$ scaling to those of the Brownian web landscape defined on the finite dimensional marginals of the dynamical Brownian web. We prove non-uniqueness of geodesics in the Brownian web landscape and we relate it to exact formulas on one-sided reflected Brownian motions. We prove a locally uniform law of large numbers and uniform deviation bounds, and identify Poisson increment-stationary laws for the associated height evolution.

title: Scaling limits of Chebyshev polynomials at a hard edge
abstract: Let $\mathsf{E}\subset\mathbb{R}$ be compact. We derive local scaling limits of the Chebyshev polynomials associated to $\mathsf{E}$ at a gap edge. We describe the scaling limits by a one parameter family of functions explicitly given by elliptic integrals. We show that for the union of two generic intervals all functions in this family are in fact attained as limits. As a consequence, we describe the local scaling behavior of the zeros of the Chebyshev polynomials at the gap edge.

title: Central limit theorems for Frobenius, Hecke and Kloosterman angles
abstract: The Frobenius angles of non-CM elliptic curves and the Hecke angles of non-CM newforms are equidistributed with respect to the Sato--Tate measure, while for Kloosterman angles, this is known on average over natural families. We study the fluctuations around these laws in large families, for smooth test functions. We prove an unconditional central limit theorem for Frobenius angles of elliptic curves for a much larger class of test functions than previously considered; earlier results assumed the Riemann hypothesis for $L$-functions of Hecke eigenforms of full level. This result follows from a general framework, developed here, which yields Gaussian moments for statistics of sequences in $[0,1]$ varying over families. In this framework, independence is replaced by two quantitative conditions: approximate independence at distinct indices, and convergence of the family averages to the Weyl limits at a suitable rate. As further applications, we extend central limit theorems for Kloosterman angles and for Hecke angles of newforms to larger classes of test functions, the latter with the weight and the level varying simultaneously. We also treat the dilated angles $αθ$ for integers $α\geq2$, whose limiting distribution is uniform. Finally, we discuss sharp statistics, obtaining a central limit theorem for Hecke angles and explaining the obstruction for the other two families.

title: On the Adams spectral sequence of $eo_2(C_4)$
abstract: We calculate the mod $2$-homology of the fixed points of the $C_4$-equivariant Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel theory $BP^{((C_4))}\langle 1\rangle$, as an $\mathcal{A}_*$-comodule algebra. $2$-locally these fixed points are $tmf_0(5)$ by a theorem of Quinn. We deduce that $tmf_0(5)$ is an indecomposable $tmf$-module that is an extension of two $tmf$-modules of the form $tmf\otimes K$ for a finite spectrum $K$. The $K(2)$-localization of $tmf_0(5)$ is $32$-periodic, and we compute the Adams spectral sequence of $tmf_0(5)$ through the $32$-stem.

title: Affine Vertex Operator Algebras and Correlation Functions on Elliptic Curves
abstract: Let $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra attached to a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra at arbitrary level, and let $M=\bigoplus_{N=0}^{\infty}M_N$ be a $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ -module. We give an explicit formula for every genus-one trace of affine currents as a finite sum over cycle partitions. We then show the convergence of all fixed zero-mode trace series, hence absolute locally uniform convergence of the current traces and their meromorphic continuation on the elliptic configuration space. The same conclusion is obtained for arbitrary affine-state insertions. Finally, we compute the cases of at most four currents and the nodal limit $q\to 0$, in which the type-1 and type-2 elliptic cycle coefficients degenerate to rational genus-zero cycle coefficients and the module trace reduces to the ground-state space.

title: Polarity of the First Dirichlet Liouville Spectral Gap
abstract: We prove zero $1$-capacity of first-gap collisions for the minimal Liouville spectral Green-response form and its canonical extension. The minimal-form diffusion avoids collisions for every initial law absolutely continuous with respect to the spectral law.

title: A Lagrangian Floer Theory over the Integers and Finite Fields
abstract: Let $L_0$ and $L_1$ be a pair of transversely intersecting closed Lagrangians in a closed symplectic manifold, equipped with a relative-spin structure with respect to a common background class. We construct a curved, filtered, $A_\infty$-bimodule structure over the integral Fukaya algebras of $L_0$ and $L_1$ as given in \cite{rabah2024fukaya}, \cite{rabah2025fukaya}; on the free module generated by the intersection points of $L_0$ and $L_1$, over the integral Novikov ring. When both Lagrangians are unobstructed, we define a Lagrangian Floer homology of the pair over the integral Novikov ring, extending the work of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono in \cite{fukaya2013lagrangian} to general closed symplectic manifolds. We use this framework to bound the number of intersection points between a Lagrangian and its transverse Hamiltonian image. Such bound incorporates the torsion subgroup in the integral homology of the Lagrangian. In return, it improves the characteristic-zero Betti number bound.

title: Total edge irregularity strength of cubic graphs
abstract: We show that every finite simple cubic graph on $n$ vertices has total edge irregularity strength $n/2+1$, confirming the Ivančo-Jendrol' conjecture for cubic graphs. The key step is to algorithmically construct a $\{1,n/2+1\}$-vertex labeling such that half of the vertices are labeled $1$ and the average degree of the subgraph induced by them is close enough to two. We extend such a labeling to a total edge irregular $(n/2+1)$-labeling, possibly after a local adjustment to a single vertex.

title: Strong Completeness of Provability Logic for Languages of size at most continuum
abstract: We investigate the strong completeness of $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ for an infinite set of propositional variables $\mathbb P$ over ordinal spaces equipped with the interval topology $\mathcal{I}_1$. For every infinite cardinal $κ$, we consider the set \[ Γ_κ= \{\Diamond p_ξ:ξ<κ\} \cup \{\Box(p_ξ\to\Diamond p_η):ξ<η<κ\}, \] and prove that $Γ_κ$ has a model on an ordinal space with $\mathcal{I}_1$ if and only if $κ\nrightarrow_{\mathrm{ipath}}(ω)^2_{ω,<ω}$. We also prove that if $|\mathbb P|<\mathfrak p$, then $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ is strongly complete with respect to $(ω^ω+1,\mathcal I_1)$. Finally, we establish the strong completeness of $\mathrm{GL}(\mathbb P)$ with respect to the same space whenever $|\mathbb P|=\aleph_1$.

title: Hilbert's 17th problem for symmetric functions: undecidability and a counterexample
abstract: We study inequalities between symmetric functions that hold in every number of variables. First, we prove that it is undecidable whether a symmetric function with rational coefficients is nonnegative in all dimensions, answering a question posed by Acevedo, Blekherman, Debus and Riener. As a consequence, the validity of dimension-free moment criteria for entanglement in quantum information is undecidable. Second, we present a homogeneous symmetric function of degree 8 which is positive definite in every dimension but admits no sum of squares multiplier that is uniform in the number of variables. Consequently, Artin's solution of Hilbert's 17th problem and the Krivine-Stengle Positivstellensatz have no any-dimensional analog and any-dimensional Positivstellensätze asked for by Levin and Chandrasekaran cannot hold in general.

title: Free Gödel algebras over Gödel hoops
abstract: We give an explicit description of the left adjoint $F$ of the forgetful functor $U\colon\mathsf{GAlg}\to\mathsf{GHoops}$ from Gödel algebras to Gödel hoops. If $H$ is a Gödel hoop with a least element $m$, then $F(H)$ is the direct product of the Gödel algebra obtained by adjoining a new bottom element to $H$ and of $H$ itself, regarded as a Gödel algebra with bottom element $m$. For an arbitrary Gödel hoop $H$, we glue these products along the principal filters of $H$, and we describe the operations of $F(H)$, the action of $F$ on homomorphisms and the unit of the adjunction. As an application, we show that the unit of the adjunction $F\dashv U$ is not cartesian, and that the same holds for BL-algebras and basic hoops. Moreover, the semi-abelian categories of Gödel hoops and of basic hoops are not equivalent to the slice categories of Gödel algebras and of BL-algebras over their initial object. Thus, in contrast with the cases of Wajsberg hoops and of product hoops, the free-forgetful adjunctions between Gödel algebras and Gödel hoops, and between BL-algebras and basic hoops, do not give rise to ideally exact contexts.

title: Exact Fourier Coupling Relations for the Method of Auxiliary Sources on Elliptic Cylinders
abstract: The Method of Auxiliary Sources has been extensively studied in the case of cylindrical geometries. In this article, the authors provide analysis elements for the elliptical geometry case. Based on a Mathieu functions expansion, the impedance matrix is projected into a reduced diagonal matrix. At the same time, the matrix is studied in the Fourier domain. A checkerboard structure is found and a relation between the different elements of the matrix is proven. Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical results. We additionally identify an exact finite-grid parity rule, an aliasing identity connecting the discrete and continuous Fourier representations, and controlled near-circular Fourier-band localization. These results are mostly independent of a small-$q$ truncation of radial Mathieu functions.

title: Information Spectrum Methods for MUltiple-Access Channels--Part III : The Strong Converse in the $K$-User Gaussian Case
abstract: This paper, Part III of a series, treats $K$-user multiple-access channels (MACs). Its starting point is a pair of fundamental lemmas, a random-coding lemma of Feinstein type and a converse lemma of Verdú--Han type, which are the $K$-user extensions of the two lemmas underlying Han's information spectrum approach to the general two-user MAC. From them we derive the capacity region of the general $K$-user MAC with cost constraint and show that it contains the polymatroid capacity region of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC. We then prove, by an elementary information spectrum calculation that adapts a diffuse--exceptional subspace decomposition used in recent second-order converses for the Gaussian MAC, that for every subset $\cS$ of users and every independent input satisfying the power constraints, the conditional information spectral-sup rate of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC does not exceed $\frac12\log(1+P_\cS/N)$, where $P_\cS$ is the total power of the users in $\cS$, with a probability bound that does not depend on the input. Consequently, the strong converse for the $K$-user Gaussian MAC, in the sense that the error probability tends to one for every rate tuple outside the capacity region, follows directly from the converse lemma, without the wringing technique and without hypothesis-testing meta-converses. This strong converse was first established by Fong and Tan, whose per-blocklength bounds yield it, through wringing and quantization. It is the key ingredient in the converse parts of the coding theorems for mixed Gaussian MACs in Part I, where the $\varepsilon$-strong converse would not suffice.

title: On compact homogeneous Locally conformal symplectic manifolds
abstract:
A locally conformally symplectic (LCS) structure on a manifold $M$ is a pair $(η,ω)$ consisting of a closed $1$-form $η$ called Lee form and a nondegenerate $2$-form $ω$ satisfying
  \[
  dω=η\wedgeω.
  \]
  We classify compact connected homogeneous LCS manifolds with nonzero Lee form. To this end, we construct three explicit families of pairs $(G,K)$, where $G$ is a connected simply connected Lie group and $K$ is a closed subgroup such that $G/K$ is compact, the $G$-action is almost effective, and $G/K$ admits a $G$-invariant LCS structure. We show that every compact connected homogeneous LCS manifold with nonzero Lee form arises from one of these families.
  Moreover, each such manifold is LCS-isomorphic to a product $(S/H_d)\times S^1$, where $S$ is a compact connected simply connected semisimple Lie group and $S/H_d$ carries an $S$-invariant contact form $α$. Under this identification, the LCS structure is given by
  \[
  η=π_2^*ξ,\qquad
  ω=d(π_1^*α)+π_1^*α\wedgeη,
  \]
  where $π_1$ and $π_2$ are the projections onto the two factors and $ξ$ is a nowhere-vanishing $1$-form on $S^1$. This description also yields topological consequences for compact homogeneous LCS manifolds. In particular,
  none of these compact
  homogeneous LCS manifolds admits a symplectic
  structure, even without any invariance assumption.
  As a consequence, we show that in dimension four the underlying manifolds are precisely $L(d,1)\times S^1$, where $L(d,1)$ is a three-dimensional lens space. In dimension eight, we obtain families arising from seven-dimensional lens spaces and Aloff--Wallach spaces, including infinitely many distinct topological types.

title: Optimal control for an anisotropic Stokes-Nernst-Planck-Poisson system
abstract: We study an optimal control problem aimed at enhancing mixing in anisotropic electrolytes described by an instationary Stokes-Nernst-Planck-Poisson system in three space dimensions, where the anisotropy is encoded by a given director field in the diffusion and permittivity matrices. The control is the external electric potential entering through the Robin boundary condition of the Poisson equation. The cost functional combines tracking-type terms for the charge concentrations and an $L^2$-regularization of the control with a negative vorticity term that favors rotational flow. Assuming that the diffusion and permittivity matrices coincide, we first prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions with nonnegative, essentially bounded concentrations, together with Lipschitz continuous dependence on the control. Since, through the negative vorticity term, the cost functional is no longer weakly lower semicontinuous, existence of an optimal control relies on strong convergence of the velocity gradients. Finally, we prove Fréchet differentiability of the control-to-state operator, introduce the adjoint system, and derive first-order necessary optimality conditions in the form of a variational inequality.

title: Kobayashi distance to submanifolds in a Riemannian manifold
abstract: We prove that totally geodesic hypersurfaces are at infinite Kobayashi distance in a Kobayashi hyperbolic Riemannian manifold. To do this, we prove a Schwarz lemma on minimal maps with a uniform control on their Laplacians. Finally we give a full characterisation of submanifolds at infinite distance on spaces of constant sectional curvature in dimension at least 4.

title: The Evertse-Ferretti interval result for a set of weights, and the exponent $1/2$ in three complexity bounds
abstract: The interval result of Evertse and Ferretti (2013) concerns a tuple $L$ of linear forms and one tuple $c$ of weights. It says that the parameters $Q$ for which the twisted height $H_{L,c,Q}$ has a small value outside an exceptional subspace $T(L,c)$ lie in $O(δ^{-2}\logδ^{-1})$ intervals $[Q_i,Q_i^ω)$. We prove this for a whole set $\mathcal{C}$ of weights with the same forms. At most $J$ subspaces $T(L,c)$ occur, where $J$ depends only on the dimension and on the number of places, and one family of $O(δ^{-2}\logδ^{-1})$ intervals serves every $c\in\mathcal{C}$ at once. Neither count depends on $\mathcal{C}$. In applications of Bugeaud-Evertse type the solutions are sorted into about $\varepsilon^{-1}$ classes with the same forms and different weights, and one application now serves all classes. We deduce three complexity bounds. For a real algebraic irrational number $ξ$, the number $p(n,ξ,b)$ of blocks of length $n$ in its base-$b$ expansion satisfies $\limsup p(n,ξ,b)/(n(\log n)^η)=\infty$ for every $η<1/2$; Bugeaud and Evertse proved this for $η<1/11$. The same holds for the continued fraction expansion of an algebraic number of degree at least three, and for the steering word of $(3/2)^n$. We explain why $1/2$ is the limit of the method. All results are machine-verified in Lean~4.

title: Counting Triangulated 3-Spheres, Nuclei, and Polyhedra
abstract: We exploit two-dimensional dual polyhedra to study triangulated $3$-spheres and nuclei. First, we show that the long-standing open problem of whether the number of triangulated $3$-spheres is exponentially bounded is equivalent to the corresponding problem for one-vertex generalized triangulations, and hence also for special spines of the $3$-ball. This also establishes an equivalent counting problem for nuclei. Second, we investigate properties of nuclei, including their dual polyhedra. We also prove that every nontrivial nucleus contains a tetrahedron with six interior edges, identify the unique vertex-minimal nontrivial nucleus with $11$ vertices and $35$ tetrahedra, and construct nuclei whose dual graphs have genus growing linearly with the number of tetrahedra.

title: Physics-constrained differentiable causal discovery of constitutive mechanisms through boundary value problems
abstract: Data-driven constitutive model discovery is recast as causal discovery of mechanism parent sets using time-unrolled structural causal models. Hard-coding balance laws and constitutive skeletons, candidate graphs score environment--mechanism and state--state edges via weak-form equilibrium gaps evaluated from full-field displacements, avoiding the need to measure stresses or internal variables. An adaptive lasso and a NOTEARS-type constraint ensure graph acyclicity and an explicit evaluation order, treating climate-chamber protocols as interventions. Automatic differentiation yields the score's Gauss--Newton matrix as a local identifiability certificate, driving greedy D-optimal test design. In a synthetic study on a hygro-thermo-viscoelastic damaging plate (8 true edges among 13 candidates), interventional data recover the exact true graph in 7 of 10 runs (0.01px displacement noise) with zero attribution error. Conversely, observational data with a temperature--moisture correlation of $-0.998$ fail entirely because confounded scores are 250--380 times flatter. Observationally discovered models reproduce training climates (3.6% error) but mispredict hot and humid climates by up to 41.5% (16.9% average), whereas interventionally discovered models stay within 3.2%. A correlation sweep shows the certificate successfully predicts attribution errors, though weak-form score noise bias remains a primary limitation. Computed without knowledge of the truth, the D-optimal design selects test sets ranked second or third out of 126 candidates.

title: Gaussian processes with random pointwise regularity
abstract: Using wavelet series, we construct Gaussian stochastic processes whose pointwise Hölder exponent is random along a typical sample path, although at every fixed point the exponent is deterministic almost surely. We first give a local non-sparsity condition under which the Hölder exponent almost surely is a deterministic function. In the opposite direction, a lacunary construction shows that the exceptional set on which the exponent is modified can have full Hausdorff dimension. For this model we determine the marginal multifractal spectra and the bivariate spectrum of the deterministic series and its Gaussian randomization.

title: A sharp bound for the $a$-number of a cyclic cover of $\mathbb{P}^1$
abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. We give upper bounds for the $a$-number $a(X)$ when $X$ is hyperelliptic or, more generally, a tame cyclic cover of the projective line. For hyperelliptic curves, writing $g=pm+r$ with $0\le r<p$ and $n=(p-1)/2$, we prove the sharp bound $a(X)\le nm+\min\{n,r\}$. For tame cyclic covers, we refine previously known upper bounds and give curves attaining the resulting bound in infinitely many genera in characteristics $3$ and $5$. The proofs combine an alternating pairing on the bundle of locally exact differentials, originally due to Raynaud, with an explicit polynomial description of the Cartier operator. We also produce an explicit locus of hyperelliptic curves $X$ with $a(X)\ge a_g$, where $\frac{a_g}{g}$ converges to $\frac{p-1}{2p}$ as $g$ goes to $\infty$, whose dimension grows linearly with the genus $g$. These families exhibit excess intersections of the Torelli locus with loci of large $a$-number in the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties.

title: Asymptotic stability of self-similar blow-up for the two-dimensional Zakharov system
abstract: We prove asymptotic stability of the small-parameter Glangetas-Merle self-similar blow-up solutions of the two-dimensional Zakharov system under nonradial perturbations in the energy space. The proof establishes dissipation on the wave time scale by canceling the fast density coupling. We impose nonlinear orthogonality to the ground state of the density-dependent Schrödinger operator for modulation and use successive energy corrections after subtracting the instantaneous density response from the Schrödinger error. The resulting dissipation yields power-law decay of the rescaled errors in the Schrödinger gradient, weighted local mass, and wave energy norms.

title: Higher moments of twisted Kloosterman sums and the arithmetic of algebraic varieties
abstract: For an odd prime $p,$ consider the affine varieties $X_k: \sum\limits_{i=1}^{k}(x_i+x_i^{-1})=0$ over the finite field $\F_p.$ In this paper, a key feature of our work is arithmetic interpretation between the higher power moments of Kloosterman sums, modular forms and arithmetic geometry of the varieties $X_5$ and $X_6$ through their rational point counts. Our main results provide two distinct explicit formulas for the point count $\#X_5(\F_p).$ In the first formula, we express $\#X_5(\F_p)$ in terms of Fourier coefficients of modular forms and a certain weighted average of fourth power twisted Kloosterman moments, where the average is taken over multiplicative characters. We further establish an identity expressing this weighted average of fourth power moment of twisted Kloosterman sums in terms of fifth power quadratic twisted Kloosterman moment, together with Fourier coefficients of modular forms. Moreover, we derive an independent expression for the same average with different weight directly in terms of Fourier coefficients of modular forms. In the second identity for $\#X_5(\F_p)$, we express this purely in terms of Fourier coefficients of two modular forms. Moreover, we express $\#X_6(\F_p),$ in terms of Fourier coefficients of three modular forms. For these two expressions of $\#X_5(\F_p)$ and $\#X_6(\F_p),$ our approach is based on an identity that relates the point counts of $X_k$ to the $k$-th power moments of Kloosterman sum and its quadratic twist.

title: Data-Driven Discovery and Rigorous Certification of Periodic Solutions in Infinite-Dimensional Dynamical Systems
abstract:
In this work, we consider a standard regression technique for time series analysis which fits a low-dimensional proxy system to a higher (even infinite) dimensional target model. We then propose a novel diagnostic that exploits a-posteriori computer-assisted proofs, and try to certify the existence of a true periodic solution of the target, nearby. When successful, this certification procedure provides mathematically rigorous information about how well an invariant structure in the proxy approximates a corresponding invariant structure in the target model.
  To illustrate the utility of the procedure, we develop surrogates using time series data from the Mackey--Glass delay differential equation, and for the Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) partial differential equation, using periodic boundary conditions for forecasting and Neumann boundary conditions for certification. In both test cases we extract invariant dynamics from low-dimensional proxies and use this to validate the existence of corresponding structures in the targets.

title: A $Θ(n)$-Multiplicative Improvement of the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound for Linear and Quantum Codes
abstract: The Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound is a fundamental benchmark for the existence of error-correcting codes. For non-linear $q$-ary codes of code length $n$, its finite length form is known to admit a multiplicative improvement of order $Θ(n)$. In contrast, for $q$-ary linear codes of arbitrary rates, the best previously known general improvement was only of order $Θ(\sqrt n)$. This leaves open whether the algebraic constraint of linearity inherently prevents a linear-order refinement. We show that it does not. For every fixed prime power $q$ and relative distance $0<δ<1-1/q$, we obtain a $Θ(n)$-multiplicative improvement of the GV bound for $q$-ary linear codes of arbitrary rate, matching the corresponding result for nonlinear codes. Our proof is based on a simple change of viewpoint. Rather than requiring the initial random linear construction to contain no low-weight vectors, we allow $O(n)$ low-weight points, show that they are independent in the underlying projective space, and then eliminate all of them simultaneously at the cost of a single dimension. The key probabilistic ingredient is an exponential bound on nontrivial linear dependencies among low-weight vectors. We further show that this approach can be extended to quantum codes despite the symplectic self-orthogonality constraint. We obtain a $Θ(n)$-multiplicative improvement of the quantum GV bound for every fixed $0<δ<1-1/q^2$ satisfying $H_{q^2}(δ)<1/2$. Thus, the same $Θ(n)$ finite length improvement is applicable to both general linear structure and symplectic self-orthogonality.

title: Differential equations for twisted intertwining operators in abelian orbifold conformal field theory
abstract:
Let $ V $ be a vertex operator algebra with two commuting automorphisms $ g_1 $ and $ g_2 $ (possibly of infinite order and non-semisimple). We derive a Jacobi identity for a twisted intertwining operator $ \mathcal{Y} $ of type $ \left( \begin{smallmatrix} W_3\\ W_1 \, W_2 \end{smallmatrix}\right) $ when $ W_1 $ is a $ g_1 $-twisted $ V $-module, $ W_2 $ is a $ g_2 $-twisted $ V $-module, and $ W_3 $ is a $ g_1 g_2 $-twisted $ V $-module.
  For any abelian group $ G $ of automorphisms of a CFT-type vertex operator algebra, under certain Noetherian assumptions, we derive differential equations satisfied by the multi-series $ \langle w_0, \mathcal{Y}_1(w_1,z_1) \cdots \mathcal{Y}_N(w_N,z_N) w_{N+1} \rangle $ when $ \mathcal{Y}_j $ are intertwining operators among $ C_2 $-cofinite and discretely graded $ V $-modules twisted by elements in $ G $. For modules twisted by automorphisms with only real positive eigenvalues, it suffices to assume $ C_1 $-cofiniteness and discrete grading. When all but at most two external modules are twisted by automorphisms having only positive real eigenvalues, it suffices to assume all in-state and internal modules are $ C_1 $-cofinite and discretely graded.
  When $ G $ is a finite abelian group, we use the theory of regular singular points to prove that the multi-series $ \langle w_0, \mathcal{Y}_1(w_1,z_1) \cdots \mathcal{Y}_N(w_N,z_N) w_{N+1} \rangle $ converges absolutely to a multivalued analytic function when $ |z_1| > \cdots > |z_N| > 0 $ and analytically extends to the region $ z_i \neq 0 $, $ z_j - z_k \neq 0 $, for $ 1 \leq i \leq N $ and $ 1 \leq j < k \leq N $. The vertex operator algebra $ V $ is not assumed to be $ C_2 $-cofinite or simple.

title: Families of (Pluri)subharmonic Functions and Separate Subharmonicity
abstract: We study the singular sets of pointwise bounded-above envelopes of families of functions. For families of subharmonic functions on open subsets of $\mathbb C$, of plurisubharmonic functions on open subsets of $\mathbb C^N$, and, more generally, of functions subharmonic in each complex variable separately, we prove that the singular set of a pointwise bounded-above envelope is relatively closed and nowhere dense. In contrast, for $N\ge3$ we construct a sequence of subharmonic functions on $\mathbb R^N$ whose upper envelope is finite everywhere but nowhere locally bounded above. We also characterize the singular sets that arise for admissible classes of functions, both with and without a continuity assumption, and give applications to separately subharmonic functions.

title: To Race or Not to Race? Exploiting Performance Variability in Mixed-Integer Programming via Root-Gated Resource Allocation
abstract:
Mixed-integer programming (MIP) solver runtimes vary substantially across random seeds. Parallel replication exploits this variability but can waste computational resources when applied indiscriminately. We investigate whether information from an ordinary solve can guide this allocation decision.
  We formulate replication under a finite deadline, establish an exact relationship between runtime dispersion and the value of independent searches, and analyze delayed replication and imperfect allocation decisions. Using 101,615 seeded SCIP runs, we examine the association between root-LP dual degeneracy and replication value. We then introduce a non-invasive root-gated policy that preserves the original solver trajectory and launches three additional seeded processes when a root dual-degeneracy indicator reaches a fixed threshold.
  In a prospective two-hour experiment on 130 paired instances, root-gated racing proves optimality on 77 instances (59.23%), versus 73 (56.15%) for both Single and unconditional Race-4, while reducing active worker-process occupancy by 43.00% relative to unconditional racing. These findings demonstrate the promise of selective parallel resource allocation without solver-source modifications.

title: Renormalized volume, Generalized Loewner energy, and Grunsky determinant of multiply connected domains
abstract: We define and study three Möbius invariant functionals for multiply connected planar domains with finitely many boundary components: the Loewner energy, the renormalized volume, and the Grunsky determinant. Using quasiconformal variations, we prove that when the boundary curves are sufficiently regular, the three functionals differ only by a modulus-dependent constant. We also prove that the Loewner energy is finite if and only if every boundary curve is a Weil--Petersson quasicircle. Moreover, we prove that the three functionals all attain their unique extremal value at the circle domains. In particular, the Loewner energy is zero if and only if it is evaluated at a circle domain. Finally, we use the minimization of Loewner energy to give a new proof of the finitely connected version of Koebe uniformization theorem.

title: Discrete Approximation of differential two-stage stochastic linear complementarity problems
abstract: This paper studies differential two-stage stochastic linear complementarity problems, in which an ordinary differential equation (ODE) is coupled with a two-stage stochastic linear complementarity problem (SLCP) under a time-dependent probability distribution. The right-hand side of the ODE involves a solution pair (here-and-now and wait-and-see decisions) of the two-stage SLCP, while the two-stage SLCP involves two functions depending on the time $t$ and the state $x(t)$ of the ODE. Under appropriate conditions, we prove that the solution function of the two-stage SLCP is Lipschitz continuous in $x(t)$ and locally $\frac{1}{2}$-Hölder continuous in $t$, and establish the existence and uniqueness of a classical solution to the differential two-stage SLCP. Moreover, we develop a discrete approximation scheme for the differential two-stage SLCP. We first use a finite-scenario partition with mesh size $δ_N$ to approximate the distribution, then apply the Euler method for time discretization with step size $h$, and finally solve the resulting finite-dimensional problems using an inexact progressive hedging method with tolerance $η$. We prove that the error between a computed solution by the discrete approximation scheme and the classical solution of the original problem is bounded by $C(δ_N+h+η)$, where $C>0$ is a constant independent of $N$, $h$ and $η$. Finally, we apply our method to find an equilibrium point of a differential two-stage stochastic two-player zero-sum game. Numerical experiments illustrate the convergence rates and the efficiency of the discrete approximation scheme.

title: Almost sure asymptotics of numerical errors for SDEs with additive noise
abstract: In this paper, we characterize the sharp almost sure asymptotics for the numerical error of the Euler--Maruyama method applied to stochastic differential equations with additive noise. Specifically, we establish, to our knowledge, the first sharp laws of the iterated logarithm for Euler--Maruyama errors in this setting along geometric mesh refinements $(N_i)_{i\in\mathbb N^+}=(α^i)_{i\in\mathbb N^+}$ for any integer $α\geq 2$. These results identify $(N_i)^{-1}\sqrt{\log\log N_i}$ as the sharp almost sure error scale and provide an explicit expression for the path-dependent constants governing the asymptotic error envelopes. The LIL constants also admit a natural interpretation through the asymptotic error distribution, specifically through the conditional covariance matrix of the stable limit of the rescaled error given the driving Wiener process. A central challenge in establishing these results is to characterize the almost sure fluctuations of Skorohod integrals arising in the error expansion, which are generally anticipating, non-Gaussian, and dependent across refinement levels. The analysis also provides a framework for studying analogous asymptotics for other numerical methods.

title: Weighted STSAFT-Modulation Spaces and Approximation by Phase-Adapted Neural Networks
abstract: We develop a transform-adapted approximation framework for shallow neural networks based on the short-time special affine Fourier transform (STSAFT). Replacing the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) in the definition of classical modulation spaces, we work with weighted STSAFT-modulation spaces, building on the existing SAFT-associated modulation-space framework, and use their chirp correspondence with classical weighted modulation spaces through the chirp factorization of the SAFT kernel. We construct an associated neural dictionary and establish an $N$-term Sobolev approximation bound of order $N^{-1/2}$ on bounded one-dimensional domains. A global approximation theorem is also obtained when the spatial translation parameter ranges over the whole real line; a compact-support argument explains why an unrestricted global conclusion cannot in general be inferred from a bounded translation range. For a fixed-scale chirp family $f_κ(x)=e^{iπκx^2}u(x)$, we combine the global estimate with a phase analysis to obtain the stronger phase-dependent upper-bound factor $\langleλ\rangle^n\langleκ-λ\rangle^{n+3/2-1/r}.$ For each fixed nonzero Schwartz envelope, matching the dictionary phase reduces the growth of this specified upper bound from order $|κ|^{n+3/2-1/r}$ to order $|κ|^n$, while preserving the $N^{-1/2}$ rate. The associated mismatch scale is stated as a comparison of upper bounds, not as a threshold for the optimal approximation error. Four numerical experiments examine model comparison, error decay with dictionary size, phase mismatch, and the obstruction caused by restricted translations. We discuss the effective number of fitted output coefficients, including the rank loss of the sine branch at zero phase, and distinguish the numerical diagnostics from the theoretical best-approximation estimates.

title: Exterior-Row Replacement for Grid-Based Multinode Shepard Collocation on Implicit Planar Domains
abstract: Grid-based multinode Shepard collocation combines tensor-product Lagrange interpolants on overlapping Cartesian subgrids. On an implicitly defined domain, retained subgrids may cross the boundary and contain exterior source nodes. Removing or moving these nodes changes the local interpolants. We introduce exterior-row replacement (ERR) to preserve the source nodes and coefficients of every retained subgrid. We assemble PDE rows at strictly interior sources and supply the remaining equations through boundary evaluations. We consider two square completion methods based on projection and redistribution, an oversampled weighted least-squares one (ERR-OS), and a completion method that selects boundary rows through the interior PDE nullspace (ERR-QR). Full column rank is characterized by the boundary action on this nullspace. We also give completion conditions for prescribed fitted rows and an error estimate in terms of the residual. Global-full (GF) support uses all retained subgrids, whereas nearest-active (NA) support uses only those containing the active source nearest to the evaluation point. NA keeps off-source boundary rows sparse. The numerical study covers a disk, an annulus, a smooth star-shaped domain, a square hole with fitted and implicit boundary components, and a fitted L-shaped domain. With degree-$4$ local tensor polynomials, ERR-OS and ERR-QR recover the expected fifth-order accuracy in the reported refinement study. Further experiments examine the effects of boundary oversampling and trimming on algebraic admissibility and boundary observability.

title: Complete critical metrics for the quadratic scalar curvature functional: examples and rigidity
abstract: We study complete critical metrics for the quadratic scalar curvature functional \[ g\mapsto\int_M S_g^2\,\dv_g, \] with criticality understood under compactly supported variations, focusing on rigidity phenomena and nontrivial examples. In dimension three, we prove that every complete critical metric is scalar-flat, without any additional assumption. In dimension four, we construct complete non-Einstein critical metrics with bounded, nonconstant negative scalar curvature. In every dimension $n\geq5$, we show that either $S_g\equiv 0$ or $S_g<0$ everywhere, and a new argument proves scalar-flatness whenever $S_g \in L^p$ for some $0<p\leq P_n$, where $P_n>2$ is an explicit threshold. Moreover, we construct complete critical metrics with bounded, negative scalar curvature, decaying to zero at infinity. These examples establish the optimality of our rigidity threshold $P_n$ in dimension six and in every dimension $n\geq10$. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first complete critical metrics for this functional that are neither scalar-flat nor Einstein.

title: An $O(L^3)$ Spherical Harmonic Transform on $L^2$ Samples
abstract: For the representation of signals on the sphere band-limited at $L$ using the optimal number of samples, $L^2$, equal to the number of degrees of freedom in harmonic space and placed on $L$ iso-latitude rings, we develop a spherical harmonic transform (SHT) that is theoretically exact, requires no solution of linear systems and no precomputation beyond the placement of the rings, and has complexity $O(L^3)$. The transform rests on the observation that, for each order $m$, the samples on the rings that resolve order $m$ are a complete set of samples for the order-$m$ profile of the signal, so that its values on the remaining rings follow from a closed-form Lagrange basis, the sampling functions of order $m$. We prove that the proposed optimal-dimensionality SHT (OSHT) recovers every band-limited signal exactly in exact arithmetic, so that the $L^2$ samples admit a sampling theorem in the collocation sense. For the final harmonic analysis we give two exact back-ends: Gauss-Legendre quadrature of the interpolated profiles and the algorithm of the equiangular sampling theorem, which applies without change because the rings coincide with its grid. We identify the amplification constant that governs numerical error, show that it replaces the condition number used previously for the placement of rings, propose a placement that minimizes it, and give an error propagation model that explains the growth of error with the band-limit. A multi-pass refinement converges in two passes to the rounding floor of the samples. We also describe a stable log-domain evaluation of the sampling functions, a rescaled Legendre recurrence, and a forbidden-region skipping rule that halves the cost of the elimination. Numerical experiments up to $L=2048$ characterize the accuracy, measured by the maximum and mean coefficient errors and the signal-to-noise ratio, the stability and the computation time.

title: Hessian sectional curvatures of conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds
abstract: Conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds generalize Hessian manifolds. Shima introduced Hessian sectional curvature in 1995 as an invariant for studying Hessian structures. We extend this invariant to conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds and study related curvature conditions and invariants. Our main results are as follows. For connected Hessian manifolds of dimension at least two, we characterize constant Hessian sectional curvature (CHC) by pointwise orthogonal invariance. We call conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds satisfying this invariance condition weakly CHC. We classify connected weakly CHC statistical manifolds of dimension at least two whose cubic forms are parallel with respect to the Levi-Civita connection. This classification characterizes the non-Hessian statistical structures induced on the classical hyperbolic affine spheres $xyz=c>0$ in the positive octant. We also introduce principal Hessian curvatures and show that they form a complete invariant for left-invariant Hessian structures on $\mathbb{R}^n$ up to statistical isomorphism.

title: Invariant complex Finsler metrics on reductive complex homogeneous spaces
abstract: Let $(M=G/H,J)$ be a reductive complex homogeneous space and $F$ be a $G$-invariant strongly pseudoconvex complex Finsler metric on $M$. Using the adapted $(1,0)$-frame field obtained by parallel transformation with respect to the canonical connection on $M$, we obtain the necessary and sufficient condition for $F$ to be a Kähler-Finsler metric (resp. weakly Kähler-Finsler metric) in terms of Lie-bracket. The curvature tensor of the complex Rund connection associated to $F$ is then decomposed into an algebraic part and a derivative part, yielding explicit formulas for the holomorphic bisectional curvature and holomorphic sectional curvature of $F$, respectively. As an application, we give a Lie-theoretic proof of the rigidity theorem: every $G$-invariant strongly pseudoconvex complex Finsler metric on a complex symmetric manifold $M=G/H$ is necessarily a Kähler--Berwald metric.

title: Removability Criteria for Separately Harmonic and Subharmonic Functions
abstract: Cegrell and Sadullaev showed that a separately harmonic and subharmonic function is subharmonic outside the product of two closed nowhere dense sets. We obtain sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of the second set, under which the function is subharmonic on the whole domain. In particular, we prove that this holds whenever the second set is polar.

title: Sharp low-dimensional Constants in the second-order hydrogen Heisenberg uncertainty principle via Jacobi chains
abstract: We establish the sharp constants $\mathcal H_N$ of the second-order Hydrogen Heisenberg uncertainty principle for $N=2,3$. Starting from the first angular mode reduction, we rewrite the fourth-order radial quotient as two coupled radial Coulomb channels. Then we turn the compatibility constraint into an explicit Jacobi chain by expanding the $B$-channel in generalized Laguerre polynomials and passing to parity-tail variables. Its tail energies satisfy scalar Riccati recursions, equivalently continued fractions. Furthermore, we characterize $2\mathcal H_2$ and $2\mathcal H_3$ as the unique roots of two explicit scalar equations, and we show that free-tail and Dirichlet finite sections provide monotone lower and upper approximations converging to the sharp constants. This yields rigorous bounds and the values $$\mathcal H_2\approx0.84478056,\quad \mathcal H_3\approx1.82348779.$$ We also obtain uniqueness of the first-mode radial extremizer up to amplitude, rotation, and dilation.

title: Weighted summability criteria for stability and instability of discrete dynamics with general growth rates
abstract: Following the time rescaling introduced by Dragičević and Silva in their paper [Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst. Ser. S 18 (2025), 3917--3944], we establish several criteria for uniform $h$-stability and uniform $h$-instability of discrete evolution cocycles. In particular, these asymptotic properties are characterized by suitable weighted summability conditions under uniform $h$-boundedness and uniform $h$-decay assumptions, respectively. Explicit examples show that the respective assumptions cannot be omitted. Our results cover a wide range of discrete growth rates $h$, including exponential and polynomial ones. Furthermore, working in the general setting of discrete evolution cocycles, we provide a framework for discrete evolution families and discrete cocycles.

title: Infectious Disease Horizon in Emerging Infectious Diseases
abstract: Emerging infectious diseases often spread freely before an outbreak is detected, yet the duration of this free-transmission period and the infection size accumulated during this period are difficult to quantify. These quantities directly affect forecasts of subsequent transmission dynamics, estimates of infection size, and decisions regarding prevention and control measures. In this study, we propose and compute the infectious disease horizon (IDH)-the time span from when an infectious disease begins spreading to when it is first detected-and examine its antecedents and consequences. First, based on the SEAIR free-transmission model, we derive transmission characteristics, including the generation interval, the serial interval, the basic reproduction number, and the effective reproduction number, and describe the incidence using a renewal equation. Second, by considering two detection routes, we further obtain the distribution and mean of the IDH under different detection settings and quantify the infection size at the time of outbreak detection. Third, intervention measures are incorporated to derive a post-detection transmission model with generally distributed stage durations, followed by the derivation of the corresponding model under exponentially distributed stage durations and the determination of the final infection size. Finally, under the exponential-distribution assumption, the model is applied to the COVID-19 outbreak in Xi'an. The unified framework developed in this study provides a theoretical basis for evaluating early surveillance capacity for emerging infectious diseases, optimizing testing strategies, and determining the intensity of prevention and control measures after outbreak detection.

title: Matrix Waring Problem in finite fields with coefficients from $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$
abstract: Let $k$ be a fixed positive integer and $p$ be an odd prime such that $\gcd(p-1,k)=1$. For sufficiently large primes $p$, we show that the equation $AX^k+BY^k=C$ has solutions $X,Y \in \mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, where $A$ and $B$ are fixed matrices in $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, and $C$ is a fixed matrix in $\mathrm{M}(2,\mathbb{F}_p).$ Our proof relies on Fourier analysis over $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p).$

title: The Query Complexity of Unknown Sparse Gradient Residuals
abstract:
We study optimization of an average of \(n\) functions when gradient predictions are exact except for at most \(k\) unknown components. An initial scan may miss these exceptions.
  For a class of smooth problems, we prove that the optimal worst-case expected number of component-gradient evaluations needed to find an approximate stationary point is \[ Θ\!\left(\min\left\{nk+\mathcal R,\frac nk\mathcal R\right\}\right), \] where \(\mathcal R\) represents the optimal cost when the exceptional components are known. Prediction evaluations are free.
  This bound shows that discovering even a few exceptions can cost more than one full scan and can account for most of the gradient evaluations.

title: A Weighted Second-Order Nonlocal Total Variation Regularizer for Image Restoration
abstract: Despite the remarkable progress of deep learning in image processing, variational methods remain a fundamental and actively developing framework, offering interpretability, mathematical rigor, and well-founded guarantees. In this work, we introduce a weighted second-order nonlocal total variation regularizer for image restoration, which is based on measuring gradient differences across the image domain and allows for weights that are neither smooth nor symmetric and may vanish outside a search window. We first provide a rigorous definition of the regularizer and prove that it enjoys several desirable properties under realistic assumptions on the underlying weight function. We then consider a nonlocal variant of the variational image restoration model of Chambolle and Lions, and prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the associated minimization problem. On the computational side, we develop a discrete formulation of the model and derive the corresponding Chambolle-Pock primal-dual algorithm. Finally, we conduct an extensive experimental evaluation, comparing the proposed regularizer with a range of local and nonlocal, first- and second-order regularizers across several image restoration tasks. The results demonstrate its strong noise-suppression and texture-preservation capabilities, as well as its robustness to nonlocal weights computed under non-ideal conditions.

title: Optimal One Health control of antimicrobial resistance: a household mean-field model with community feedback and parameters from Burkina Faso
abstract: We study how to combine three One Health interventions against antimicrobial resistance: prescription-only dispensing of antibiotics to people, access to veterinary care for animals, and treatment of household sludge and manure. Each household is a Markov chain on the carriage states of its people, animals and soil, and households are linked through the community, whose prevalence feeds the acquisition rates. We prove that, as the number of households grows, the distribution of household states converges to the solution of a nonlinear mean-field equation. This system is monotone for the stochastic order, so that no intervention increases carriage anywhere, and for every constant intervention it has exactly one equilibrium, which attracts all solutions and is given by a scalar equation. For the optimal control problem we prove existence, necessary conditions, positivity of all controls under a quadratic cost, uniqueness for short horizons, and a turnpike property under an explicit dissipativity condition, which we verify for our parameters by a computer-assisted numerical certification. With parameters from Tenkodogo, Burkina Faso, the optimal combined strategy averts about 17% of human carriage over three years in the baseline scenario, and 11% to 28% over the plausible scenarios for the parameters that the survey cannot identify; these figures are projections conditional on the model. The strategy itself is robust: the value of perfect information on the unmeasured parameters is about 2% of the achievable benefit. A compartmental model with the same transmission rates but without households underestimates the benefit, and targeting the interventions by zone of the town increases it.

title: Minimising Disquotational Truth
abstract: We present a new axiomatic theory of disquotational truth based on the theory of positive disquotation PUTB. Formulated in classical logic, PUTB restricts the T-schema to positive sentences and satisfies key epistemic desiderata (semantic conservativity and trustworthiness). However, it fares poorly in proof-theoretic strength compared to reflective truth frameworks. To address this, we propose a new theory of positive disquotation aimed at axiomatizing its least fixed-point model. Without requiring additional resources, we achieve this by incorporating ill-founded reasoning under suitable soundness restrictions, applying the tools of cyclic proof theory to axiomatic theories of truth. The resulting theory, CPUTB, is sound relative to the minimal fixed-point model and proves the same arithmetical theorems as the impredicative theory ID1.

title: Recovering Small Perturbations of a Known Inclusion from One Mixed Steklov Eigenpair with Local Boundary Data
abstract: We study the recovery of small normal displacements of a known inclusion from a single mixed Steklov eigenpair. The data consist of the eigenvalue and the eigenfunction trace on any nonempty open subset of the fixed outer boundary, with the eigenfunction normalized using only that subset. For an inner Dirichlet condition, we prove that the linearized measurement map is injective at every simple eigenvalue. A compatible adjoint identity yields a reconstruction method with a conditional stability estimate on any fixed finite-dimensional space of smooth displacements. For the principal Dirichlet eigenpair, the same local data also determine the inclusion uniquely among sufficiently small normal graphs. In a three-dimensional concentric shell, the eigenvalue determines the mean displacement at first order, while spherical harmonics diagonalize the remaining full-boundary trace map. The singular values decay exponentially with harmonic degree, yielding logarithmic conditional stability under a Sobolev prior. Numerical experiments using the perturbed geometry illustrate the quadratic linearization error and the deterioration of conditioning as the observed patch shrinks. For an inner Neumann condition, we prove linearized injectivity at every positive simple eigenvalue.

title: A locally complete family of Kummer type hyperkähler fourfolds
abstract: We construct a 4-dimensional family of projective hyperkähler fourfolds of Kummer type. A general member of this family can be described as an irreducible component of a complete intersection of Heisenberg-invariant cubics in an 8-dimensional projective space. Several properties of the corresponding moduli space are also obtained. Our arguments rely on specializing to the case of generalized Kummer fourfolds of genus-two Jacobians, and make use of classical results dating back to Burkhardt and Coble.

title: The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies
abstract: The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies asks whether uniform ellipticity implies $H^s$-coercivity for symmetric nonlocal kernels of order $2s$, with $0<s<1$. We show that the conjecture fails whenever $n>2s$ for every $s \in (0,1)$ and $n \geq 1$, even for smooth compactly supported test functions; for $n=1$ and $s>1/2$, we show that it holds. The construction also gives bounded discontinuous weak solutions in $H^s_{\rm loc}$ to nonlocal equations in divergence form with kernels in this class. Despite the failure, we show that the conjecture holds for several important classes of kernels. We establish a general local coercivity criterion based on annular cancellation, which applies in particular to kernels satisfying both divergence- and nondivergence-form symmetry. The criterion also allows us to treat kernels comparable to stable kernels with bounded measurable coefficients, as well as non-cutoff Boltzmann kernels under a geometric nonconcentration assumption. As an application, we obtain a short and self-contained proof of the Gressman--Strain anisotropic coercivity estimate. Furthermore, by combining our new criterion with existing regularity results, we obtain Hölder estimates under ellipticity and cancellation assumptions.

title: Observability from Measurable Sets for Heat Equations with Bounded Space-Time Potentials
abstract: We establish final-state observability for heat equations with real-valued bounded space--time potentials on bounded $C^2$ domains, from arbitrary measurable space--time sets of positive measure. On $\mathbb R^n$, we prove observability from time-dependent sets whose spatial slices are uniformly thick on a set of times of positive measure. A counterexample for the free heat equation on $\mathbb R$ shows that integral thickness alone is insufficient for observability.

title: Classification and Geometry of Loxodromic Curves on Surfaces of Revolution in Three-Dimensional Euclidean Space
abstract:
This paper investigates the global geometry of loxodromes and loxodromic curves on surfaces of revolution in $\mathbb{R}^3$. A loxodrome is a regular curve avoiding the poles and making a constant directed angle with the meridians. To allow curves to reach or pass through poles, we introduce loxodromic curves, whose pole-free interior portions are loxodromes. The directed azimuths of these portions agree modulo $π$.
  We classify surfaces of revolution into four types based on the number of poles and whether the profile curve is closed: cylinder-like, torus-like, paraboloid-like, and sphere-like. For cylinder-like surfaces, every maximal loxodromic curve other than a parallel is non-self-intersecting. For torus-like surfaces, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves are closed or dense according to the rationality of their rotation numbers. For paraboloid-like and sphere-like surfaces, only maximal meridians can pass smoothly through poles, while nonmeridional, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves have poles as endpoints.
  We derive the differential equations for arc-length-parametrized loxodromes and introduce coordinates in which they are represented by straight lines. We solve the direct and inverse problems for loxodromic segments on all four surface types and give criteria for maximal loxodromic curves to be geodesics. We show that diffeomorphisms preserving maximal loxodromic curves preserve surface type and that their inverses preserve such curves. These maps preserve maximal meridians and parallels on surfaces with poles, but need not do so on pole-free surfaces. We characterize azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms and, for cylinder-like surfaces, establish criteria for conformality and isometry. In particular, azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms are conformal when both surfaces have poles.

title: Finite Bodies on Norton's Dome: Escape-Time Divergence and a Center-of-Mass Barrier Theorem
abstract: Norton's dome illustrates how a Newtonian initial-value problem can admit both rest and delayed departure from the same initial state. We examine how this nonuniqueness changes when the point particle is replaced by a rigid sphere of positive radius. For a generalized family of Norton's domes, we show that any fixed positive sphere radius prevents spontaneous departure from rest at the apex. We then extend the analysis to more general bodies and establish two sufficient conditions: a geometric constraint on the distance between the center of mass and the apex, and an interior tangent ball condition for rigid bodies whose center of mass is vertically aligned with the initial contact point. Both arguments combine geometric estimates with an energy inequality and Grönwall's inequality. The first condition also applies to passive deformable bodies without releasable internal energy. These results identify explicit conditions under which finite-body geometry excludes the spontaneous motion allowed by Norton's point-particle model.

title: Boundary Actuation of a Chain Fountain - Physically Admissible Tracking, Stochastic Limits and Zero-Gravity Circulation
abstract: This paper was inspired by a post on Twitter and by the eight months the author spent at the AASS Centre at Orebro University in 2007. This phenomenon is interesting not only to a physicist, but also to someone like me working in control theory, because of its potential relevance to stabilizing drones and similar flying machines subject to random velocity fluctuations while hovering. A chain fountain can settle without an engineered controller, yet its natural height is selected by transport and boundary forces. We ask how an ideal boundary traction force can sustain a prescribed height or motion. Within an established three-state model, we connect feedback design to force and energy balances and derive sufficient conditions for nominal tracking that preserve the model's mechanical constraints. We also bound the deviations caused by bounded pickup uncertainty. The resulting framework explains how feedback can shape a naturally regulated process and identifies physical limits on the motions it can sustain: stabilizing a mathematical trajectory is useful only if the corresponding motion remains mechanically admissible. This is a preliminary step towards stabilization of the chain in three dimensions.

title: Key Relay and Secure Network Coding: One-Shot Equivalence and Separation on Undirected Networks
abstract: Motivated by quantum key distribution networks, we compare key relay protocols with secure network coding on the same undirected graph. In this comparison, we fix the finite field, terminal set, and wiretap family. Each edge supplies one independent uniform symbol to its endpoints for key relay, or carries one symbol once for network coding. The network code may choose its source terminal, edge orientations, and causal transmission order before execution. In this setting, the standard one-time-pad simulation readily converts every secure network code to key relay. We investigate the reverse conversion to linear network coding. For two terminals and a one-symbol key, arbitrary key relay is equivalent to scalar linear acyclic network coding over the prescribed field. The proof uses connectivity and flow conservation, related to the binary $st$-flow protocol. However, this equivalence fails in general when several terminals seek one common key. A doubled triangle separates key relay from acyclic coding but admits causal coding on a cyclic orientation. On the four-terminal complete graph, a linear key relay protocol over the ternary field withstands the three perfect-matching wiretap sets, whereas no linear causal network code distributes a source symbol of the same size, even with private randomness at every vertex and its use in decoding. We also establish a linear key relay normal form that removes interaction and private randomness and bounds public communication. All results concern one-shot feasibility with exact agreement and perfect secrecy.

title: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
abstract:
We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture.
  The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity.
  We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar.
  In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.

title: Certified Hierarchical Planning and Tracking: A Learning-Based Approach
abstract: In this paper, we develop a hierarchical control framework for nonlinear dynamical systems with safety constraints. Specifically, a low-fidelity model is introduced for trajectory planning, while a tracking controller is designed for the high-fidelity system. We first characterize the tracking error bound (TEB) using a storage function. Then, we formulate the synthesis of the tracking controller, the storage function, and the TEB as an optimization problem. Following that, we develop an offline learning approach to approximately solve the optimization problem, by incorporating behavior cloning and satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) solver. We further integrate the learned controller and the TEB into online tracking of the high-fidelity system. This framework enables the control of high-dimensional nonlinear systems with safety guarantees, while maintaining computational efficiency for real-time implementation. Finally, experiments are provided for illustration.

title: A binomial-adjusted $θ$-trapezoidal tau-leaping method for chemical kinetic systems
abstract: In Hu, Li and Min (2011), the authors propose a weak second order accurate $θ$-trapezoidal method as an improvement to the classical tau-leaping method. However, for complex chemical kinetic systems their model's underlying analytical assumptions can fail to hold in practice, leading to a significant reduction in its computational effectiveness. Here we introduce a modification to the method which allows it to regain desirable convergence characteristics, both given the original and a relaxed version of the underlying assumptions. We confirm this improvement through a local error analysis and present numerical examples showing it consistently performs either better or comparable to the $θ$-trapezoidal method.

title: Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
abstract: We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.

title: Rainbow matchings in non-uniform hypergraph systems
abstract: Let $s\geq 1$, $r_1, r_2,\dots, r_{s+1}$ be given positive integers and $r=\max\{r_1, r_2,\ldots, r_{s+1}\}$. We prove that if $\mathcal{F} = \{\mathcal{F}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{F}_{s+1}\}$ is a family of hypergraphs on a ground set of $n$ vertices, $n\geq 4r^2(s+1)$, such that $\mathcal{F}_i\subseteq \binom{n}{r_i}$ and $|\mathcal{F}_i|>\binom{n}{r_i}-\binom{n-s}{r_i}-\binom{n-s-r}{r_i-1}+1$, for all $i \in [s+1]$, then $\mathcal{F}$ admits a rainbow matching of size $s+1$ or there exists $W \in \binom{[n]}{s}$ such that $W$ is a vertex cover of $\mathcal{F}_i$, for all $i \in [s+1]$. This improves upon the previously known range $n>2r^3s$ to $n>4r^2(s+1)$. Moreover, for a given family $\mathcal{F} = \{\mathcal{F}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{F}_{s+1}\}$ of hypergraphs $\mathcal{F}_i\subseteq \binom{n}{r_i}$, we give a best possible Ore-degree condition for $\mathcal{F}_{i}$'s that guarantees the existence of a rainbow matching of size $s+1$ for $\mathcal{F}$.

title: Asymptotic Dimension of Persistence Modules of Bounded Presentation
abstract: We compute the asymptotic dimension of spaces of multiparameter persistence modules of bounded presentation under the interleaving distance. The $d$-parameter modules with at most $n$ generators and $m$ relations have asymptotic dimension, and Assouad-Nagata dimension, exactly $d(n+m)$, the number of coordinates of their generator and relation grades, over every field; for two parameters this is $2(n+m)$. The space has continuous moduli, already for two parameters and $n,m\ge2$: over an infinite field it contains, at every scale, infinite uniformly separated families of pairwise non-isomorphic modules with one fibered barcode, so it is not doubling even at a fixed fibered barcode; already for $m\ge1$ it is not coarsely equivalent to a proper metric space. The proof is an induction on the number of distinct grade coordinates: an interleaving small compared with the gaps between these coordinates moves each of them by at most twice its size and preserves the induced grid representation, so the continuous moduli are invisible at large scale. Each class of modules at finite distance therefore embeds coarsely into Hilbert space; for $n,m\ge2$ over an uncountable field, the classes that contain these families admit no such embedding into a separable Hilbert space. Under the two-parameter matching distance $2(n+m)$ is a lower bound, attained for one generator and for two generators with at most one relation; on a finite net of $S$ slices the asymptotic dimension is at most $2nS$.

title: On real-analytic non-degeneracy of left-symmetric algebras in dimension 3
abstract: In this paper, we show that any three-dimensional differentially non-degenerate left-symmetric algebra over $\mathbb R$ is non-degenerate both in the formal and real-analytic categories via the correspondence with Nijenhuis operators.

title: On the packing-dimension analogue of Bourgain's constant
abstract: For every $n\geq 2$, we construct a domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose harmonic measure has packing dimension $n$. That is, the packing analogue of Bourgain's constant is zero, in contrast with Bourgain's constant, which is positive. Moreover, the elliptic measure of the same domain also has packing dimension $n$ for every uniformly elliptic matrix.

title: GFF for 3D Ising interfaces in three moves of Tetris
abstract: We show that at sufficiently large inverse-temperature $β>0$, the 3D Ising model on the torus, under boundary conditions that have a positive slope $θ_1,θ_2>0$, has a GFF scaling limit for its interface. The proof goes through three steps of a Tetris map, which lets cubes drop according to gravity in each of the three axes, yielding Solid-On-Solid (SOS), Half-Monotone SOS (HMSOS) and monotone surfaces (dimers). We establish GFF limits sequentially, in particular resolving the analogous problem for the $(2+1)$D SOS. A crucial ingredient is an improved RG analysis for interacting dimers, which is of independent interest: it relaxes the assumptions on interactions from being uniformly bounded in $L^\infty$ to only being typically small.

title: Optimal strong convergence rates of explicit stabilized method for the Galerkin finite element discretization SPDEs driven by multiplicative noise
abstract: Explicit stabilized methods provide an efficient approach to stiff systems arising from deterministic parabolic equations, yet rigorous convergence theory for their application to stochastic partial differential equations remains scarce. To the best of our knowledge, the only prior fully discrete strong convergence analysis of explicit stabilized integrators for SPDEs is due to [A. Abdulle et al. IMA J. Numer. Anal. 43(1)(2023), pp. 258--292] and it is restricted to additive noise. The present work addresses the extension to multiplicative noise, by coupling Galerkin finite element spatial discretization with explicit stabilized time integrators. Under global Lipschitz assumptions and appropriate spatial regularity conditions, we derive the strong error bound $\mathcal{O}(h^{1+r}+τ^{1/2})$ with $r\in[0,1)$, which achieves the optimal temporal strong convergence rate $1/2$ for the considered family of methods. One- and two-dimensional numerical tests with multiplicative noise validate the predicted convergence rates and compare the computational performance of explicit stabilized methods against the linearly implicit Euler method.

title: Strong Approximation of Stochastic Burgers Equations with Space-Time White Noise
abstract: In this paper, we establish algebraic strong convergence rates for spectral Galerkin and fully discrete approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive space--time white noise. For deterministic initial data in $H^1$, the spectral approximation is shown to be convergent in the spatial supremum norm, uniformly in time and in every finite probability moment, with order arbitrarily close to $1/2$. Furthermore, we prove that an accelerated fully tamed exponential method possesses spatial and temporal strong convergence orders arbitrarily close to $1/2$ and $1/4$ under a CFL condition. The key to our analysis is a polynomial stability estimate for the conservative Burgers flux, which allows us to control the nonlinear error using polynomial moment bounds for the exact and numerical solutions. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first algebraic strong convergence rates on the whole probability space for this equation with additive space--time white noise.

title: On the minimum energy required to trigger a spike
abstract: We formulate and numerically study the problem of finding the minimum energy required to trigger a spike in a three-dimensional conductance-based excitable model. The variational formulation seeks a state trajectory that reaches the boundary of the spiking region with the least \textit{peak} cumulative work supplied through the membrane port. We approximate voltage histories by sums of real exponentials, reducing the problem to a finite-dimensional optimization. The best-found voltage waveform consists of a hyperpolarization phase followed by a depolarization phase, which seems to match the experimentally determined optimal stimulus in squid giant axons.

title: Complex singularities and obstructions to pseudo-Einstein structures: An expository note
